ex.zh: 斯克鲁奇的外甥又痛痛快快笑了一场；这股风气实在挡不住，虽然那胖姑娘拼命拿香醋来抵挡；大家也就一齐跟着笑了。

ex.t: Unanimously voted.
ex.zh: 全体一致通过。

senses.d: impossible to answer

ex.t: He’s getting great bumps over his eyes, and learning to ask the most unanswerable questions.”
ex.zh: 他眼睛上头都鼓起来了，还学着问些最答不上的问题。”

ex.t: But in effect it was unanswerable even now, since the few scattered survivors from the ancient world were incapable of comparing one age with another.
ex.zh: 可实际上它现在就已经无法回答，因为旧世界少数零散的幸存者没有能力把一个时代跟另一个时代相比较。

ex.t: It is to be achieved either by gradually acquiring more and more territory and so building up an overwhelming preponderance of power, or by the discovery of some new and unanswerable weapon.
ex.zh: 这要靠逐渐夺取越来越多的领土、从而积聚起压倒性的力量优势来实现，或者靠发现某种新的、无法对付的武器。

senses.d: not returned in kind

ex.t: O'Brien left this unanswered.
ex.zh: 奥布莱恩没有回答。

senses.d: not readily apparent
x: the answer was at first unapparent

ex.t: Consider the subtleness of the sea; how its most dreaded creatures glide under water, unapparent for the most part, and treacherously hidden beneath the loveliest tints of azure.
ex.zh: 想一想海的狡黠吧：它那些最可怖的生物在水下滑行，大半时候看不见，阴险地藏在那最可爱的蔚蓝色调底下。

senses.d: not to be placated or appeased or moved by entreaty

ex.t: Oh, his unappeasable brow drives on towards one, whose duty tells him he cannot depart.
ex.zh: 啊，他那不可平息的额头，直逼着一个人，而那人的职责叫他不能离开。

ex.t: Because of its thinness the mouth and eyes looked disproportionately large, and the eyes seemed filled with a murderous, unappeasable hatred of somebody or something.
ex.zh: 因为太瘦，嘴和眼睛显得不成比例地大；那眼睛里像是充满对某人或某物的杀气腾腾、无法平息的仇恨。

senses.d: discouraging intimacies; reserved
inaccessibly located or situated
x: an unapproachable chalet high in the mountains

ex.t: When the tea bell rang, Jo appeared, looking so grim and unapproachable that it took all Amy’s courage to say meekly...
ex.zh: 茶铃响时，乔出来了，脸色那么阴沉、那么叫人不敢靠近；艾米鼓起全部勇气，才低声说……

ex.t: “As you both locked your doors at night, your rooms were unapproachable from that side.
ex.zh: “既然你们夜里都锁门，那么从那一面是进不了你们屋子的。”

ex.t: Joe was sourer than ever, and Sol-leks was unapproachable, blind side or other side.
ex.zh: 乔比以往更酸，索尔莱克斯谁也近不得，瞎眼那边不行，另一边也不行。

senses.d: (used of persons or the military) not having or using arms
(used of plants or animals) lacking barbs or stings or thorns

ex.t: I seen him grapple four and knock their heads together--him unarmed.”
ex.zh: 我见过他空着手一个人对付四个，把他们的脑袋往一块儿撞。”

ex.t: At the same time, observing Gray to be unarmed, I handed him my cutlass.
ex.zh: 同时我看格雷没有武器，就把我的短剑递给他。

ex.t: If you’ll come up one by one, unarmed, I’ll engage to clap you all in irons and take you home to a fair trial in England.
ex.zh: 你们要是一个一个空着手过来，我担保给你们全戴上镣铐，带回英国去公平受审。

senses.d: used of persons or their behavior; feeling no shame

ex.t: They alighted on the floor, quite unashamed of themselves, and the youngest one had already forgotten his home.
ex.zh: 他们落在地板上，一点也不惭愧；最小的那个已经忘了自己的家。

ex.t: A subdued impassioned murmur was audible in the room beyond, and Miss Baker leaned forward unashamed, trying to hear.
ex.zh: 隔壁房间里传来一阵压低了的、激昂的低语，贝克小姐毫不遮掩地向前倾身，想听个清楚。

senses.d: immune to attack; incapable of being tampered with
x: fortifications that made the frontier inviolable

senses.d: impossible to assail
without flaws or loopholes

ex.t: How at such an apparently unassailable surface, they contrive to gouge out such symmetrical mouthfuls, remains a part of the universal problem of all things.
ex.zh: 他们怎样在这样一个看似攻不进去的表面上凿出这样匀称的一口口肉来，仍是万事万物那个普遍难题的一部分。

senses.d: not arrogant or presuming
x: unassuming to a fault, skeptical about the value of his work

ex.t: “This unassuming style promotes study, that’s why we adopt it,” returned Laurie, who certainly could not be accused of vanity, having voluntarily sacrificed a handsome curly crop to the demand for quarter-inch-long stubble.
ex.zh: “这种不招摇的样式宜于读书，我们才留它，”劳里答道；他倒真不能算爱虚荣，因为他是自愿把一头好看的鬈发牺牲掉，换成四分长的短茬的。

ex.t: Father Mapple rose, and in a mild voice of unassuming authority ordered the scattered people to condense.
ex.zh: 梅普尔神父站起身来，用一种温和却自有威权的口气，吩咐散坐的人们靠拢些。

ex.t: “He is perfectly well-behaved, polite, and unassuming,” said her uncle.
ex.zh: “他举止得体，彬彬有礼，毫不拿架子，”舅舅说。

senses.d: not watched
x: she dashed out leaving the bar unattended

senses.d: lacking accompaniment or a guard or escort
lacking a caretaker

ex.t: But this critical act is not always unattended with the saddest and most fatal casualties.
ex.zh: 可这一危急的举动并不总是没有最悲惨、最致命的伤亡相伴。

ex.t: The precipitating manner in which Captain Ahab had quitted the Samuel Enderby of London, had not been unattended with some small violence to his own person.
ex.zh: 亚哈船长离开伦敦的“塞缪尔·恩德比号”时那样急急忙忙的架势，对他自己的人身也不是没有带来一点小小的损伤。

ex.t: After having been recognized, he could not go and sit at a table with an unattended girl.
ex.zh: 被人认出来之后，他就不能跑去跟一个没人陪的姑娘坐一桌。

senses.d: producing no result or effect

ex.t: But even that refuge proved unavailing, for he was delivered over to the enemy, with a "Be gentle with him, John," which struck the culprit with dismay, for when Mamma deserted him, then the judgment day was at hand.
It held up its chain at arm's length, as if that were the cause of all its unavailing grief, and flung it heavily upon the ground again.
ex.zh: 它伸直手臂举起链子，仿佛这就是它那一切无济于事的悲痛的缘由，然后重重地把它摔回地上。

ex.t: But even that refuge proved unavailing, for he was delivered over to the enemy, with a “Be gentle with him, John,” which struck the culprit with dismay, for when Mamma deserted him, then the judgment day was at hand.
ex.zh: 可连这个避难所也不中用：他被交到敌人手里，还伴着一声“约翰，别太凶”；这话叫那小犯人慌了，因为妈妈一丢下他，审判的日子就到了。

senses.d: for which vengeance has not been taken

ex.t: Otherwise, the governor would escape, and the people’s blood (suddenly of some value, after many years of worthlessness) be unavenged.
ex.zh: 否则，那总管就会逃走，人民的血（多少年一文不值之后，忽然有了点价值）就得不到报偿。

ex.t: Not all unavenged did they die, for with Lean Wolf fell Alf Mason, to disturb the Spanish Main no more, and among others who bit the dust were Geo.
ex.zh: 他们死得并非全无报复，因为瘦狼倒下时，阿尔夫·梅森也倒了，再不能搅扰西班牙海了；另外还啃了土的，有乔治·

ex.t: Young Openshaw shall not long remain unavenged.
ex.zh: 年轻的奥彭肖不会久久无人为他报仇。

senses.d: impossible to avoid or evade

ex.t: There was no reproach either in their faces or in their hearts, only the knowledge that they must die in order that he might remain alive, and that this was part of the unavoidable order of things.
That is unavoidable.
ex.zh: 这躲不掉。

ex.t: 'This is unavoidable,' his voice seemed to say; 'this is what we have got to do, unflinchingly.
ex.zh: “这是躲不掉的，”他的声音似乎在说，“这是我们非做不可的，毫不畏缩地做。

senses.d: by necessity
x: the situation slid inescapably toward disaster

ex.t: He’s unavoidably detained.
ex.zh: 他给什么事绊住了，脱不开身。

senses.d: (often followed by `of') not aware
x: unaware of the danger they were in

ex.t: Feeling stronger than ever to meet and subdue her Apollyon, she pinned the note inside her frock, as a shield and a reminder, lest she be taken unaware, and proceeded to open her other letter, quite ready for either good or bad news.
ex.zh: 她觉得比从前更有力气去迎战、制伏她的亚玻伦，就把字条别在衣裳里，当作盾牌和提醒，免得一时不备；然后拆开另一封信，不管好坏都准备好了。

ex.t: And, as usual, the ruling groups of all three powers are simultaneously aware and unaware of what they are doing.
ex.zh: 而且照例，三个强国的统治集团同时既明白自己在做什么，又不明白。

ex.t: Unaware of the tragedy being enacted above, Peter had continued, for a little time after the children left, to play gaily on his pipes: no doubt rather a forlorn attempt to prove to himself that he did not care.
ex.zh: 彼得不知道上面正演着那场惨剧，孩子们走后他又快活地吹了一阵笛子：这无疑是想向自己证明他不在乎，只是这证明有点凄凉。

senses.d: without forethought or plan; inadvertently
suddenly and unexpectedly- A.Lincoln
x: sorrow comes to all, and to the young it comes with bittered agony because it takes them unawares

senses.d: at a disadvantage

ex.t: I know just what I should say, for I’ve planned it all, so I needn’t be taken unawares.
ex.zh: 我该说什么，我清楚得很，全都想好了，不会叫他打个措手不及。

ex.t: Fourth: Stealing unawares upon the whale in the fancied security of the middle of solitary seas, you find him unbent from the vast corpulence of his dignity, and kitten-like, he plays on the ocean as if it were a hearth.
ex.zh: 第四：你以为在孤寂大海的中央万无一失，悄悄逼近这鲸，却发现他从那庞大肥胖的尊严里松弛下来，像只小猫，在洋面上嬉戏，仿佛那是一座壁炉前的地面。

senses.d: not awed

ex.t: “Espying the mate drawing near as he was toiling at the pump with the rest, the Lakeman affected not to notice him, but unawed, went on with his gay banterings.
ex.zh: “那湖区人正跟大家一道在泵上苦干，瞥见大副走近，便装作没看见他，却毫无惧色地继续他那快活的打趣。

senses.d: remove a bar from (a door)

ex.t: “She wants me to unbar the window,” thought Peter, “but I won’t, not I!”
ex.zh: “她要我开窗，”彼得想，“可我不开，我才不呢！”

senses.d: not firmly fastened or secured
x: went through the unlatched gate into the street

ex.t: Casement windows opened, crazy doors were unbarred, and people came forth shivering--chilled, as yet, by the new sweet air.
ex.zh: 窗扉打开，破旧的门拔了闩，人们出来时打着寒噤——还叫那新鲜的甜空气冻着。

ex.t: It was Tink, and quickly he unbarred to her.
ex.zh: 是叮叮铃；他赶快给她开了闩。

ex.t: Then he unbarred the window.
ex.zh: 然后他拉开了窗闩。

senses.d: incapable of being tolerated or endured

ex.t: (There was a time in my imprisonment, when my desire for vengeance was unbearable.)
ex.zh: （我坐牢的时候，有一段日子，我报仇的欲望强烈得叫人受不了。）

ex.t: And them and their descendants, to the last of their race, I, Alexandre Manette, unhappy prisoner, do this last night of the year 1767, in my unbearable agony, denounce to the times when all these things shall be answered for.
ex.zh: 我，亚历山大·马内特，一个不幸的囚徒，在一七六七年这最后一夜，在无法忍受的痛苦里，把他们和他们的后代，直到他们一族的最末一个，控告到这一切都要清偿的那些日子。

ex.t: But though slightly drunk he was also suffering under some grief that was genuine and unbearable.
ex.zh: 可他虽然微醉，也在受着某种真实而难以忍受的悲痛。

senses.d: to an unbearable degree
x: it was unbearably hot in the room

ex.t: Moreover his varicose ulcer had begun itching unbearably.
The Parsons children played it at all hours of the night and day, unbearably, on a comb and a piece of toilet paper.
ex.zh: 帕森斯家的孩子日夜不分地用一把梳子和一张手纸吹它，叫人受不了。

ex.t: By the third day his eyes ached unbearably and his spectacles needed wiping every few minutes.
ex.zh: 到第三天，他的眼睛疼得受不了，眼镜每隔几分钟就得擦。

senses.d: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society

ex.t: Nothing unbecoming tinged the pride; it was a natural and worthy one; but he observed it as a curiosity.
ex.zh: 这自豪里没有一丝不体面的东西；它是自然的、可敬的；可他把它当作一件稀奇事来观察。

ex.t: Now Florence’s mama hadn’t a particle of taste, and Amy suffered deeply at having to wear a red instead of a blue bonnet, unbecoming gowns, and fussy aprons that did not fit.
ex.zh: 弗洛伦斯的妈妈一点品味也没有，艾米得戴红的而不是蓝的帽子，穿不合身的袍子，系花哨又不合身的围裙，心里苦得很。

ex.t: “There is something a little stately in him, to be sure,” replied her aunt; “but it is confined to his air, and is not unbecoming.
ex.zh: “他身上是有点端着的味道，”舅母答道，“可那只是在外表上，并不难看。

senses.d: a rejection of belief

ex.t: Was not Saul of Tarsus converted from unbelief by a similar fright?
ex.zh: 大数的扫罗不也是被一场类似的惊吓从不信中转变过来的么？

ex.t: Tom glanced around to see if we mirrored his unbelief.
ex.zh: 汤姆四下看看，看我们是否映出他的不信。

senses.d: not easy to believe
in an unbelievable manner

ex.t: He led a ghostlike existence between the tiny, dark shop, and an even tinier back kitchen where he prepared his meals and which contained, among other things, an unbelievably ancient gramophone with an enormous horn.
ex.zh: 他在那间又小又暗的铺子和一间更小的后厨之间过着幽灵般的日子，他在后厨做饭，那儿除别的之外，还摆着一台带巨大喇叭的、老得叫人难以相信的留声机。

senses.d: rejecting any belief in gods
holding that only material phenomena can be known and knowledge of spiritual matters or ultimate causes is impossible
denying or questioning the tenets of especially a religion
x: a skeptical approach to the nature of miracles

ex.t: The word ‘Mother’ suggested other maternal counsels given long ago, and received with unbelieving protests.
ex.zh: “母亲”这两个字又叫她想起从前母亲给过的别的劝告，当时她都不信地顶回去了。

senses.d: in an incredulous manner
x: the woman looked up at her incredulously

ex.t: “Why, Anne, how you’ve grown!” she said, almost unbelievingly.
ex.zh: “哎呀，安妮，你长了这么多！”她几乎不信地说。

senses.d: straighten up or out; make straight
unfasten, as a sail, from a spar or a stay
free from flexure
make less taut
x: relax the tension on the rope

senses.d: become less tense, rest, or take one's ease
x: He relaxed in the hot tub
Let's all relax after a hard day's work

senses.d: release from mental strain, tension, or formality
x: unbend the mind from absorbing too much information

ex.t: “Then here’s to Johnny Plank!” he cried brazenly, hating the boys more than ever because they had seen him unbend.
ex.zh: “那就敬约翰尼跳板一杯！”他厚着脸皮喊，比从前更恨那些孩子，因为他们看见他软下来过。

senses.d: incapable of adapting or changing to meet circumstances

ex.t: This man, whose name was Beaufort, was of a proud and unbending disposition and could not bear to live in poverty and oblivion in the same country where he had formerly been distinguished for his rank and magnificence.

senses.d: not bent
x: trees with straight unbent trunks make the best lumber

senses.d: erect in posture

ex.t: On this occasion, Miss Pross, responding to Ladybird’s pleasant face and pleasant efforts to please her, unbent exceedingly; so the dinner was very pleasant, too.
ex.zh: 这一回，普罗斯小姐见小鸟儿一脸愉快，又那样费力讨好她，就大大松了下来；于是这顿饭也吃得很愉快。

ex.t: The shaggy eyebrows unbent a little as he rolled the steps toward the shelf where the Johnsonian literature was placed.
ex.zh: 他把梯凳推向放约翰逊那套书的那格书架，那浓乱的眉毛松开了一点。

ex.t: Fourth: Stealing unawares upon the whale in the fancied security of the middle of solitary seas, you find him unbent from the vast corpulence of his dignity, and kitten-like, he plays on the ocean as if it were a hearth.
ex.zh: 第四：你以为在孤寂大海的中央万无一失，悄悄逼近这鲸，却发现他从那庞大肥胖的尊严里松弛下来，像只小猫，在洋面上嬉戏，仿佛那是一座壁炉前的地面。

senses.d: free from physical or moral spots or stains

ex.t: If he had been wavering before, as to what he should do, which had often seemed likely, the advice and entreaty of so near a relation might settle every doubt, and determine him at once to be as happy as dignity unblemished could make him.
ex.zh: 他要是本来还在犹豫该怎么办——这常常像是很可能的——那么一位这样近的亲戚的劝告和恳求，也许就能打消一切疑虑，叫他立刻下定主意，去享他那种不损尊严的幸福。

senses.d: showing no emotion
x: the convicted killer listened unblinkingly to the reading of his sentence

ex.t: That unblinkingly vivid Japanese sun seems the blazing focus of the glassy ocean’s immeasurable burning-glass.
ex.zh: 那轮一眨也不眨、鲜明得刺目的日本太阳，仿佛是那镜面似的海洋这面无边的取火镜的炽烈焦点。

senses.d: having no body
not having a material body

ex.t: Oh, Ahab! what shall be grand in thee, it must needs be plucked at from the skies, and dived for in the deep, and featured in the unbodied air!
ex.zh: 哦，亚哈！你身上凡有伟大的地方，都非得从天上去摘，往深海里潜取，在无形无体的空中描摹出面目来不可！

senses.d: not yet brought into existence

ex.t: “I have looked at her, speculating thousands of times upon the unborn child from whom I had been rent.
ex.zh: “我看过她，千百次地揣度那个我被迫分离的未生的孩子。

ex.t: For the future, for the unborn.
ex.zh: 为将来，为那些还没出生的人。

senses.d: seemingly boundless in amount, number, degree, or especially extent

ex.t: The Lion's gratitude was unbounded; he looked upon the man as his friend, and they shared the cave for some time together.
But I was in reality very ill, and surely nothing but the unbounded and unremitting attentions of my friend could have restored me to life.
ex.zh: 可我实际上病得很重，若不是我朋友那无边的、不间断的照料，绝没有别的什么能把我救活。

ex.t: Upon this occasion my father said, with an expression of unbounded wonder, “My dearest Victor, what infatuation is this?
ex.zh: 这一回，父亲带着无限惊异的神情说：“我最亲爱的维克多，这是什么糊涂念头？

senses.d: undo the braids of

ex.t: A series of staccato taps on the west window brought Anne flying in from the yard, eyes shining, cheeks faintly flushed with pink, unbraided hair streaming behind her in a torrent of brightness.
ex.zh: 西窗上断断续续敲了几下，安妮就从院子里飞跑进来，眼睛发亮，脸颊微微泛红，没编辫子的头发在身后像一道亮流。

senses.d: impossible to break especially under ordinary usage

ex.t: He was a patentee of the Openshaw unbreakable tire, and his business met with such success that he was able to sell it and to retire upon a handsome competence.
ex.zh: 他是奥彭肖不破车胎的专利持有人，生意做得极成功，后来把厂子卖了，带着一笔可观的财产退了休。

ex.t: It was heartbreaking, only Buck’s heart was unbreakable.
ex.zh: 这叫人看着心碎，只是巴克的心碎不了。

senses.d: not restrained or controlled

ex.t: He opened his eyes, and into them came the unbridled anger of a kidnapped king.
My own spirits were high, and I bounded along with feelings of unbridled joy and hilarity.
ex.zh: 我自己的精神也高，我一路蹦跳，怀着无羁的欢喜与欢闹。

senses.d: marked by continuous or uninterrupted extension in space or time or sequence
x: the unbroken quiet of the afternoon

senses.d: not subdued or trained for service or use
(of farmland) not plowed
(especially of promises or contracts) not violated or disregarded
not broken; whole and intact; in one piece
x: fortunately the other lens is unbroken

ex.t: Scrooge expressed himself much obliged, but could not help thinking that a night of unbroken rest would have been more conducive to that end.
ex.zh: 斯克鲁奇表示十分感激，却忍不住想：睡一整夜安稳觉，对达到这个目的恐怕更有帮助。

ex.t: The Spirit dropped beneath it, so that the extinguisher covered its whole form; but though Scrooge pressed it down with all his force, he could not hide the light: which streamed from under it, in an unbroken flood upon the ground.
ex.zh: 幽灵在罩子底下缩了下去，熄灯罩把它整个身形都盖住了；可斯克鲁奇尽管使出全身力气往下按，也遮不住那光：光从罩子底下涌出来，连绵不断地淌到地上。

ex.t: On the right hand, scrub firs, their spirits quite unbroken by long years of tussle with the gulf winds, grew thickly.
ex.zh: 右手边密密地生着矮小的冷杉，它们跟海湾的风搏斗了这么多年，脾气一点没被磨平。

senses.d: undo the buckle of

ex.t: I never saw a man unbuckle harness so quickly as he did, and with a pat and a good word he led me to a long stable, with six or eight stalls in it, and two or three horses.

ex.zh: 接着又是一鞭；其实我们一直不声不响、老老实实地拼命往前赶，尽管常给折腾得够呛，心里憋闷。

ex.t: Dear, bequeath me that great patience Which has power to sustain A cheerful, uncomplaining spirit In its prison-house of pain.
ex.zh: 亲爱的，把那份大耐性遗给我——它能在痛苦的牢里撑住一颗欢欢喜喜、不抱怨的心。

senses.d: not yet finished
not caught or not caught within bounds

ex.t: But I now leave my cetological System standing thus unfinished, even as the great Cathedral of Cologne was left, with the crane still standing upon the top of the uncompleted tower.
ex.zh: 可我现在就把我这一套鲸学分类法这样搁着，任它半截未完，正如科隆那座大教堂当初被搁下时一样，起重机至今还立在那座没完工的塔顶上。

senses.d: lacking understanding
x: tried to explain to her uncomprehending husband

ex.t: Ampleforth marched clumsily out between the guards, his face vaguely perturbed, but uncomprehending.
ex.zh: 安普尔福斯笨拙地在看守之间走出去，脸上有些不安，却不明白是怎么回事。

senses.d: not making concessions
x: took an uncompromising stance in the peace talks

ex.t: A fell, uncompromising, murderous business-meaning there.
ex.zh: 那里只有一种凶残的、毫不通融的、要人性命的办事神气。

ex.t: “It may seem to point very straight to one thing, but if you shift your own point of view a little, you may find it pointing in an equally uncompromising manner to something entirely different.
ex.zh: “它看上去可能直指一件事，可你只要把自己的视角稍稍移一移，就会发现它同样毫不含糊地指向完全不同的另一件事。

senses.d: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
a feeling of lack of concern

ex.t: But it was all in vain, for they were just out of reach: so he gave up trying, and walked away with an air of dignity and unconcern, remarking, "I thought those Grapes were ripe, but I see now they are quite sour."
Josie walked the Barry fence with an airy unconcern which seemed to imply that a little thing like that wasn’t worth a “dare.”
ex.zh: 乔西走完巴里家那道栅栏，一副满不在乎的神气，仿佛这点小事根本不配叫“激”。

ex.t: Mr. Bennet raised his eyes from his book as she entered, and fixed them on her face with a calm unconcern, which was not in the least altered by her communication.
ex.zh: 她进来时，班纳特先生把眼睛从书上抬起，沉着淡然地把目光定在她脸上；听了她的话，那神色也毫没改动。

senses.d: lacking in interest or care or feeling
x: the average American...is unconcerned that his or her plight is the result of a complex of personal and economic and governmental actions...beyond the normal citizen's comprehension and control
blithely unconcerned about his friend's plight

senses.d: easy in mind; not worried
x: the prisoner seems entirely unconcerned as to the outcome of the examination

senses.d: not occupied or engaged with

ex.t: “Ay, there she comes,” continued Mrs. Bennet, “looking as unconcerned as may be, and caring no more for us than if we were at York, provided she can have her own way.
ex.zh: “唉，她来了，”班纳特太太接着说，“一副满不在乎的样子，只要我们由着她，她就把我们看作远在约克一般。

ex.t: I know you will do him such ample justice, that I am growing every moment more unconcerned and indifferent.
ex.zh: 我知道你会替他主持这么大的公道，所以我也一刻比一刻更无所谓、更不动心了。

ex.t: I tried to put on as unconcerned an air as possible, but I had not forgotten the warnings of the lady, even though I disregarded them, and I kept a keen eye upon my two companions.
ex.zh: 我尽量装出若无其事的样子，可我没有忘记那位女士的警告，尽管我没有听她的，我仍警惕地留意着两个同伴。

senses.d: in an unconcerned manner
x: war was breaking out in Europe, but she unconcernedly planned for a holiday

ex.t: “Why, go to school next year and try again,” said Marilla unconcernedly.
ex.zh: “那就明年再上学，再考一回，”玛丽拉不在意地说。

senses.d: not conditional
not modified or restricted by reservations
not contingent; not determined or influenced by someone or something else

ex.t: A flank movement produced an unconditional surrender, however, for Laurie knew where to have him.
ex.zh: 可一次侧翼包抄就叫他无条件投降了；劳里知道该从哪儿下手。

ex.t: I own thy speechless, placeless power; but to the last gasp of my earthquake life will dispute its unconditional, unintegral mastery in me.
ex.zh: 我认你这无声、无处的力量；可直到我这地震般生命的最后一口气，我也要争辩它在我身上那种无条件、不完备的主宰。

ex.t: Hurriedly turning, with averted face, he descended into his cabin, leaving the strange captain transfixed at this unconditional and utter rejection of his so earnest suit.
ex.zh: 他急急转身，把脸避开，下舱去了；丢下那陌生船长，被这对他的恳求如此彻底、如此无条件的拒绝钉在那儿。

senses.d: not suitable to your tastes or needs
x: the uncongenial roommates were always fighting
the task was uncongenial to one sensitive to rebuffs

senses.d: very unfavorable to life or growth
used of plant stock or scions; incapable of being grafted

ex.t: “I don’t care,” and Jo shut the door, feeling that food was an uncongenial topic just then.
ex.zh: “随便。”乔关上门，觉得那会儿吃食是个不投机的题目。

senses.d: not joined or linked together
not connected by birth or family
lacking orderly continuity
x: a confused dream about the end of the world

ex.t: People not immediately connected with Monseigneur or the State, yet equally unconnected with anything that was real, or with lives passed in travelling by any straight road to any true earthly end, were no less abundant.
ex.zh: 那些跟爵爷或国家没有直接关系，却同样跟任何实在的东西没有关系、跟任何沿着直路走向真实尘世目标的生活没有关系的人，也不见少。

ex.t: As well as the prisoner could see, he and Mr. Lorry were the only men there, unconnected with the Tribunal, who wore their usual clothes, and had not assumed the coarse garb of the Carmagnole.
ex.zh: 就囚犯所能看见的，他和洛里先生是那儿仅有的与法庭无关、却穿着平常衣服、没有换上卡马尼奥拉那种粗陋服装的人。

ex.t: It was better to make it deal with something totally unconnected with its original subject.
ex.zh: 最好让它讲些与原来题目毫不相干的东西。

senses.d: not capable of being conquered or vanquished or overcome- R.E.Danielson
x: a tribute to his courage...and his unconquerable will

senses.d: incapable of being surmounted or excelled

ex.t: Each of the three powers which now divide the world is in fact unconquerable, and could only become conquerable through slow demographic changes which a government with wide powers can easily avert.
But unfortunately Demi’s most unconquerable prejudice was against going to bed, and that night he decided to go on a rampage.
ex.zh: 可不巧，德米最难克服的偏见就是不肯上床；那一晚他偏决定大闹一场。

ex.t: His father was a High Chief, a King; his uncle a High Priest; and on the maternal side he boasted aunts who were the wives of unconquerable warriors.
ex.zh: 他父亲是一位大酋长，一个国王；他叔父是一位大祭司；母系那边，他还有几位可夸耀的姑姨，都是些战无不胜的武士的妻子。

senses.d: not conquered

ex.t: Still Silver was unconquered.
ex.zh: 西尔弗却还没被降住。

senses.d: not conscious; lacking awareness and the capacity for sensory perception as if asleep or dead
without conscious volition
(followed by `of') not knowing or perceiving- Charles Dickens
x: happily unconscious of the new calamity at home

senses.d: that part of the mind wherein psychic activity takes place of which the person is unaware

ex.t: Uncle Scrooge had imperceptibly become so gay and light of heart, that he would have pledged the unconscious company in return, and thanked them in an inaudible speech, if the Ghost had given him time.
An overpowering smell of sweat, a sort of unconscious testimony to the strenuousness of his life, followed him about wherever he went, and even remained behind him after he had gone.
“And what do you suppose, you conceited female,” said Mr. Cruncher, with unconscious inconsistency, “that the worth of your prayers may be?
ex.zh: “你倒猜猜，你这个自负的女人，”克朗彻先生不知不觉自相矛盾地说，“你那祷告能值多少？

senses.d: without awareness
x: she jumped up unconsciously when he entered the room

ex.t: Unconsciously he defines for me the lines of a fresh school, a school that is to have in it all the passion of the romantic spirit, all the perfection of the spirit that is Greek.
The quarter was so long, that he was more than once convinced he must have sunk into a doze unconsciously, and missed the clock.
ex.zh: 这一刻钟长得厉害，他不止一次断定自己准是不知不觉打了个盹，把钟点错过了。

ex.t: "It isn't that," said Scrooge, heated by the remark, and speaking unconsciously like his former, not his latter, self.
ex.zh: “不是这个意思，”斯克鲁奇说，被这话激得动了气，不知不觉用旧日的自己、而不是后来的自己在说话。

senses.d: a state lacking normal awareness of the self or environment

ex.t: There was something awful in his unconsciousness of the figure that could have put out its hand and touched him as he stooped over his labour.
ex.zh: 有一个人影本可以伸出手来碰他，而他俯身做活，竟全然不觉，这里面有种可怕的东西。

ex.t: Was there ever such unconsciousness?
ex.zh: 可曾有过这样不觉得自己了不起的人？

ex.t: That was the ultimate subtlety: consciously to induce unconsciousness, and then, once again, to become unconscious of the act of hypnosis you had just performed.
ex.zh: 这才是最终的微妙之处：有意识地造成无意识，然后又一次对自己刚才施行的催眠行为本身变得无意识。

senses.d: free from constraint
x: he was unconstrained by any of the sanctions of polite society

ex.t: Its dark brown curls were long and free; free as its genial face, its sparkling eye, its open hand, its cheery voice, its unconstrained demeanour, and its joyful air.
ex.zh: 它深褐色的鬈发又长又散；散得像它那张和气的脸、那双闪亮的眼、那只张开的手、那个欢快的嗓子、那副无拘无束的举止、那身喜气洋洋的神态。

senses.d: not consumed

ex.t: The wind increased to a howl; the waves dashed their bucklers together; the whole squall roared, forked, and crackled around us like a white fire upon the prairie, in which, unconsumed, we were burning; immortal in these jaws of death!
ex.zh: 风增强成了嚎叫；浪把它们的圆盾互相撞击；整个飑风在我们四周咆哮、分叉、噼啪作响，像草原上一场白色的火，而我们就在其中燃烧着，却未被烧掉；在这死亡的巨口里，我们是不死的！

senses.d: difficult to solve or alleviate
incapable of being controlled
x: the little boy's parents think he is spirited, but his teacher finds him unruly

senses.d: incapable of being controlled or managed
impossible to repress or control

ex.t: The uncontrollable and hopeless mass of decomposition so engendered, would have polluted the air, even if poverty and deprivation had not loaded it with their intangible impurities; the two bad sources combined made it almost insupportable.
“Felix had accidentally been present at the trial; his horror and indignation were uncontrollable when he heard the decision of the court.
ex.zh: “费利克斯偶然在场听审；听到法庭的判决，他的恐惧和愤慨无法抑制。

ex.t: He paused, looking on me with wonder, and again turning towards the lifeless form of his creator, he seemed to forget my presence, and every feature and gesture seemed instigated by the wildest rage of some uncontrollable passion.
ex.zh: 他停下来，惊奇地看着我；随后又转向他造物主那没有生气的身体，像是忘了我在场，每一道纹、每一个姿势都像被某种管不住的激情的狂怒催着。

senses.d: in an uncontrolled manner

ex.t: Yet, still, words like those I have recorded would burst uncontrollably from me.
ex.zh: 然而，像我所记下的那些话，仍会不由自主地从我嘴里迸出来。

ex.t: At every few moments the fury of the crowd boiled over and the voice of the speaker was drowned by a wild beast-like roaring that rose uncontrollably from thousands of throats.
ex.zh: 每隔一会儿人群的愤怒就沸出来，演说者的声音被几千条喉咙里无法控制地涌起的、野兽般的吼叫淹没。

ex.t: His large pouchy cheeks were quivering uncontrollably.
ex.zh: 他那两个大腮袋不受控制地抖着。

senses.d: not being under control; out of control
x: the greatest uncontrolled health problem is AIDS

ex.t: Vain, ignorant, idle, and absolutely uncontrolled!
ex.zh: 虚荣、无知、懒惰，又全然无人管束！

senses.d: lacking conviction

ex.t: “I don’t know--exactly,” said Jane unconvinced.
ex.zh: “我不知——道，”简说，并不服气。

senses.d: not convincing
x: as unconvincing as a forced smile

senses.d: having a probability too low to inspire belief

ex.t: They were simply an imitation of his earlier manner, and curiously lifeless and unconvincing.
ex.zh: 那只是模仿他早年的手法，而且古怪地没有生气，不能令人信服。

senses.d: in an unconvincing manner

ex.t: "I can't complain," answered Wilson unconvincingly.
ex.zh: “还过得去。”威尔逊答道，语气却不足以服人。

senses.d: release
draw the cork from (bottles)

ex.t: There was no label this time with the words "DRINK ME," but nevertheless she uncorked it and put it to her lips.
There was no label this time with the words “DRINK ME,” but nevertheless she uncorked it and put it to her lips.
ex.zh: 这一次瓶子上没有写“喝我”的标签，可她还是拔开瓶塞，把瓶子凑到嘴边。

ex.t: Marilla took it, uncorked it, smelled it.
ex.zh: 玛丽拉接过去，拔开塞子，闻了闻。

senses.d: release
draw the cork from (bottles)

ex.t: Tirelessly the woman marched to and fro, corking and uncorking herself, singing and falling silent, and pegging out more diapers, and more and yet more.
ex.zh: 那女人不知疲倦地来回走，一会儿闭嘴一会儿张嘴，一会儿唱一会儿停，晾出一块又一块尿布，越来越多。

senses.d: (of language) not having its purity or excellence debased- Van Wyck Brooks
x: learn to speak pure English undefiled

senses.d: not decayed or decomposed
not debased
x: though his associates were dishonest, he remained uncorrupted

ex.t: Each of these stoppages was made at a doleful grating, by which any languishing good airs that were left uncorrupted, seemed to escape, and all spoilt and sickly vapours seemed to crawl in.

senses.d: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
x: he had coarse manners but a first-rate mind
behavior that branded him as common

ex.t: He would become dreadful, hideous, and uncouth.
He was an uncouth man, but deeply imbued in the secrets of his science.
ex.zh: 他是个粗鲁无文的人，却深深浸透了他那门学问的奥秘。

ex.t: Sometimes I wished to express my sensations in my own mode, but the uncouth and inarticulate sounds which broke from me frightened me into silence again.
ex.zh: 有时我想用我自己的方式表达我的感觉，可从我这里出来的那些粗野而不成声的声音把我吓得又不出声了。

senses.d: inelegance by virtue of being an uncouth boor

ex.t: And besides all this, there was a certain lofty bearing about the Pagan, which even his uncouthness could not altogether maim.
ex.zh: 除此之外，这异教徒身上还有一种高卓的气度，连他的粗野也没能把它整个毁掉。

senses.d: remove all or part of one's clothes to show one's body
x: The man exposed himself in the subway

senses.d: reveal to view as by removing a cover
x: The curtain rose to disclose a stunning set

senses.d: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
x: The auction house would not disclose the price at which the van Gogh had sold
The actress won't reveal how old she is

ex.t: Uncover your face.
ex.zh: “把手放下来。”

senses.d: remove all or part of one's clothes to show one's body
x: The man exposed himself in the subway

senses.d: reveal to view as by removing a cover
x: The curtain rose to disclose a stunning set

senses.d: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
x: The auction house would not disclose the price at which the van Gogh had sold
The actress won't reveal how old she is

senses.d: not covered with clothing

ex.t: I uncovered it, and a gentle breeze quickly fanned it into a flame.
ex.zh: 我把盖的揭开，一阵轻风很快把它扇成了火焰。

ex.t: “That looks too pretty to eat,” he said, smiling with pleasure, as Jo uncovered the dish, and showed the blanc mange, surrounded by a garland of green leaves, and the scarlet flowers of Amy’s pet geranium.
ex.zh: “这好看得都舍不得吃了。”他高兴地笑着说；乔揭开碟子，露出那盘牛奶冻，四周围着绿叶和艾米心爱的天竺葵的红花。

ex.t: Winston uncovered his face.
ex.zh: 温斯顿把手放下。

senses.d: the removal of covering
the act of discovering something

ex.t: Down at street level another poster, torn at one corner, flapped fitfully in the wind, alternately covering and uncovering the single word INGSOC.
ex.zh: 街面高度还有一张招贴画，一角撕破了，在风里一阵阵地翻动，时遮时露那一个词：英社。

ex.t: Then, without uncovering it again, he dropped the photograph into the memory hole, along with some other waste papers.
ex.zh: 然后，他没有再揭开它，把照片连同一些别的废纸一起丢进了记忆洞。

ex.t: The picture had fallen to the floor uncovering the telescreen behind it.
ex.zh: 那幅画掉到地板上，露出后面的电幕。

senses.d: unpleasantly and excessively suave or ingratiating in manner or speech

ex.t: Dropping his spade, he thrust both hands in, and drew out handfuls of something that looked like ripe Windsor soap, or rich mottled old cheese; very unctuous and savory withal.
ex.zh: 他丢下铲子，把两只手伸进去，掏出一把把东西，看上去像熟透的温莎皂，又像油润斑驳的陈年干酪；摸起来腻滑，气味也浓。

ex.t: A sweet and unctuous duty!
ex.zh: 一桩甜美而油润的差事！

ex.t: In a word, after being tried out, the crisp, shrivelled blubber, now called scraps or fritters, still contains considerable of its unctuous properties.
ex.zh: 一句话，鲸脂熬过之后，那焦脆皱缩、如今叫作“渣”或“油饼”的东西，仍然含有相当多的油性。

senses.d: smug self-serving earnestness

ex.t: Granting other whales to be in sight, the fishermen will seldom give chase to one of these Grand Turks; for these Grand Turks are too lavish of their strength, and hence their unctuousness is small.
ex.zh: 即便望见别的鲸，渔人也很少去追这样一位“大土耳其人”；因为这些大土耳其人太不吝惜力气，所以身上的油水也少。

ex.t: Plum-pudding is the term bestowed upon certain fragmentary parts of the whale’s flesh, here and there adhering to the blanket of blubber, and often participating to a considerable degree in its unctuousness.
ex.zh: “葡萄干布丁”这名称，是给鲸肉上某些零碎部分的，那些东西东一点西一点粘在脂肪的被毯上，往往也带着相当程度的油润。

senses.d: not seasoned

ex.t: Will you understand, Winston, that no one whom we bring to this place ever leaves our hands uncured?
ex.zh: “温斯顿，你明白吗：凡被我们带到这儿来的人，没有一个未经治好就离开我们的手。”

senses.d: not provided with curtains
x: blank, curtainless windows stared back at her

ex.t: He recoiled in terror, for the scene had changed, and now he almost touched a bed: a bare, uncurtained bed: on which, beneath a ragged sheet, there lay a something covered up, which, though it was dumb, announced itself in awful language.
ex.zh: 他吓得往后一缩，因为景物已经变了，这会儿他几乎碰到了一张床：一张光秃秃、没挂帐子的床；床上一条破床单底下盖着个什么东西，那东西虽然一声不响，却用可怕的语言表明了自己的身份。

ex.t: And from the three long uncurtained windows the beautiful stretch of meadow and moorland, the far violet of the hills, and the unchanging changefulness of cloud and sky.
ex.zh: 三扇没挂窗帘的长窗外，是好看的一大片草场和荒原，远远的紫山，还有云和天那样千变万化又始终如一。

senses.d: not trimmed
(used of grass or vegetation) not cut down with a hand implement or machine
not shaped by cutting or trimming
(of pages of a book) having adjacent leaves still joined at the fore edge
x: a book with its leaves still uncut

senses.d: not cut
not cut- Tobias Smollett
x: glad to get out of the house with my throat uncut

ex.t: (The Psychologist, to show that he was not unhinged, helped himself to a cigar and tried to light it uncut.)
ex.zh: （心理学家为了表明自己并没有神经错乱，自己拿了一支雪茄，没剪头就试着去点。）

senses.d: not bearing a date

ex.t: The note was undated, and without either signature or address.
ex.zh: 这张字条没有日期，也没有署名和地址。

senses.d: unshaken in purpose
x: wholly undismayed by the commercial failure of the three movies he had made

senses.d: resolutely courageous
x: undaunted in the face of death

ex.t: The yards were hard up; and once more the Pequod thrust her undaunted bows into the opposing wind, for the supposed fair one had only been juggling her.
ex.zh: 帆桁紧紧转向上风；裴廓德号又一次把她无所畏惧的船头插进逆风里，因为那以为是顺的风，不过是在耍她。

senses.d: unshaken in purpose
x: wholly undismayed by the commercial failure of the three movies he had made

senses.d: resolutely courageous
x: undaunted in the face of death

ex.t: But Anne continued to face Mrs. Rachel undauntedly, head up, eyes blazing, hands clenched, passionate indignation exhaling from her like an atmosphere.
ex.zh: 可安妮仍然毫不畏缩地面对雷切尔太太，昂着头，眼睛冒火，两手紧握，一腔愤怒的义愤像气息一样从她周身散发出来。

senses.d: free from deception or illusion

ex.t: On the contrary, every particular relative to his sister was meant to be kept as much as possible to myself; and if I endeavour to undeceive people as to the rest of his conduct, who will believe me?
ex.zh: 恰恰相反，凡有关他妹妹的细节，本意都是尽量只让我一个人知道；我要是想纠正别人对他其余行为的看法，谁会信我呢？

senses.d: not brought to a conclusion; subject to further thought
x: our position on this bill is still undecided

senses.d: characterized by indecision
x: some who had been on the fence came out in favor of the plan
too many voters still declare they are undecided

ex.t: And he added in an undertone to the Queen, “Really, my dear, you must cross-examine the next witness.
ex.zh: 他又低声对王后补了一句：“说真的，亲爱的，下一个证人你得亲自盘问。

ex.t:
“Unimportant, of course, I meant,” the King hastily said, and went on to himself in an undertone,

“important—unimportant—unimportant—important—” as if he were trying which word sounded best.
ex.zh:
“当然，我的意思是‘不重要’，”国王急忙说，又低声自言自语：

“重要——不重要——不重要——重要——”像是在试哪个词听起来最好。

senses.d: enter upon an activity or enterprise
accept as a challenge
promise to do or accomplish
enter into a contractual arrangement
accept as a charge

ex.t: I undertook to pay him a fee if he cured me, and he, on his part, promised to charge nothing if he failed.
“Jacques,” returned Defarge, drawing himself up, “if madame my wife undertook to keep the register in her memory alone, she would not lose a word of it--not a syllable of it.
ex.zh: “雅克，”德法热挺直身子答道，“要是我妻子太太答应把这名册只记在她脑子里，她一个字也不会丢——一个音节也不会丢。

ex.t: The boy was proud of his charge, and undertook it in all seriousness.
ex.zh: 男孩为这份差事得意，认认真真担了起来。

senses.d: assign too low a value to
x: Don't underestimate the value of this heirloom-you may sell it at a good price

senses.d: esteem lightly
lose in value

ex.t: Highly as the dog-driver had forevalued Buck, with his two devils, he found, while the day was yet young, that he had undervalued.
ex.zh: 赶狗人原就把巴克估得很高，说他有俩魔鬼；可这天还没过完，他就发现自己还估低了。

senses.d: beneath the surface of the water
growing or remaining under water
x: viewing subaqueous fauna from a glass-bottomed boat

ex.t: A coral reef is a large underwater structure made of dead and living corals.
He had the impression of swimming up into this room from some quite different world, a sort of underwater world far beneath it.
ex.zh: 他觉得自己是从一个完全不同的世界游上来的，那世界在下面很深的地方，像是水底。

senses.d: undergarment worn next to the skin and under the outer garments

ex.t: I was standing beside his bed and he was sitting up between the sheets, clad in his underwear, with a great portfolio in his hands.
ex.zh: 我站在他床边，他坐在被单里，穿着内衣，手里捧着一大本作品集。

senses.d: pass through
x: The chemical undergoes a sudden change

ex.t: He corroborated everything, remembered everything, enjoyed everything, and underwent the strangest agitation.
ex.zh: 他样样都印证，样样都记得，样样都受用，心里翻腾得厉害，前所未有。

ex.t: The inexorable finger underwent no change.
ex.zh: 那毫不容情的手指一点没变。

ex.t: We know, now what you underwent when you suspected my descent, and when you knew it.
ex.zh: 我们现在知道了，你疑心我的出身时、知道它时，受了什么。

senses.d: the brush (small trees and bushes and ferns etc.) growing beneath taller trees in a wood or forest

ex.t: Accordingly I hid myself in some thick underwood, determining to devote the ensuing hours to reflection on my situation.
ex.zh: 于是我就躲在密密的矮树丛里，决定用接下来的几个钟头思索我的处境。

senses.d: the criminal class
(religion) the world of the dead-Theognis
x: No one goes to Hades with all his immense wealth

ex.t: You have imagined, probably, a huge underworld of conspirators, meeting secretly in cellars, scribbling messages on walls, recognizing one another by codewords or by special movements of the hand.
ex.zh: 你们大概想象过一个庞大的地下阴谋世界，在地窖里秘密集会，在墙上涂写消息，靠暗语或者特别的手势彼此相认。

ex.t: What so natural, then, as to assume that it was in this artificial Underworld that such work as was necessary to the comfort of the daylight race was done?
ex.zh: 那么，设想白昼种族舒适所必需的那些活儿，都是在这人造的地下世界完成的，岂不最自然？

ex.t: I proceeded, as I have said, to question Weena about this Underworld, but here again I was disappointed.
ex.zh: 正如我说过的，我接着就向薇娜打听这个地下世界，可在这里我又失望了。

senses.d: not deserved or earned
x: has an undeserved reputation as a coward

ex.t: Woe to the man who played tricks with that Army, or got undeserved promotion in it!
ex.zh: 谁要是在那支军队里耍花招，或是得了不该得的升迁，就有祸了！

ex.t: “How unfortunate that you should have used such very strong expressions in speaking of Wickham to Mr. Darcy, for now they do appear wholly undeserved.”
ex.zh: “不幸的是，你当初在达西先生面前把威克姆说得那样过火，如今看来，那些话全然不配。”

ex.t: The milkman, the literary innkeeper, Sir Harry, the roadman, and the idiotic Marmie, were all pieces of undeserved good fortune.
ex.zh: 送奶工、爱文学的小店主、哈里爵士、筑路工，还有那个白痴马米，都是我不配得的好运。

senses.d: in an unmerited manner
x: the team chalked up another victory, the last one quite undeservedly, in my opinion

ex.t: The only poor comfort he had was that she snubbed Charlie Sloane, unmercifully, continually, and undeservedly.
ex.zh: 他唯一的、可怜的安慰，就是她毫不留情、接二连三、无缘无故地冷落查理·斯隆。

senses.d: not deserving

ex.t: “No, Miss Manette; all through it, I have known myself to be quite undeserving.
ex.zh: “不会，马内特小姐；从头到尾，我都知道自己完全不配。

ex.t: Well, he is a very undeserving young man--and I do not suppose there is the least chance in the world of her ever getting him now.
ex.zh: 唉，他是个极不配的青年——我看她现在要得到他，世上一点指望也没有了。

ex.t: “Wickham is not so undeserving, then, as we have thought him,” said her sister.
ex.zh: “那么威克姆倒不像我们想的那样不配了，”姐姐说。

senses.d: not wanted
not worthy of being chosen (especially as a spouse)
one whose presence is undesirable
x: rounding up vagrants and drunks and other undesirables

ex.t: So long as defeat meant the loss of independence, or some other result generally held to be undesirable, the precautions against defeat had to be serious.
ex.zh: 只要失败意味着丧失独立，或者意味着其他一般认为不可取的结果，防败的措施就必须认真。

ex.t: This was done partly by the invention of new words, but chiefly by eliminating undesirable words and by stripping such words as remained of unorthodox meanings, and so far as possible of all secondary meanings whatever.
ex.zh: 做到这一点，部分靠发明新词，但主要靠淘汰不合需要的词，并剥去留存下来的词中那些不正统的意义，以及尽可能剥去一切次要意义。

ex.t: As we have already seen in the case of the word FREE, words which had once borne a heretical meaning were sometimes retained for the sake of convenience, but only with the undesirable meanings purged out of them.
ex.zh: 正如我们在 FREE 一词上已经看到的，曾经带有异端意义的词有时为了便利而被保留，但只是在其不合需要的意义被清除之后。

senses.d: not perceived or discerned
x: they feared some undetected trace of poison
she looked around to be sure her faux pas was undetected

ex.t: What is yonder undetected villain’s marble mansion with a door-plate for a waif; what is that but a Fast-Fish?
ex.zh: 那边那个未被识破的恶棍的大理石宅第，门上钉一块铜牌作标记旗，那除了是有主鲸还能是什么？

ex.t: Or they would disappear, alter themselves out of recognition, learn to speak with proletarian accents, get jobs in a factory and live out their lives undetected in a back-street.
ex.zh: 或者他们消失，改头换面到认不出来，学会用无产者的口音说话，在工厂里找到活干，在一条后街里不被发觉地过完一辈子。

ex.t: This was because he had no great opinion of the simple country deities, but thought that the thief would not pass undetected by the shrewder gods of the town.
ex.zh: 这是因为他不大看得起乡下那些老实的神，以为贼总逃不过城里那些更精明的神的眼睛。

senses.d: not developed, mature, or fully formulated
x: courses in interior design were rare and undeveloped

senses.d: not developed, improved, exploited or used
x: taxes on undeveloped lots are low

ex.t: It is a German conceit, that the vertebræ are absolutely undeveloped skulls.
ex.zh: 椎骨绝对就是未发育的头骨——这是德国人的一个构想。

ex.t: So, therefore, that mortal man who hath more of joy than sorrow in him, that mortal man cannot be true—not true, or undeveloped.
ex.zh: 所以，那个心里欢乐多于忧伤的凡人，不可能真实——不真实，或者尚未长成。

senses.d: going directly ahead from one point to another without veering or turning aside
x: some people see evolution as an undeviating upward march from simple organisms to the very complex
a straight and narrow tree-lined road unswerving across the lowlands

senses.d: used of values and principles; not subject to change; steady

ex.t: The Sperm Whale blows as a clock ticks, with the same undeviating and reliable uniformity.
ex.zh: 抹香鲸喷水就像钟摆滴答，有着同样不偏不倚、可靠的均匀。

ex.t: Besides, if you regard him very closely, and time him with your watch, you will find that when unmolested, there is an undeviating rhyme between the periods of his jets and the ordinary periods of respiration.
ex.zh: 再说，你若非常仔细地观察他，用表给他计时，就会发现：不受打扰时，他喷射的间隔跟他平常呼吸的间隔之间，有一种毫不偏差的韵律。

senses.d: cancel, annul, or reverse an action or its effect
x: I wish I could undo my actions

senses.d: deprive of certain characteristics
cause the ruin or downfall of
x: A single mistake undid the President and he had to resign

senses.d: cause to become loose
remove the outer cover or wrapping of

ex.t: All tried and all failed: and then he undid the bundle, and handed them the sticks one by one, when they had no difficulty at all in breaking them.
Winston undid the bit of string that held his overalls together.
Some one came and loosened the throat strap of my bridle, and undid the traces which kept the collar so tight upon me.
ex.zh: 有人过来把我笼头的喉带放松，又把勒得颈圈紧贴我身上的挽绳解开。

senses.d: not differentiated

ex.t: Not merely the love of one person but the animal instinct, the simple undifferentiated desire: that was the force that would tear the Party to pieces.
A violent emotion, not fear exactly but a sort of undifferentiated excitement, flared up in him, then faded again.
ex.zh: 一股猛烈的情绪在他心里烧起来，又不是恐惧，而是一种说不清的激动，然后又退了。

senses.d: not thought over and arranged systematically in the mind; not absorbed or assimilated mentally
x: an undigested mass of facts gathered at random

senses.d: not digested

ex.t: You may be an undigested bit of beef, a blot of mustard, a crumb of cheese, a fragment of an underdone potato.
ex.zh: 你也许是一块没消化的牛肉，一抹芥末，一点奶酪渣，一角没煮熟的土豆。

ex.t: In one word, Queequeg, said I, rather digressively; hell is an idea first born on an undigested apple-dumpling; and since then perpetuated through the hereditary dyspepsias nurtured by Ramadans.
ex.zh: 一句话，魁魁格，我说得有点离题了；地狱这个念头，最初是从一只没消化的苹果团子上生出来的；打那以后，又靠斋月养出来的、代代相传的消化不良，一直传了下来。

ex.t: They simply swallowed everything, and what they swallowed did them no harm, because it left no residue behind, just as a grain of corn will pass undigested through the body of a bird.
ex.zh: 他们干脆把什么都吞下去，吞下去的东西也不害他们，因为什么也没留下，就像一粒谷子穿过鸟的身体，不消化。

senses.d: lacking dignity

ex.t: Mr. Gresham was a very good man and a very religious man, but he told too many funny stories and made the people laugh in church; he was undignified, and you must have some dignity about a minister, mustn’t you, Matthew?
ex.zh: 格雷沙姆先生是个很好的人，很虔诚，可他笑话讲得太多，逗得大家在教堂里笑；他不庄重，牧师总得有点庄重，是不是，马修？

ex.t: Instead of which, that undignified creature answered, with an irrepressible sob, “Because you are going away.”
ex.zh: 可这没出息的人反倒带着按不住的抽噎答：“因为你要走了。”

ex.t: I don’t like this cobbling sort of business—I don’t like it at all; it’s undignified; it’s not my place.
ex.zh: 我不喜欢这种补补缝缝的活——我一点也不喜欢；这有失体面；这不是我该干的。

senses.d: not lessened or diminished

ex.t: From fire to oil was a natural transition for burned fingers, and Amy fell to painting with undiminished ardor.
ex.zh: 对烫了手指的人来说，从火转到油是自然的过渡，艾米就扑到油画上去了，热劲儿一点不减。

ex.t:
Mrs. Bennet rejoiced to see Jane in undiminished beauty; and more than once during dinner did Mr. Bennet say voluntarily to Elizabeth,----

“I am glad you are come back, Lizzy.”
ex.zh:
班纳特太太见简风姿依旧，十分高兴；吃饭时，班纳特先生还不止一次主动对伊丽莎白说：

“你回来了，我很高兴，莉琪。”

senses.d: any of various female water spirits

ex.t: I agree not to expect anything from Mother or you, but I do want to buy Undine and Sintran for myself.
ex.zh: 我同意不向妈妈和你要东西，可我真想给自己买一本《水妖与辛特拉姆》。

ex.t: “So am I,” added Jo, slapping the pocket wherein reposed the long-desired Undine and Sintram.
ex.zh: “我也一样，”乔补一句，拍拍口袋——那里头躺着她盼了好久的《水妖与辛特拉姆》。

senses.d: aimlessly drifting

ex.t: If your sagacity, knowledge, and experience, could put me on the right track, I might be able to do so much; unenlightened and undirected, I can do so little.
ex.zh: 要是你的精明、学识和经验能把我引上正路，我就能做很多；没人指点、没人指引，我就做不了什么。

ex.t: And yet the rage that one felt was an abstract, undirected emotion which could be switched from one object to another like the flame of a blowlamp.
ex.zh: 然而人所感到的这股怒火是抽象的、没有方向的情绪，可以像喷灯的火舌一样从一个对象转向另一个对象。

senses.d: not discovered
x: with earth-based telescopes many stars remain undiscovered

senses.d: not yet discovered

ex.t: If no adventurer were cast on the undiscovered island--it would remain undiscovered.
He was not, as the other traveller seemed to be, a savage inhabitant of some undiscovered island, but a European.
Its productions and features may be without example, as the phenomena of the heavenly bodies undoubtedly are in those undiscovered solitudes.

senses.d: plain to see

ex.t: Mr. Lorry immediately remembered, and regarded his new visitor with an undisguised look of abhorrence.
ex.zh: 洛里先生立刻想起来，便毫不掩饰地带着憎恶看这位新来的客人。

ex.t: He was staring at her with undisguised surprise, and disapproval also, she thought, for though he bowed and smiled, yet something in his honest eyes made her blush and wish she had her old dress on.
ex.zh: 他正盯着她看，那惊讶毫不掩饰，她觉得还有不赞成的意思；因为他虽然鞠躬微笑，那双诚实的眼睛里却有一样东西叫她脸红，叫她恨不得自己穿的是那件旧裙子。

ex.t: He also possessed a philosophic bent, to the great delight of his grandfather, who used to hold Socratic conversations with him, in which the precocious pupil occasionally posed his teacher, to the undisguised satisfaction of the womenfolk.
ex.zh: 他还有一副好穷理的性子，叫他爷爷大为高兴；爷爷常跟他作苏格拉底式的问答，这早熟的学生有时倒把老师问住，女人们便毫不掩饰地称意。

senses.d: generally agreed upon; not subject to dispute

ex.t: Thus the most vexatious and violent disputes would often arise between the fishermen, were there not some written or unwritten, universal, undisputed law applicable to all cases.
ex.zh: 这样，渔人之间往往要起最恼人、最激烈的争执，若不是有一条成文或不成文、普遍通行、无人置疑的法律，适用于一切情形的话。

ex.t: Meanwhile no Inner Party member wavers for an instant in his mystical belief that the war is real, and that it is bound to end victoriously, with Oceania the undisputed master of the entire world.
ex.zh: 同时，没有一个内党党员会有一刻动摇他那种神秘的信念：战争是真的，而且必定以胜利告终，大洋国将成为全世界无可争议的主人。

senses.d: not capable of being distinguished or differentiated
x: the two specimens are actually different from each other but the differences are almost indistinguishable

ex.t: The burial-place had got to the pass that its little heaps of poor grass were undistinguishable from one another; the figure on the Cross might have come down, for anything that could be seen of it.
ex.zh: 那片墓地已经到了这种地步：它那些小瘦草堆彼此都分不清了；十字架上那尊像，就看得见的部分而言，简直可能是走下来了。

senses.d: untroubled by interference or disturbance
x: he could pursue his studies undisturbed

ex.t: It was double-locked, as he had locked it with his own hands, and the bolts were undisturbed.
ex.zh: 门是上了双锁的，正如他亲手锁的那样，门闩也没被动过。

ex.t: Miss Pross had lighted the lamp, but had put it aside in a corner, that they might enjoy the fire-light undisturbed.
ex.zh: 普罗斯小姐已点起灯，却把它放到一个角落里，好让他们安安静静享受炉火的光。

ex.t: I was undisturbed by thoughts which during the preceding year had pressed upon me, notwithstanding my endeavours to throw them off, with an invincible burden.
ex.zh: 我不再被那些念头搅扰——过去这一年里，它们不顾我竭力摆脱，仍以不可战胜的重量压在我身上。

senses.d: not parted by conflict of opinion
not shared by or among others
not divided among or brought to bear on more than one object or objective
x: judging a contest with a single eye

senses.d: not separated into parts or shares; constituting an undivided unit
x: an undivided interest in the property

ex.t: Under the guidance of my new preceptors I entered with the greatest diligence into the search of the philosopher's stone and the elixir of life; but the latter soon obtained my undivided attention.
Under the guidance of my new preceptors I entered with the greatest diligence into the search of the philosopher’s stone and the elixir of life; but the latter soon obtained my undivided attention.
ex.zh: 在我这些新导师的指引下，我极其勤勉地投入了寻找哲人石和长生灵药的工作；可不久，后一样就占去了我全部的心思。

ex.t: We will not speak of all Queequeg’s peculiarities here; how he eschewed coffee and hot rolls, and applied his undivided attention to beefsteaks, done rare.
ex.zh: 魁魁格的那些怪癖，我们在这里不必一一细说；比如他怎么不碰咖啡和热面包卷，只把全副心思用在半生不熟的牛排上。

senses.d: cancel, annul, or reverse an action or its effect
x: I wish I could undo my actions

senses.d: deprive of certain characteristics
cause the ruin or downfall of
x: A single mistake undid the President and he had to resign

senses.d: cause to become loose
remove the outer cover or wrapping of

ex.t: "And now undo my bundle, Joe," said the first woman.
ex.zh: “现在解开我的包袱吧，乔，”头一个女人说。

ex.t: “Oh, do let me help to undo it!”
ex.zh: “哦，让我帮你解开它吧！”

ex.t: Undo the bundle and see, Meg,” said Beth, eying the knobby parcel with curiosity.
ex.zh: 解开包袱看看吧，梅格，”贝丝说，好奇地看着那鼓鼓囊囊的包。

senses.d: an act that makes a previous act of no effect (as if not done)
loosening the ties that fasten something
x: the tying of bow ties is an art; the untying is easy

ex.t: As soon as she had made out the proper way of nursing it, (which was to twist it up into a sort of knot, and then keep tight hold of its right ear and left foot, so as to prevent its undoing itself,) she carried it out into the open air.
John had praised her, and was undoing the old pocketbook which they called the ‘bank’, when Meg, knowing that it was quite empty, stopped his hand, saying nervously...
ex.zh: 约翰夸了她，正打开那只他们叫作“银行”的旧钱夹，梅格知道里头已经空了，就按住他的手，紧张地说——

ex.t: Why can’t I learn to keep it quiet?” groaned Jo, remembering words which had been her undoing.
ex.zh: 我怎么就学不会让它闭上呢？”乔呻吟道，想起那些害了自己的话。

senses.d: cancel, annul, or reverse an action or its effect
x: I wish I could undo my actions

senses.d: deprive of certain characteristics
cause the ruin or downfall of
x: A single mistake undid the President and he had to resign

senses.d: cause to become loose
remove the outer cover or wrapping of
not done
x: the work could be done or undone and nobody cared

ex.t: She did her best, she asked advice of Mrs. Cornelius, she racked her brain to remember what Hannah did that she left undone, she reboiled, resugared, and restrained, but that dreadful stuff wouldn’t ‘jell’.
ex.zh: 她尽了力，向科尼利厄斯太太讨主意，绞尽脑汁回想汉娜做了什么而自己漏了什么，重煮、加糖、再滤，可那可怕的东西就是不肯“冻”。

ex.t: They left nothing undone that was consistent with the reputation of their tribe.
ex.zh: 凡合乎他们族名声的事，他们一件也没落下。

ex.t: We are undone, but we are ourselves to blame.
ex.zh: 我们完了，可这只能怪自己。

senses.d: without doubt; certainly

ex.t: Its productions and features may be without example, as the phenomena of the heavenly bodies undoubtedly are in those undiscovered solitudes.
Undoubtedly it was.
ex.zh: 无疑是真的。

ex.t: “But our Defarge,” said Jacques Three, “is undoubtedly a good Republican?
ex.zh: “可我们的德法热，”雅克三号说，“无疑是个好共和派吧？

senses.d: stripped of drapery
lacking drapery or draperies

ex.t: That immaculate manliness we feel within ourselves, so far within us, that it remains intact though all the outer character seem gone; bleeds with keenest anguish at the undraped spectacle of a valor-ruined man.
ex.zh: 我们感到自身之内有那么一种无瑕的男子气概，它在我们里面那样深，纵使外面的一切品格似乎都消失了，它仍旧完好无损；而一见一个勇气毁尽了的人被剥得赤裸裸的样子，它就要以最尖利的痛苦流血。

senses.d: not imagined even in a dream

ex.t: “Undreamed of!” cried Mercedes, throwing up her hands in dainty dismay.
ex.zh: “想都别想！”默塞德斯叫起来，娇气地一惊，两手一扬。

senses.d: get undressed
x: please don't undress in front of everybody!
She strips in front of strangers every night for a living

x: The nurse quickly undressed the accident victim
She divested herself of her outdoor clothes

senses.d: partial or complete nakedness

ex.t: “Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed.
ex.zh: “好了，快点儿脱衣服上床吧。

ex.t: Now, I’ll undress Minnie May and put her to bed and you try to find some soft flannel cloths, Diana.
ex.zh: 现在我来给明妮·梅脱衣服，放她上床，黛安娜，你去找些软法兰绒布。

ex.t: “Let’s undress here,” said Diana.
ex.zh: “我们就在这儿脱衣裳吧，”黛安娜说。

senses.d: of lumber or stone or hides; not finished or dressed
having removed clothing

ex.t: But there was no help for it, so up stairs I went to my little room in the third floor, undressed myself as slowly as possible so as to kill time, and with a bitter sigh got between the sheets.
ex.zh: 可这事没法子，我只得上楼，到三楼我那间小屋子里去，尽可能慢地脱衣服，好磨掉些时间，然后凄惨地叹一口气，钻进被单里。

senses.d: get undressed
x: please don't undress in front of everybody!
She strips in front of strangers every night for a living

senses.d: remove (someone's or one's own) clothes
x: The nurse quickly undressed the accident victim
She divested herself of her outdoor clothes

ex.t: Meanwhile, he continued the business of undressing, and at last showed his chest and arms.
It could be shut off from the rest of the house by a tiny curtain, which Tink, who was most fastidious, always kept drawn when dressing or undressing.
Young Jerry, who had only made a feint of undressing when he went to bed, was not long after his father.
ex.zh: 小杰里上床时只是假装脱了衣服，父亲走后不久他就跟上了。

senses.d: not yet payable
not appropriate or proper (or even legal) in the circumstances
x: I didn't want to show undue excitement

senses.d: lacking justification or authorization
beyond normal limits

ex.t: His manner was brisk, and yet his general appearance gave an undue impression of age, for he had a slight forward stoop and a little bend of the knees as he walked.
ex.zh: 他的举止轻快，可整体外貌却给人年纪偏大的印象，因为他走路时微微前倾，膝盖也有些弯。

ex.t: Geniuses are rare and, without being at all an undue praiser of times past, one can say without hesitation that until the appearance of Hugh Lofting, the successor of Miss Yonge, Mrs. Ewing, Mrs. Gatty and Lewis Carroll had not appeared.
ex.zh: 天才是稀少的；而且我绝不是过分地夸赞往昔——可以毫不迟疑地说，在休·洛夫廷出现之前，扬格小姐、尤因夫人、加蒂夫人和刘易斯·卡罗尔的接班人一直都没有出现。

senses.d: stir up (water) so as to form ripples
occur in soft rounded shapes
move in a wavy pattern or with a rising and falling motion
x: the waves rolled towards the beach

senses.d: increase and decrease in volume or pitch, as if in waves
having a wavy margin and rippled surface

ex.t: For leagues and leagues it undulated round us, so that we seemed to be sailing through boundless fields of ripe and golden wheat.
ex.zh: 一里格又一里格，它在我们四周起伏，我们仿佛航行在无边无际、成熟金黄的麦田里。

ex.t: No perceptible face or front did it have; no conceivable token of either sensation or instinct; but undulated there on the billows, an unearthly, formless, chance-like apparition of life.
ex.zh: 它没有看得出的脸或正面；没有可以想见的表示感觉或本能的迹象；它只是在那里随波起伏，一个非人间的、无形无状的、偶然生成的生命的幻影。

senses.d: stir up (water) so as to form ripples
occur in soft rounded shapes
move in a wavy pattern or with a rising and falling motion
x: the waves rolled towards the beach

senses.d: increase and decrease in volume or pitch, as if in waves
having a wavy margin and rippled surface

ex.t: The huge corpulence of that Hogarthian monster undulates on the surface, scarcely drawing one inch of water.
ex.zh: 荷加斯那头怪物的庞大肥躯在水面上起伏，吃水几乎不到一英寸。

ex.t: Nor does this—its amazing strength, at all tend to cripple the graceful flexion of its motions; where infantileness of ease undulates through a Titanism of power.
ex.zh: 而这份惊人的力量，也丝毫不曾妨碍它动作那优美的屈伸；在那里，一种婴儿般的自在，起伏于一种泰坦式的力量之中。

senses.d: stir up (water) so as to form ripples
occur in soft rounded shapes
move in a wavy pattern or with a rising and falling motion
x: the waves rolled towards the beach

senses.d: increase and decrease in volume or pitch, as if in waves

ex.t: Whether it was that this undulating tester rolled the savage away to far distant scenes, I know not, but he now spoke of his native island; and, eager to hear his history, I begged him to go on and tell it.
ex.zh: 是这顶起伏的烟帐把这野人卷回到遥远的故地去了呢，还是别的缘故，我不知道；可他这时谈起了他的本岛；我急着听他的经历，就求他接着讲下去。

ex.t: But lazily undulating in the trough of the sea, and ever and anon tranquilly spouting his vapory jet, the whale looked like a portly burgher smoking his pipe of a warm afternoon.
ex.zh: 可他在波谷里懒懒地起伏，时不时安静地喷出一股雾气的喷泉，看起来像个在温暖午后抽烟斗的胖市民。

ex.t: The white men have in the meantime made a rude stockade on the summit of yonder undulating ground, at the foot of which a stream runs, for it is destruction to be too far from water.
ex.zh: 这期间白人在那边起伏的高地顶上草草筑了道栅栏，高地脚下有条溪流过，因为离水太远就是死路。

senses.d: an undulating curve
wavelike motion; a gentle rising and falling in the manner of waves
(physics) a movement up and down or back and forth

ex.t: While composing a little treatise on Eternity, I had the curiosity to place a mirror before me; and ere long saw reflected there, a curious involved worming and undulation in the atmosphere over my head.
ex.zh: 我在写一篇论永恒的小论文时，好奇地在面前摆了一面镜子；不久就看见镜里映出我头顶上空气中有一种奇特的、盘绕蜿蜒的波动。

senses.d: an undulating curve
wavelike motion; a gentle rising and falling in the manner of waves
(physics) a movement up and down or back and forth

ex.t: I saw him descend the mountain with greater speed than the flight of an eagle, and quickly lost among the undulations of the sea of ice.
ex.zh: 我看见他下山，比鹰飞还快，很快就在那冰海的起伏里不见了。

ex.t: There is, one knows not what sweet mystery about this sea, whose gently awful stirrings seem to speak of some hidden soul beneath; like those fabled undulations of the Ephesian sod over the buried Evangelist St. John.
ex.zh: 这海上有一种说不出的甜美神秘，它那轻柔而可畏的涌动，似乎在说着底下某个隐藏的灵魂；就像传说中以弗所的草地，在埋葬的传道者圣约翰上面起伏那样。

senses.d: to an undue degree
x: she was unduly pessimistic about her future

ex.t: Her love made her afraid of being unduly indulgent, indeed.
ex.zh: 这爱叫她生怕自己过于纵容。

ex.t: I no more felt unduly concerned for the landlord’s policy of insurance.
ex.zh: 我再也不为店主那份保险单过分操心了。

ex.t: But if there happen to be an unduly slender, clumsy, or timorous wight in the ship, that wight is certain to be made a ship-keeper.
ex.zh: 可船上若碰巧有个过分瘦弱、笨手笨脚或者胆小的家伙，那家伙准会被派去守船。

senses.d: lacking due respect or dutifulness

ex.t: I have no pleasure in talking to undutiful children.
ex.zh: 跟不孝顺的孩子说话，我一点乐趣也没有。

senses.d: bring to light
x: The CIA unearthed a plot to kill the President

senses.d: recover through digging

ex.t: Long John Silver unearthed a very competent man for a mate, a man named Arrow.
But when he was at last unearthed, and Spitz flew at him to punish him, Buck flew, with equal rage, in between.
ex.zh: 可等派克终于被刨出来，斯皮茨扑上去要罚他，巴克也带着同样的怒火扑到中间。

ex.t: A resident clerk was unearthed, who presently fetched from the library the Admiralty Tide Tables.
ex.zh: 我们找出一个值夜的文书，他不久从库房取来了海军部潮汐表。

senses.d: concerned with or affecting the spirit or soul
suggesting the operation of supernatural influences- John Galsworthy- Henry Kingsley

ex.t: The tall man called out again with a most unearthly cry, “Dead!”
ex.zh: 那高个子又用极其非人的声音叫起来：“死了！”

ex.t: The swoop of bats in the darkness over her was as the wings of unearthly creatures.
ex.zh: 蝙蝠在她头顶的黑暗里掠过，像是什么非人间的东西的翅膀。

ex.t: He approached; his countenance bespoke bitter anguish, combined with disdain and malignity, while its unearthly ugliness rendered it almost too horrible for human eyes.
ex.zh: 他走近了；他的面容显出苦味的剧痛，又夹着轻蔑与恶毒，而它那非人间的丑恶叫它几乎太可怕，不是人眼所能看。

senses.d: with anxiety or apprehension

ex.t: Matthew stirred uneasily.
They swung out on the trail with remarkable lack of exertion, turned their heads uneasily, and stopped in surprise.
Defarge, who had been uneasily biting his thumb-nail and looking at her, collected his face into a sterner expression.
ex.zh: 德法热一直不安地咬着拇指甲，看着她，这时把脸一收，做出更严厉的神情。

senses.d: feelings of anxiety that make you tense and irritable
physical discomfort (as mild sickness or depression)
embarrassment deriving from the feeling that others are critically aware of you
the trait of seeming ill at ease
inability to rest or relax or be still

ex.t: Indeed, it is this doubt and the uneasiness it sometimes causes me that has led me to our present confidence.”
ex.zh: 说实话，正是这份疑虑，以及它有时引起的不安，才引出了我们眼下这番交心。”

ex.t: He was in no uneasiness concerning his getting into the house again, for it was full of lodgers, and the door stood ajar all night.
ex.zh: 他不担心再进屋去，因为那房子里住满了房客，大门整夜虚掩着。

ex.t: There is such an uneasiness in Paris, that we have actually a run of confidence upon us!
ex.zh: 巴黎那边人心那么不安，我们这儿反倒真来了一阵信任潮！

senses.d: lacking a sense of security or affording no ease or reassurance
x: farmers were uneasy until rain finally came

senses.d: lacking or not affording physical or mental rest
x: she fell into an uneasy sleep

senses.d: causing or fraught with or showing anxiety
x: spent an anxious night waiting for the test results

senses.d: socially uncomfortable; unsure and constrained in manner
x: ill at ease among eddies of people he didn't know

senses.d: relating to bodily unease that causes discomfort

ex.t: Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute, "and then," thought she, "what would become of me?
The stranger has gradually improved in health but is very silent and appears uneasy when anyone except myself enters his cabin.
I was very uneasy and alarmed, as you may fancy, and it rather added to my fears to observe that the stranger was certainly frightened himself.

senses.d: not having a good education

ex.t: Even the common uneducated audience of the pit and gallery lost their interest in the play.
ex.zh: 连正厅和楼座那些没教养的普通观众也对戏失去了兴趣。

senses.d: not embarrassed- Jerome Stone
x: a tinseled charm and unabashed sentimentality
an unembarrassed greeting as if nothing untoward had happened

ex.t: Elizabeth, who had expected to find in her as acute and unembarrassed an observer as ever Mr. Darcy had been, was much relieved by discerning such different feelings.
ex.zh: 伊丽莎白原以为她会像达西先生那样眼光敏锐、从容不迫，如今看出她的心情全然不同，倒大大松了口气。

senses.d: people who are involuntarily out of work (considered as a group)
not engaged in a gainful occupation
x: unemployed workers marched on the capital

ex.t: I first became acquainted with him on board a whale vessel; finding that he was unemployed in this city, I easily engaged him to assist in my enterprise.
No doubt in that perfect world there had been no unemployed problem, no social question left unsolved.
ex.zh: 无疑，在那个完美的世界里，没有失业问题，没有未解决的社会问题。

senses.d: continuing forever or indefinitely
x: the ageless themes of love and revenge

ex.t: The result was a beautiful and unending family quarrel.
All that was needed was an unending series of victories over your own memory.
ex.zh: 所需要的只是对自己的记忆取得一连串无穷无尽的胜利。

ex.t: Day after day, for days unending, Buck toiled in the traces.
ex.zh: 一天又一天，没完没了，巴克在绳套里苦熬。

senses.d: incapable of being tolerated or endured

ex.t: He was standing in front of a wall of darkness, and on the other side of it there was something unendurable, something too dreadful to be faced.
ex.zh: 他站在一堵黑暗的墙前面，墙的那一边有什么无法忍受的东西，有什么可怕得不敢面对的东西。

ex.t: For you, they are unendurable.
ex.zh: 对你，它们受不了。

ex.t: Upon which impeachment of what to her was her most essential sex-prerogative, she made their lives unendurable.
ex.zh: 这等于攻击她身上最要紧的女性特权，她就叫他们日子过不下去。

senses.d: not enlightened; ignorant
x: the devices by which unenlightened men preserved the unjust social order

senses.d: lacking information or instruction
x: lamentably unenlightened as to the laws

ex.t: If your sagacity, knowledge, and experience, could put me on the right track, I might be able to do so much; unenlightened and undirected, I can do so little.
ex.zh: 要是你的精明、学识和经验能把我引上正路，我就能做很多；没人指点、没人指引，我就做不了什么。

senses.d: not enthusiastic; lacking excitement or ardor
x: an unenthusiastic performance by the orchestra

ex.t: “My face would be always dirty, wouldn't it?” said Phyllis, in unenthusiastic tones, “and I expect I should break something.”
ex.zh: “那我的脸不就老是脏兮兮的了？”菲利斯一点不带劲地说，“再说我准会弄坏什么东西。”

senses.d: poorly balanced or matched in quantity or value or measure
lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task

ex.t: “I am growing more and more unequal to the task I have set myself.
ex.zh: “我越来越担不起我给自己定下的这件事了。

ex.t: Thus situated, employed in the most detestable occupation, immersed in a solitude where nothing could for an instant call my attention from the actual scene in which I was engaged, my spirits became unequal; I grew restless and nervous.
ex.zh: 我处在这种情况下，做着最可憎的活，陷在一种孤独里，没有任何东西能有一刻把我的心从眼前的场景拉开，我的精神便变得不平衡；我变得烦躁而神经紧张。

ex.t: Do you suppose our mathematicians are unequal to that?
ex.zh: 你以为我们的数学家干不了这个？”

senses.d: in an unequal or partial manner
x: angry at being dealt with so unequally

ex.t: I am still a little afraid of missing something if I forget that, as my father snobbishly suggested, and I snobbishly repeat, a sense of the fundamental decencies is parcelled out unequally at birth.
ex.zh: 我至今仍有点怕自己会遗漏什么，倘若我忘了父亲那番势利的提醒、而我又势利地重复一遍的话：人的基本体面感，生来就是分配不均的。

senses.d: not liable to error-G.G.Coulton
x: the Church was...theoretically inerrant and omnicompetent

ex.t: But no longer snuffing in the trail of the wild beasts of the woodland, Tashtego now hunted in the wake of the great whales of the sea; the unerring harpoon of the son fitly replacing the infallible arrow of the sires.
ex.zh: 但塔什特戈如今不再嗅着林中野兽的足迹了，他追的是海里的大鲸；儿子那从不失手的鱼叉，正好接替了父辈那从不虚发的箭。

senses.d: without making errors
x: he unerringly fixed things for us

ex.t: Over unsounded gorges, through the rifled hearts of mountains, under torrents’ beds, unerringly I rush!
ex.zh: 越过无底的峡谷，穿过被凿空的山心，钻过激流的河床，我毫厘不差地冲过去！

senses.d: not basic or fundamental

ex.t: But all this part of it seemed remote and unessential.
ex.zh: 可这一切在我看来都遥远而不关紧要。

senses.d: not even or uniform as e.g. in shape or texture
(of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
x: vaudeville...waged an uneven battle against the church

senses.d: not divisible by two
variable and recurring at irregular intervals
lacking consistency
x: the golfer hit the ball well but his putting was spotty

ex.t: After a few hours the road began to be rough, and the walking grew so difficult that the Scarecrow often stumbled over the yellow bricks, which were here very uneven.
In this state they set forth with the sharp rain driving in their faces: clattering at a heavy dragoon trot over the uneven town pavement, and out upon the mire-deep roads.
ex.zh: 他们就这样出发，尖利的雨扑面打来：在高低不平的城中石板路上，以龙骑兵那种沉重的小跑嗒嗒作响，然后出了城，上了泥泞深陷的道路。

ex.t: The hard uneven pavement is under us, the soft deep mud is on either side.
ex.zh: 我们下面是又硬又不平的路面，两边是又软又深的泥。

senses.d: marked by no noteworthy or significant events
x: the voyage was pleasant and uneventful

ex.t: While these internal revolutions were going on, her external life had been as busy and uneventful as usual, and if she sometimes looked serious or a little sad no one observed it but Professor Bhaer.
ex.zh: 这些内心的翻腾进行着的时候，她外面的生活照旧忙碌而平淡；她有时神色郑重，或者有点伤心，可除了巴尔教授，谁也没看出来。

senses.d: in an uneventful manner

ex.t: It had begun so uneventfully, so precisely like a hundred other evenings, with Nana putting on the water for Michael’s bath and carrying him to it on her back.
ex.zh: 那一夜开始得那么平静，跟别的上百个夜晚一模一样：娜娜放好水给迈克尔洗澡，把他背到澡盆边。

senses.d: having no previous example or precedent or parallel

ex.t: Pardon this gush of sorrow; these ineffectual words are but a slight tribute to the unexampled worth of Henry, but they soothe my heart, overflowing with the anguish which his remembrance creates.
ex.zh: 请原谅这一阵悲伤；这些无用的话只是对亨利无人可比的价值的微薄敬意，可它们安慰了我的心——那心正满溢着因想起他而生的痛苦。

ex.t: It preaches a contempt for the working class unexampled for centuries past, and it dresses its members in a uniform which was at one time peculiar to manual workers and was adopted for that reason.
ex.zh: 它宣扬对工人阶级的蔑视，其程度在过去几百年里没有先例；它让党员穿一种制服，那制服一度是体力劳动者特有的，也正是因为这个原因才被采用。

ex.t: I can no longer help thanking you for your unexampled kindness to my poor sister.
ex.zh: 我不得不谢谢你对我那可怜的妹妹那份前所未有的好意。

senses.d: not expected or anticipated

ex.t: I suppose it was the unexpected nature of my loss that maddened me.
It carried me into great and unexpected peril; but it is a sacred object, and if it had carried me to death I hope it would have sustained me.”
ex.zh: 它把我带进了极大而意外的危险；可那是个神圣的目的，就算它把我带到死地，我希望它也会支撑我。”

ex.t: Anne came running in presently, her face sparkling with the delight of her orchard rovings; but, abashed at finding the delight herself in the unexpected presence of a stranger, she halted confusedly inside the door.
ex.zh: 过了一会儿，安妮跑了进来，脸上还闪着在果园里游荡的欢喜；可她一见屋里有个意想不到的生人，自己的欢喜一下子无处安放，便窘迫地在门里站住了。

senses.d: in a way that was not expected
x: her brother showed up at the wedding out of the blue

senses.d: without advance planning

ex.t: If John had not forgotten all about the jelly, it really would have been unpardonable in him to choose that day, of all the days in the year, to bring a friend home to dinner unexpectedly.
We will say that he was unexpectedly found at his forge again.
ex.zh: 咱们就说，他出人意料地又被人发现站在他的铁炉前。

ex.t: As I was telling you last night when Lucie came in so unexpectedly, I have at length done all that I can do here.
ex.zh: 就像昨晚露西那样突然进来时我跟你说的，我在这儿能做的终于都做完了。

senses.d: not explained
having the reason or cause not made clear

ex.t: That, he seemed on the point of being at once released, when the tide in his favour met with some unexplained check (not intelligible to the Doctor), which led to a few words of secret conference.
ex.zh: 看来他就要立刻获释，可那股对他有利的势头忽然遇到一种说不清的阻滞（医生也不明白），引得几个人低声密谈了几句。

senses.d: not yet discovered

ex.t: I am going to unexplored regions, to "the land of mist and snow," but I shall kill no albatross; therefore do not be alarmed for my safety or if I should come back to you as worn and woeful as the "Ancient Mariner."
Then unexplored patches arose in it and spread, black shadows moved about in them, the roar of the beasts of prey was quite different now, and above all, you lost the certainty that you would win.
Sir Isaac Newton is said to have avowed that he felt like a child picking up shells beside the great and unexplored ocean of truth.

senses.d: not liable to failure
x: the unfailing sign of an amateur

senses.d: always able to supply more
x: an unfailing source of good stories

senses.d: unceasing

ex.t: Dress was the one unfailing talisman and charm used for keeping all things in their places.
ex.zh: 衣着是唯一从不失效的符咒和法术，用来把一切事物都保持在它们的位置上。

ex.t: The correspondence flourished famously, and letters flew to and fro with unfailing regularity all through the early spring.
ex.zh: 通信兴旺得很，整个初春，信都按时来来去去，从没误过。

ex.t: They’ll make you sick,” says Mamma to the young person who offers his services in the kitchen with unfailing regularity on plum-pudding day.
ex.zh: 要肚子疼的。”妈妈对这位每逢做李子布丁的日子就准到厨房来帮忙的小人物说。

senses.d: without fail

ex.t: If he braved the matter out, death would unfailingly come upon him, and usually in some strange and unforeseen manner.
ex.zh: 要是他硬顶下去，死亡必定会降临到他头上，而且往往以某种离奇、出乎意料的方式。

senses.d: not fair; marked by injustice or partiality or deception

ex.t: Her presence had seemed a blessing to them, but it would be unfair to her to keep her in poverty and want when Providence afforded her such powerful protection.
All here is so unprecedented, so changed, so sudden and unfair, that I am absolutely lost.
ex.zh: 这里一切都那么没有先例，那么变了样，那么突然、那么不公，我简直完全没了主意。

ex.t: I cheered him up and persuaded him to stay to the end because it would be unfair to Miss Stacy if he didn’t.

ex.zh: 可她天生比那匹黑马性子急；苍蝇更招她烦，挽具哪儿不对劲，她更受不住；要是有人虐待她、亏待她，她多半是要一报还一报的。

ex.zh: 每个孩子头一回受到不公平对待，都是这样。

ex.zh: 叫彼得发懵的不是疼，是这不公平。

ex.zh: 不久，大家各喝了一口，就躺下睡了；西尔弗报复的表面文章，是派乔治·梅里放哨，还威胁他若不忠心就要他的命。

ex.zh: 听！那地狱般的狂欢！那欢闹在船头！你再看船尾那毫不动摇的寂静！

ex.zh: 因为它们只是被人从一个海角赶到另一个海角；若有一处海岸不再因它们的水柱而生动，那么你放心，总有别的、更远的海岸最近才被这不常见的景象惊动过。

ex.zh: 农妇们把那些不时髦的娃娃关在身边养大，而六十岁的迷人奶奶们打扮起来、吃起夜宵来，还跟二十岁一样。

ex.zh: 梅格和约翰恰好一同站在草地中间，劳里忽然来了个灵感，给这场不时兴的婚礼添上了最后一笔。

ex.zh: 乔跪下去，好方便解开它；他解开许多个结，拖出一大卷又大又沉的深色料子。

ex.zh: 戴夫病成那样，还是不愿被解下来，解绳的时候他哼哼、低吼；看见索尔莱克斯站上他守了那么久的位子，他伤心得呜呜叫。

ex.zh: “在深不可测的水里追索我们的研究，是何等不宜。”

ex.t: O man unfathomable.
ex.zh: 人啊，深不可测。

ex.zh: 那是黑沉沉、险恶的水的海，是浪头对着浪头毁灭性掀起的海，它的深处还没探到底，它的力量还没人知道。

ex.zh: 治安官用锐利的眼睛看着我，自然从我的神态里得了个不好的兆头。

ex.zh: 弄不到马，我只能由湖上回去；可风不顺，雨又倾盆地下。

ex.zh: 可这也有不便之处；她最后打定主意：先私下打听这家人可在不在，若问得不好，再走这一步也不迟。

ex.zh: 这当口，火还没生，营支了一半，狗也没喂。

ex.zh: “真该挑圣诞节这一天，”她说，“来为斯克鲁奇先生这样一个人干杯：可憎、吝啬、心硬、无情。

ex.zh: “你推得真漂亮，”我由衷地赞叹道。

那咒语并非柯尔律治最早施下的；施下它的是上帝那位伟大而不奉承的桂冠诗人——自然。*

ex.zh: 可她默想了几分钟，又说：“我倒记得有一天在尼日斐，他夸口说他怨恨起来绝不罢休，说他是个不肯宽恕的脾气。

ex.t: But the chief grievance that rankled in her soul, and gave an excuse for her unfriendly conduct, was a rumor which some obliging gossip had whispered to her, that the March girls had made fun of her at the Lambs’.
ex.zh: 可是她心里最扎根、也给她那不友好的举动找到借口的，是一桩谣言：有位好事的嚼舌人悄悄告诉她，马奇家姐妹在拉姆家拿她取笑。

ex.t: Wendy could no longer see to thread her needle, and when she looked up, the lagoon that had always hitherto been such a laughing place seemed formidable and unfriendly.
ex.zh: 温迪再也看不清穿针，抬起头来，一向那么爱笑的礁湖，此刻显得凶险而不友好。

ex.t: This stratagem succeeded so well that ere long the Bulls grew cold and unfriendly, and finally avoided each other and fed each one by himself apart.
ex.zh: 这计策十分奏效，不久三头牛就冷淡疏远起来，最后各自避开，分开吃草。

senses.d: not frozen

ex.t: There were fringes of ice along the sea margin, with drifting masses farther out; but the main expanse of that salt ocean, all bloody under the eternal sunset, was still unfrozen.
ex.zh: 海边结着冰缘，更远处有漂流的冰块；但那片咸涩大洋的主体，在永恒落日下血红一片，仍然没有冻住。

senses.d: of persons; marked by failure to realize full potentialities

ex.t: You took me on board when my vigour was exhausted, and I should soon have sunk under my multiplied hardships into a death which I still dread, for my task is unfulfilled.
ex.zh: 我力气用尽时，你把我接上了船；不然我不久就会在这重重艰辛下沉入一种我至今还怕的死，因为我的事还没做完。

ex.t: How all this will terminate, I know not, but I had rather die than return shamefully, my purpose unfulfilled.
ex.zh: 这一切会怎样了结，我不知道；可我宁愿死，也不愿耻辱地回去，让我的目的没完成。

senses.d: lacking grace in movement or posture

senses.d: difficult to handle or manage especially because of shape

ex.t: He may have been quite right in thinking so, for he was an odd-looking personage, with an ungainly figure and long iron-gray hair that touched his stooping shoulders, and a full, soft brown beard which he had worn ever since he was twenty.
Its evil eyes were wriggling on their stalks, its mouth was all alive with appetite, and its vast ungainly claws, smeared with an algal slime, were descending upon me.

So he got up from his place and began dancing, but he cut such a ridiculous figure as he plunged about, and made such a grotesque exhibition of his ungainly person, that the beasts all fell upon him with ridicule and drove him away.
ex.zh: 他便从座位上起来跳舞，可他扭来扭去的样子实在可笑，那笨拙的身架摆出种种怪相，众兽一齐哄笑他，把他赶走了。

a meanspirited man unwilling to forgive

ex.zh: “要是假装不知道你的克制是出于对她父亲的体谅，那就不厚道了。

ex.t: On that head, therefore, I shall be uniformly silent: and you may assure yourself that no ungenerous reproach shall ever pass my lips when we are married.”
ex.zh: 所以这上头我一概不提；你可以放心，等我们结了婚，我嘴里决不会漏出一句小气的埋怨。”

ex.t: No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there.
ex.zh: 你在那件事上做得不公道、不宽厚，没有任何动机可以辩解。

senses.d: lacking in magnanimity- Times Litt. Sup.

ex.t: I have not treated her ungenerously, and she had no just cause of complaint against me, but you know what women are, Mr. Holmes.
ex.zh: 我待她不薄，她也没有正当理由抱怨我；可您知道女人是怎么回事，福尔摩斯先生。

senses.d: not of the nobility

ex.t: So you must try to be contented with making your name boyish, and playing brother to us girls,” said Beth, stroking the rough head with a hand that all the dish washing and dusting in the world could not make ungentle in its touch.
ex.zh: 那你就将就着，用个男孩子的名字，给我们姑娘家当兄弟吧。”贝丝说着，摸摸那颗毛茸茸的头。她那双手不管洗多少碗、掸多少灰，摸上去还是那么轻柔。

senses.d: not befitting a gentleman

ex.t: “I’ll try, but it was a very ungentlemanly thing to do, I didn’t think you could be so sly and malicious, Laurie,” replied Meg, trying to hide her maidenly confusion under a gravely reproachful air.
ex.zh: “我尽量吧；可这事实在不像个君子干的，我没想到你会这样鬼祟、这样存心，劳里，”梅格回答，想用一脸郑重的责备遮住少女的慌乱。

ex.t: And if he were not lively about it, if he did not go with a nimble hop-skip-and-jump, then Tashtego had an ungentlemanly way of accelerating him by darting a fork at his back, harpoon-wise.
ex.zh: 他若是办得不麻利，若不用轻快的蹦跳跑来跑去，塔什特戈就有一种不合绅士体统的办法催他快些——拿叉子照他背上掷去，像掷鱼叉一样。

senses.d: not furnished with glass
