senses.d: not having a shiny coating

ex.t: There was a small, heavily-grated, unglazed window high in the wall, with a stone screen before it, so that the sky could be only seen by stooping low and looking up.
ex.zh: 高高的墙上有一扇小小的、装了粗铁栅、没有玻璃的窗子，窗前有一道石挡板，要看天只能弯下腰抬头望。

ex.t: The roof was in shadow, and the windows, partially glazed with coloured glass and partially unglazed, admitted a tempered light.
ex.zh: 屋顶在阴影里，窗子一部分镶着彩色玻璃，一部分没有玻璃，透进柔和的光。

senses.d: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
x: he said it was sinful to wear lipstick

ex.t: He’s a grand, ungodly, god-like man, Captain Ahab; doesn’t speak much; but, when he does speak, then you may well listen.
ex.zh: 他是个气派非凡、不敬神、却像神一样的人，亚哈船长；话不多；可他一开口，你就该好好听着。

ex.t: Peleg!” said Bildad, lifting his eyes and hands, “thou thyself, as I myself, hast seen many a perilous time; thou knowest, Peleg, what it is to have the fear of death; how, then, can’st thou prate in this ungodly guise.
ex.zh: 佩莱格！”比勒达抬起眼睛和双手说，“你自己跟我一样，见过许多危难的时刻；你知道，佩莱格，怀着对死亡的恐惧是什么滋味；那你怎么还能这样不敬神地胡扯。

senses.d: incapable of being controlled
x: the little boy's parents think he is spirited, but his teacher finds him unruly

ex.t: In a word, it was Queequeg’s conceit, that if a man made up his mind to live, mere sickness could not kill him: nothing but a whale, or a gale, or some violent, ungovernable, unintelligent destroyer of that sort.
ex.zh: 一句话，魁魁格的想头是：一个人若打定主意要活，单是疾病杀不了他；只有鲸、或者大风，或者别的什么暴烈的、管不住的、没脑子的毁灭者才成。

ex.t: What was worst of all was that by means of such organizations as the Spies they were systematically turned into ungovernable little savages, and yet this produced in them no tendency whatever to rebel against the discipline of the Party.
ex.zh: 最糟的是，通过少年侦察队这类组织，他们被系统地变成无法无天的小野人，可这丝毫没有使他们产生反抗党纪律的倾向。

ex.t: She was not of so ungovernable a temper as Lydia; and, removed from the influence of Lydia’s example, she became, by proper attention and management, less irritable, less ignorant, and less insipid.
ex.zh: 她的性子不像莉迪亚那样管不住；一离开莉迪亚的榜样，再加上好好的照看和管教，她便不那么爱生气，不那么无知，也不那么乏味了。

senses.d: without grace; rigidly

ex.zh: 她穿着从孤儿院带来的那件又短又紧的棉毛混纺连衣裙，下面两条细腿显得又长又不好看，模样确实是个怪模怪样的小东西。

senses.d: lacking charm and good taste

ex.zh: “一个男孩子，算很不错了，”梅格答得有点不客气，因为这话不叫她起劲。

ex.zh: “这个不知好歹、忘恩负义的狗东西！”斯塔巴克喊道；“他竟拿我不到五分钟前给他装满的济贫箱来嘲弄我、向我叫阵！”——随后用他那种老有的激烈低语——“使劲划，猎狗们！

ex.t: Oh, how heartily did she grieve over every ungracious sensation she had ever encouraged, every saucy speech she had ever directed towards him!
ex.zh: 哦，她心里多么痛悔，悔自己从前纵容过的每一分不近人情的情绪，悔自己向他说过的每一句无礼的话！

senses.d: without grace; rigidly

ex.zh: “不行也得行吧。”布卢伊特太太没好气地说。

ex.zh: “说出来！”他嚷道；她就用一句不合语法的话，长得像魔术师从嘴里拉出来的彩带，讲了温迪和孩子们被捉的事。

ex.zh: “我敢说他给了我们不少乐子，”弗雷德说，“要是不为他的健康干一杯，那就太不知好歹了。

ex.zh: “别不知好歹。

ex.zh: 我是个坏透了、不知感恩的丫头，活该受罚，活该被体面人永远赶出去。

ex.zh: “我看秘密跟我不合脾胃，你告诉了我，我心里就乱糟糟的，”乔有点不领情地说。

ex.t: She was too tired, sometimes, even to smile, John grew dyspeptic after a course of dainty dishes and ungratefully demanded plain fare.
ex.zh: 她有时候累得连笑都笑不出；约翰吃了一程精致菜，倒吃出消化不良来，不领情地要粗茶淡饭。

senses.d: lacking protection or a guard
x: his unguarded queen was open to attack

senses.d: displaying or feeling no wariness

ex.t: I will not lead you on, unguarded and ardent as I then was, to your destruction and infallible misery.
ex.zh: 我不愿像当年我自己那样毫无防备又满腔热望，把你引向毁灭和那无可避免的苦难。

ex.t: I have a warm unguarded temper, and I may perhaps have sometimes spoken my opinion of him, and to him, too freely.
ex.zh: 我性子急，又不加检点，也许有时候议论他，或当面对他说，都说得太随便。

ex.t: But the wisdom of our ancestors is in the simile; and my unhallowed hands shall not disturb it, or the Country's done for.
ex.zh: 可这个比喻里藏着我们祖宗的智慧；我这双不敬的手不会去动它——一动，这国家就完了。

ex.t: Who shall conceive the horrors of my secret toil as I dabbled among the unhallowed damps of the grave or tortured the living animal to animate the lifeless clay?
ex.zh: 谁能想象我暗中劳作的种种可怖——我在坟墓那不洁净的潮气里摸索，为要给无生命的泥土以生气，而去折磨活着的动物？

ex.t: Thus spoke my prophetic soul, as, torn by remorse, horror, and despair, I beheld those I loved spend vain sorrow upon the graves of William and Justine, the first hapless victims to my unhallowed arts.
ex.zh: 我的灵魂就这样预言着，那时我被悔恨、恐怖和绝望撕扯，看着我那些心爱的人把徒然的悲伤洒在威廉和贾斯汀的坟上——他们是我那亵渎的技艺头一批不幸的牺牲。

ex.zh: “不幸她身体欠佳，不能到城里来；因此，正如我有天对凯瑟琳夫人本人所说，英国宫廷也就少了它最光彩的一件饰物。

Anne’s unhappiness continued for a week.
ex.zh: 安妮的不幸持续了一个星期。

ex.t: Is this to prognosticate peace, or to mock at my unhappiness?”
ex.zh: 这是在预示和平，还是在讥笑我的不幸？”

generalized feeling of distress

marked by or producing unhappiness- American Guide Series

I have seen him wringing his hands after such a rebuff, and I am sure the annoyance and the terror he lived in must have greatly hastened his early and unhappy death.

ex.zh: 它身体虽未受伤，却发出叫喊，像某个国王的鬼魂在超自然的痛苦里。

ex.zh: 小艇虽然整个儿灌满了水，却几乎没受损伤。

ex.zh: 这工夫第三个绕着屋子跑了一圈，一点儿没伤着，忽然出现在门口，挥着短剑朝医生砍去。

ex.t: Then the mice were unharnessed from the truck and scampered away through the grass to their homes.
ex.zh: 接着田鼠们从车上解下来，蹿过草地回家去了。

senses.d: not in or exhibiting good health in body or mind
detrimental to health
not conducive to good health

ex.zh: 它越少被健康的事占着，就越有危险往不健康的方向去。

ex.t:
But that was not all: standing as I did on a quantity of moist straw my feet grew unhealthy and tender, and the master used to say:

“I don't know what is the matter with this horse; he goes very fumble-footed.
ex.zh:
这还不算：我老站在一大堆湿草上，蹄子就变得不健康，又软又疼；主人常说：

“我不知道这马怎么了，走起来脚底下很不利索。

ex.t: There were no carpets and no signs of any furniture above the ground floor, while the plaster was peeling off the walls, and the damp was breaking through in green, unhealthy blotches.
ex.zh: 一层以上没有地毯，也看不出有家具的痕迹；墙上的灰泥在剥落，潮气透出来，结成一片片发绿的、病态的斑块。

senses.d: not necessarily inaudible but not heard

ex.zh: 村里的喷泉看不见、听不见地流着，宅邸的喷泉看不见、听不见地滴着——两者都像从时间之泉里落下的分分秒秒一样消逝——过了三个黑暗的钟头。

ex.t: “Yes, of course,” said Marilla, as if getting boys from orphan asylums in Nova Scotia were part of the usual spring work on any well-regulated Avonlea farm instead of being an unheard of innovation.
ex.zh: “当然是真的。”玛丽拉说，那口气就像从新斯科舍的孤儿院领个男孩，是任何一家管得好的阿冯利农庄春天照例要干的活，而不是什么闻所未闻的新花样。

ex.t: Marilla had come in unheard by the small dreamer.
ex.zh: 玛丽拉进来时，这个小做梦家一点没听见。

ex.zh: “好吃的东西”这词孩子们没听过——可他们猜是糖果，因为他从袋子里拿出三个扎绿丝带的大盒子，粉的绿的，里头装着一层又一层说不出的好巧克力。

ex.zh: 这里也许藏着一点至今没人留意的意思。

ex.zh: 不知过了多久，我一直抓着那台摇晃震动的机器，全然不顾自己到了哪里；等我定下神再看那些表盘时，我惊讶地发现我到了什么地方。

ex.zh: 大树们觉得这请求不算什么，立刻答应了，毫不迟疑地给他一棵小白蜡树苗，他就用它做了想要的斧柄。

ex.zh: 那十条狗的队解了下来，巴克套着自己的挽具，被安到雪橇上。

But Phyllis, always unlucky, had upset a jug of lemonade down the front of her dress.

senses.d: not possessing qualities befitting a man
lacking in courage and manly strength and resolution; contemptibly fearful
without qualities thought to befit a man

ex.t: Jo wanted to lay her head down on that motherly bosom, and cry her grief and anger all away, but tears were an unmanly weakness, and she felt so deeply injured that she really couldn’t quite forgive yet.
ex.zh: 乔很想把头埋进那母亲的怀里，把委屈和怒气哭个干净；可流眼泪是没出息的人才干的软弱事，她又觉得自己受了那么大的委屈，实在还咽不下这口气。

ex.t: It might be unmanly, but he couldn’t help it, and I am glad of it.
ex.zh: 这也许不像男子汉，可他忍不住，我倒为这个高兴。

ex.t: “Silver, if you like,” cried the squire; “but as for that intolerable humbug, I declare I think his conduct unmanly, unsailorly, and downright un-English.”
ex.zh: “西尔弗，那还罢了，”乡绅叫道，“可那个叫人受不了的假货，我说他做事不像个男人，不像个水手，简直就不像个英国人。”

senses.d: lacking a crew

ex.t: Here’s a man from Man; a man born in once independent Man, and now unmanned of Man; which is sucked in—by what?
ex.zh: 这儿有个人来自马恩岛；一个生在曾经独立的马恩岛、如今被马恩岛去了势的人；那岛被吸进去了——被什么吸的？

senses.d: socially incorrect in behavior
x: resentment flared at such an unmannered intrusion

ex.t: “The unmannerly Dutch dogger!” cried Stubb.
ex.zh: “这没规矩的荷兰渔船！”斯塔布喊道。

ex.t: Halloa! whew! there goes my tarpaulin overboard; Lord, Lord, that the winds that come from heaven should be so unmannerly!
ex.zh: 喂！呼！我的油布帽掉到海里去了；主啊，主啊，从天上来的风竟这样没规矩！

senses.d: not having an identifying mark
not taken into account
x: his retirement was not allowed to go unmarked

ex.t: The evening passed quietly, unmarked by anything extraordinary.
ex.zh: 这一晚过得很平静，没有什么特别的事。

senses.d: not married or related to the unmarried state

ex.t: A married woman grabs at her baby; an unmarried one reaches for her jewel-box.

And so it came to pass that in the summer I was sold to Mr. Barry.

30 A Thief

My new master was an unmarried man.
ex.zh:
就这么着，那年夏天我被卖给了巴里先生。

第三十章 一个贼。

我的新主人是个没成家的男人。

senses.d: reveal the true nature of
x: The journal article unmasked the corrupt politician

ex.t: Unmask and receive my blessing.”
ex.zh: 摘下面具，领我的祝福吧。”

senses.d: reveal the true nature of
x: The journal article unmasked the corrupt politician

senses.d: take the mask off

ex.t: I enjoyed it very much, and when we unmasked it was fun to see them stare at me.
ex.zh: 我玩得很痛快；等大家摘了面具，看他们瞪着我，真有趣。

ex.t: A day never passed when spies and saboteurs acting under his directions were not unmasked by the Thought Police.
ex.zh: 没有一天没有受他指使的间谍和破坏分子被思想警察揭出来。

senses.d: without meaning--Pythagoras
x: Silence is better than unmeaning words

ex.t: He flopped the reins about as we started, and of course gave me several unmeaning cuts with the whip, though I was fairly off.
ex.zh: 一出发他就把缰乱甩，还无缘无故抽了我好几鞭，我明明已经走得很顺了。

ex.t: It was all very indistinct: the heavy smell, the big unmeaning shapes, the obscene figures lurking in the shadows, and only waiting for the darkness to come at me again!
ex.zh: 一切都十分模糊：浓重的气味，那些毫无意义的庞然形状，那些潜伏在阴影里、只等黑暗再次扑向我的污秽身影！

senses.d: without meaning--Pythagoras
x: Silence is better than unmeaning words

ex.t: Oh, Pip! thy wretched laugh, thy idle but unresting eye; all thy strange mummeries not unmeaningly blended with the black tragedy of the melancholy ship, and mocked it!
ex.zh: 啊，皮普！你那可怜的笑，你那闲散却不得安歇的眼睛；你那些古怪的哑剧，都不是毫无意义地混进这条忧郁的船的黑悲剧里，而且在嘲弄它！

senses.d: not composed of measured syllables; not metrical
without limits in extent or size or quantity--Sophocles
x: limitless vastness of our solar system
The long unmeasured pulse of time moves everything. There is nothing hidden that it cannot bring to light, nothing once known that may not become unknown.

ex.t: I’ll ten times girdle the unmeasured globe; yea and dive straight through it, but I’ll slay him yet!”
ex.zh: 我要绕着这无法丈量的地球转十圈；是的，还要直穿过去，可我总要把他杀掉！”

senses.d: in an unmelodious manner

ex.t: He lolled at his ease, humming, not unmelodiously, snatches of a rude song, and fingering a pack of cards.
ex.zh: 他懒懒地靠着，哼一支粗野小曲的片段，哼得还不难听，手指拨弄着一副牌。

senses.d: not melted
x: streets unpassable because of piles of unmelted snow

ex.t: The great buildings about me stood out clear and distinct, shining with the wet of the thunderstorm, and picked out in white by the unmelted hailstones piled along their courses.
ex.zh: 周围那些巨大建筑清晰分明地显现出来，被雷雨的湿气浸得发亮，沿墙的层线还堆着未化的冰雹，把它们衬出白线。

senses.d: a garment worn under other garments
unsuitable or forbidden as a topic of conversation

ex.t: Wonderfullest things are ever the unmentionable; deep memories yield no epitaphs; this six-inch chapter is the stoneless grave of Bulkington.
ex.zh: 最奇妙的事永远是不可言说的；深沉的记忆不产出墓志铭；这六英寸长的一章，就是布尔金顿没有墓碑的坟。

senses.d: without pity; in a merciless manner
x: he was mercilessly trounced by his opponent in the House

ex.t: But one day he was unwise enough to start chattering, when they at once saw through his disguise and pecked him so unmercifully that he was glad to escape and join his own kind again.
The only poor comfort he had was that she snubbed Charlie Sloane, unmercifully, continually, and undeservedly.
ex.zh: 他唯一的、可怜的安慰，就是她毫不留情、接二连三、无缘无故地冷落查理·斯隆。

ex.t: Here we saw a cart heavily laden with bricks; the wheels had stuck fast in the stiff mud of some deep ruts, and the carter was shouting and flogging the two horses unmercifully.
ex.zh: 这儿有一辆装满了砖的大车；车轮死死陷在深深的车辙里，泥又稠又黏；赶车的又喊又打，把那两匹马抽得没一点情面。

senses.d: not mindful or attentive- G.B.Shaw
x: while thus unmindful of his steps he stumbled

senses.d: (followed by `to' or `of') lacking conscious awareness of
x: oblivious of the mounting pressures for political reform
oblivious to the risks she ran

ex.t: Nor was Ahab unmindful of another thing.
ex.zh: 亚哈也没有忽略另一件事。

ex.t: Unmindful of the tedious rope-ladders of the shrouds, the men, like shooting stars, slid to the deck, by the isolated backstays and halyards; while Ahab, less dartingly, but still rapidly was dropped from his perch.
ex.zh: 那些人不管侧支索上那累人的绳梯，像流星一样，顺着单独的后支索和升降索滑到甲板上；亚哈呢，没那么疾，可也很快地从他的高座上被放下来。

senses.d: not mixed with extraneous elements

ex.t: I passed a night of unmingled wretchedness.
ex.zh: 我过了一个纯粹凄惨的夜。

senses.d: clearly evident to the mind
x: his opposition to slavery was unmistakable

senses.d: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
x: the effects of the drought are apparent to anyone who sees the parched fields

ex.t: But the odour of camphor was unmistakable.
He had got together a big bunch and was smelling their faint sickly scent when a sound at his back froze him, the unmistakable crackle of a foot on twigs.
Both Marilla and Mrs. Lynde recognized its unmistakable ring.
ex.zh: 玛丽拉和林德太太都听出了那不容错认的声调。

senses.d: without possibility of mistake
x: this watercolor is unmistakably a synthesis of nature

senses.d: in a signal manner

ex.t: But if, like Queequeg and me in the bed, the tip of your nose or the crown of your head be slightly chilled, why then, indeed, in the general consciousness you feel most delightfully and unmistakably warm.
ex.zh: 可要是像床上的魁魁格和我这样，你的鼻尖或者头顶稍稍有点凉，那么，在总体的感觉里，你真会觉得暖得再舒服不过、再分明不过。

ex.t: It was definitely, unmistakably, a shade of green.
ex.zh: 那确实是、明白无误地，一种绿色。

ex.t: The fingers stood up before his eyes like pillars, enormous, blurry, and seeming to vibrate, but unmistakably four.
ex.zh: 那些手指像柱子一样立在他眼前，巨大、模糊、似乎在颤，但明白无误是四根。

senses.d: not diminished or moderated in intensity or severity; sometimes used as an intensifier

ex.t: He never used to swear, though, at his men, they said; but somehow he got an inordinate quantity of cruel, unmitigated hard work out of them.
ex.zh: 不过他们说，他从不骂人；可不知怎么的，他总能从他们身上榨出多得没边的、毫不留情的苦活来。

senses.d: not mixed with extraneous elements
not constituting a compound

ex.t: His face had become frozen, as it were, in a very curious look at Darnay: an intent look, deepening into a frown of dislike and distrust, not even unmixed with fear.
ex.zh: 他的脸仿佛冻住了，正用一种很古怪的神情看达尔内：那目光专注，渐渐深成一种厌恶和不信任的皱眉，甚至还掺着恐惧。

senses.d: not interfered with, disturbed, or harmed

ex.t: As it was, I lived ungazed at and unmolested, hardly thanked for the pittance of food and clothes which I gave, so much does suffering blunt even the coarsest sensations of men.
ex.zh: 可事实上，我住着没人来看，也没人来扰，我给的那点食物和衣服几乎得不到一声谢——苦难就这样把连人最粗的感觉都磨钝了。

ex.t: If unmolested, upon rising to the surface, the Sperm Whale will continue there for a period of time exactly uniform with all his other unmolested risings.
ex.zh: 若不受打扰，抹香鲸浮到水面后，会在那里待上一段跟他所有别的未受打扰的浮升完全一样长的时间。

ex.t: Besides, if you regard him very closely, and time him with your watch, you will find that when unmolested, there is an undeviating rhyme between the periods of his jets and the ordinary periods of respiration.
ex.zh: 再说，你若非常仔细地观察他，用表给他计时，就会发现：不受打扰时，他喷射的间隔跟他平常呼吸的间隔之间，有一种毫不偏差的韵律。

senses.d: emotionally unmoved
x: always appeared completely unmoved and imperturbable

senses.d: being in the original position; not having been moved
x: the archeologists could date the vase because it was in situ

ex.t: Still the Ghost pointed with an unmoved finger to the head.
ex.zh: 那幽灵仍旧一动不动地用手指着死者的头。

ex.t: This vocal exercise usually conquered Meg, but John sat as unmoved as the post which is popularly believed to be deaf.
ex.zh: 这嗓子的操练往常总能降住梅格；约翰却坐得纹丝不动，像俗话说的那根聋柱子。

ex.t:
“No.”

To show that her departure would leave him unmoved, he skipped up and down the room, playing gaily on his heartless pipes.
ex.zh: “不走。”为了表示她走也动不了他，他在屋里蹦来蹦去，快活地吹着他那没心肝的笛子。

senses.d: (used of grass or vegetation) not cut down with a hand implement or machine

ex.t: The sullen murmur of the bees shouldering their way through the long unmown grass, or circling with monotonous insistence round the dusty gilt horns of the straggling woodbine, seemed to make the stillness more oppressive.

senses.d: not in accordance with or determined by nature; contrary to nature
x: the child's unnatural interest in death

senses.d: not normal; not typical or usual or regular or conforming to a norm
speaking or behaving in an artificial way to make an impression

ex.t: The formality, the under-breeding, the meanness, are there; but the portrait is only half alive, and is felt to be even a little unnatural.
It has sometimes, I believe, been urged that his pride is unnatural at first in its expression and later in its yielding, while his falling in love at all is not extremely probable.
An unnatural silence and desertion reigned there.
ex.zh: 那里笼罩着一种不自然的寂静和荒凉。

senses.d: in an unnatural way
x: his other arm lay across his chest, unnaturally, as if placed there deliberately, for a purpose

senses.d: not according to nature; not by natural means
in a manner at variance with what is natural or normal
x: The early Church not unnaturally adopted the position that failure to see the messianic character of his work was really caused by the people's own blindness

ex.t: The hollowness and thinness of his face would have caused them to look large, under his yet dark eyebrows and his confused white hair, though they had been really otherwise; but, they were naturally large, and looked unnaturally so.
ex.zh: 他脸颊的凹陷和瘦削，在他那两道还没变白的眉毛和蓬乱的白发底下，本来就会叫那双眼睛显得大，哪怕它们其实并不大；可它们天生就大，这时便大得不自然了。

ex.t: By supposing such an affection, you make everybody acting unnaturally and wrong, and me most unhappy.
ex.zh: “你这样设想一份情意，就把人人都说成行事反常、无理，也叫我最难堪。

ex.t: My voice seemed unnaturally loud across the garden.
ex.zh: 我的声音隔着花园显得不自然地响。

senses.d: in an unnecessary manner
without any necessity
x: this marathon would exhaust him unnecessarily

ex.t: “Don’t irritate him unnecessarily,” had been Wendy’s instructions in the hold; so Tootles stepped forward politely.
ex.zh: “别无缘无故惹他。”这是温迪在货舱里的嘱咐；所以图图礼貌地走上前。

senses.d: not necessary

ex.t: The warning seemed not unnecessary, so uplifted and aerial was Anne’s expression and attitude as she sprang to her feet, her face irradiated with the flame of her spirit.
ex.zh: 这警告似乎并不多余，因为安妮跳起来的时候，那神情、那姿态，真是又高又飘，脸上像燃着她灵魂的火光。

ex.t: One of the young ladies asked Jo where she got the pretty drab hat she wore to the picnic and stupid Jo, instead of mentioning the place where it was bought two years ago, must needs answer with unnecessary frankness, “Oh, Amy painted it.
ex.zh: 一位小姐问乔，野餐时戴的那顶好看的浅褐色帽子是哪儿买的；傻乔不提两年前买它的铺子，偏要多余地老实回答：“哦，是艾米染的。

ex.t: “You needn’t go and tell them all our little shifts, and expose our poverty in that perfectly unnecessary way.
ex.zh: “你也不必把我们那些穷对付全说给他们，用那种完全没必要的样子把我们的穷揭出来。

senses.d: not necessary

ex.t: Nor are these monitions at all unneeded.
ex.zh: 这些告诫也绝不是多余的。

senses.d: disturb the composure of

ex.t: As he did it he avoided glancing at the sleeper, but not lest pity should unnerve him; merely to avoid spilling.
ex.zh: 做这事时他避着不看睡着的人，倒不是怕怜悯叫他手软，只是怕洒出来。

senses.d: not noticed
x: hoped his departure had passed unnoticed

ex.t: As usual, there was no definite rule against talking to proles and frequenting their pubs, but it was far too unusual an action to pass unnoticed.
ex.zh: 照例，并没有明确的规矩禁止跟无产者说话、进他们的酒馆，可这行为太不寻常，不会不被人注意。

ex.t: “Not invisible but unnoticed, Watson.
ex.zh: “不是看不出来，是没注意到，华生。

senses.d: too numerous to be counted

ex.t: It was invested with the woe of unnumbered generations, this plaint by which Buck was so strangely stirred.
ex.zh: 这哀诉里裹着无数代的苦，巴克被它搅动得那样古怪。

senses.d: not consciously observing
x: looked through him with blank unseeing eyes

ex.t: “Pshaw, my dear fellow, what do the public, the great unobservant public, who could hardly tell a weaver by his tooth or a compositor by his left thumb, care about the finer shades of analysis and deduction!
ex.zh: “呸，老兄，公众——那广大的、毫无观察力的公众，连织工的门牙、排字工左拇指都分辨不出——哪里在乎分析和推理的细微差别！

senses.d: not seen or observed

ex.t: When the revelry of his companions had mounted to its height, this man slipped away unobserved, and I saw no more of him till he became my comrade on the sea.
Before this equatorial coin, Ahab, not unobserved by others, was now pausing.
ex.zh: 亚哈就在这枚赤道的钱币前停下了，别人并非没有看见。

ex.t: Unobserved he rose and glided away; while, awestruck by the aspect of their commander, the seamen clustered together on the forecastle, till Ahab, troubledly pacing the deck, shouted out—“To the braces!
ex.zh: 他没人注意地起身溜走了；水手们被他们指挥官那副样子吓得敬畏，聚在船头楼上，直到亚哈烦躁地在甲板上来回走，喊道——“到转帆索去！

senses.d: free from impediment or obstruction or hindrance

ex.t: If it be made in the unobstructed air, especially if it descend to its mark, the stroke is then simply irresistible.
ex.zh: 倘若这一击是在毫无阻碍的空中打出，尤其若是自上而下落到目标上，那就简直无法抵挡。

ex.t: Having already in various ways put before you his skull, spout-hole, jaw, teeth, tail, forehead, fins, and divers other parts, I shall now simply point out what is most interesting in the general bulk of his unobstructed bones.
ex.zh: 我已经用各种方式向你们展示了他的头骨、喷水孔、下颌、牙齿、尾巴、额头、鳍和别的许多部分；现在我只要指出他那副除去遮挡的骨头在总体积上最有趣的地方。

senses.d: in an unobtrusive manner
x: messengers were moving unobtrusively over the jet-black mountain ranges, bearing confidential tidings from sheikhdom to sheikhdom

ex.t: Sometimes she and Miss Baker talked at once, unobtrusively and with a bantering inconsequence that was never quite chatter, that was as cool as their white dresses and their impersonal eyes in the absence of all desire.
ex.zh: 有时她和贝克小姐会同时开口，不露痕迹，打趣着说些不相干的话，从来算不上闲扯；那话语像她们的白衣裙一样清凉，也像她们在毫无欲念时那双不带个人色彩的眼睛。

senses.d: not held or filled or in use
not seized and controlled
not leased to or occupied by a tenant
x: very little unclaimed and untenanted land

ex.t: As he wandered about in search of food and shelter, he came to a cave, which he entered and found to be unoccupied.
I sought the landlord, and telling him I desired to be accommodated with a room, received for answer that his house was full-not a bed unoccupied.
I sought the landlord, and telling him I desired to be accommodated with a room, received for answer that his house was full—not a bed unoccupied.
ex.zh: 我找到店主人，说想请他给我安排一个房间，得到的回答是：他店里客满了——没有一张空床。

senses.d: not offending
x: an unoffending motorist should not have been stopped

senses.d: not causing anger or annoyance

ex.t: Turning in a temper to the ant-heap he stamped upon it and crushed hundreds of unoffending ants.
ex.zh: 他气冲冲转身朝蚁窝跺下去，踩死了几百只无辜的蚂蚁。

senses.d: not having official authority or sanction
not officially established
x: the early election returns are unofficial

ex.t: “She does plenty of unofficial preaching as it is.
ex.zh: “她现在已经讲了不少非正式的道了。

ex.t: “Of course, in your position of unofficial adviser and helper to everybody who is absolutely puzzled, throughout three continents, you are brought in contact with all that is strange and bizarre.
ex.zh: “当然，你身处这样一个位置：三大洲凡是走投无路的人，都来找你这位非官方的顾问和帮手，你自然接触到种种稀奇古怪的事。

senses.d: without official authorization
x: he had made some money on the side

senses.d: not in an official capacity
x: unofficially, he serves as the treasurer

ex.t: Tranquilly permitting these irregular cursings to evaporate, Stubb then in a plain, business-like, but still half humorous manner, cursed Pip officially; and that done, unofficially gave him much wholesome advice.
ex.zh: 斯塔布安然让这些不按规矩的骂声散掉，然后才用平实的、公事公办的、却还带几分诙谐的口气，正式骂了皮普一顿；骂完，又以非正式的身份给了他许多有益的劝告。

senses.d: not yet opened or unsealed

ex.t: The House approached Mr. Lorry, and laying a soiled and unopened letter before him, asked if he had yet discovered any traces of the person to whom it was addressed?
ex.zh: 银行的人走到洛里先生跟前，把一封弄脏了、没有拆开的信放到他面前，问他有没有查到收信人的踪迹？

ex.t: As I waited, I lifted the unopened newspaper from the table and glanced my eye over it.
ex.zh: 等候的时候，我拿起桌上那份还没打开的报纸，扫了一眼。

ex.t: After a moment Tom got up and began wrapping the unopened bottle of whisky in the towel.
ex.zh: 过了一会儿，汤姆起身，开始把那瓶没开的威士忌用毛巾裹起来。

senses.d: not having opposition or an opponent

ex.t: In the years following the Revolution it was able to step into this commanding position almost unopposed, because the whole process was represented as an act of collectivization.
ex.zh: 革命后的那些年里，它几乎未遇抵抗就取得了这个支配地位，因为整个过程被说成是一次集体化行动。

senses.d: independent in behavior or thought
x: she led a somewhat irregular private life

senses.d: breaking with convention or tradition

ex.t: It had been on the tip of his tongue to say 'Except the proles,' but he checked himself, not feeling fully certain that this remark was not in some way unorthodox.
ex.zh: “除了无产者”这话已经到了舌尖，可他忍住了，因为他不能完全确定这话在某种方式上不算不正统。

ex.t: You could not say that he was unorthodox.
ex.zh: 你不能说他不正统。

ex.t: It would even have seemed slightly unorthodox, a dangerous eccentricity, like talking to oneself.
ex.zh: 那甚至显得有点不正统，是一种危险的怪癖，像自言自语。

senses.d: any opinions or doctrines at variance with the official or orthodox position
a belief that rejects the orthodox tenets of a religion
the quality of being unorthodox

ex.t: It was always the women, and above all the young ones, who were the most bigoted adherents of the Party, the swallowers of slogans, the amateur spies and nosers-out of unorthodoxy.
ex.zh: 最死心塌地拥护党的总是女人，尤其是年轻的女人：她们吞得下口号，是业余的密探，专爱嗅出不正当的东西。

ex.t: And again, perhaps it was not even unorthodoxy that was written in his face, but simply intelligence.
ex.zh: 再说，也许写在他脸上的并不是不正统，而只是聪明。

ex.t: Another year, two years, and they would be watching her night and day for symptoms of unorthodoxy.
ex.zh: 再过一年、两年，他们就会日夜监视她，找她不正统的迹象。

senses.d: not ostentatious
exhibiting restrained good taste
x: the room is pleasant and understated

ex.t: But look at the godly, honest, unostentatious, hospitable, sociable, free-and-easy whaler!
ex.zh: 可你瞧瞧那敬神、老实、不摆架子、好客、爱交游、随随便便的捕鲸船吧！

senses.d: remove from its packing

ex.t: It has become known that we have never had occasion to unpack the money, and that it is still lying in our cellar.
ex.zh: 后来外界知道我们一直没机会拆开这笔钱，它还躺在我们地窖里。

ex.t: The day passed in helping Mother to unpack and arrange things.
ex.zh: 这一天就帮着妈妈开箱、摆东西，过去了。

senses.d: remove from its packing

ex.t: That evening Miss Barry gave Diana a silver bangle bracelet and told the senior members of the household that she had unpacked her valise.
ex.zh: 那天晚上，巴里小姐送给黛安娜一只银手镯，又告诉家里的大人们，她把行李箱又打开了。

ex.t: We rested, unpacked, and shopped a little between the showers.
ex.zh: 我们歇了歇，打开行李，趁雨停的工夫买了点东西。

ex.t: They threaded their way across the crowded room and unpacked their trays on to the metal-topped table, on one corner of which someone had left a pool of stew, a filthy liquid mess that had the appearance of vomit.
ex.zh: 他们穿过拥挤的屋子，把托盘里的东西摊在一张金属面的桌上；桌子一角有人留下一摊炖菜，一汪脏乎乎的液体，看着像呕吐物。

senses.d: remove from its packing

ex.t: “Oh, yes,” said Mother, “only it'll mean unpacking one of those big cases that we put in the cellar.
ex.zh: “哦，吃得上的，”妈妈说，“只不过得把放在地窖里的大箱子打开一个。

senses.d: not having makeup on
not having a coat of paint or badly in need of a fresh coat

ex.t: For all these reasons, then, any way you may look at it, you must needs conclude that the great Leviathan is that one creature in the world which must remain unpainted to the last.
ex.zh: 因此，由于这一切理由，不管你从哪个角度看，你都不能不得出结论：伟大的巨鲸是世上唯一一种注定到末了也画不成的生物。

senses.d: not pleasant or acceptable to the taste or mind

ex.t: "When we come to you," said they to the Sea, "we are sweet and drinkable: but when once we have mingled with you, our waters become as briny and unpalatable as your own."
ex.zh: “我们流到你这里来的时候，”它们对海说，“又甜又能喝：可一旦跟你混在一处，我们的水就变得跟你的一样咸苦难饮。”

senses.d: radically distinctive and without equal
x: he is alone in the field of microbiology
this theory is altogether alone in its penetration of the problem

ex.t: Yesterday the stranger said to me, "You may easily perceive, Captain Walton, that I have suffered great and unparalleled misfortunes.
He is so gentle, yet so wise; his mind is so cultivated, and when he speaks, although his words are culled with the choicest art, yet they flow with rapidity and unparalleled eloquence.
Yesterday the stranger said to me, “You may easily perceive, Captain Walton, that I have suffered great and unparalleled misfortunes.
ex.zh: 昨天，那陌生人对我说：“沃尔顿船长，你很容易看出，我遭受过巨大而无与伦比的不幸。

senses.d: not admitting of pardon

ex.t: An ethical sympathy in an artist is an unpardonable mannerism of style.
If John had not forgotten all about the jelly, it really would have been unpardonable in him to choose that day, of all the days in the year, to bring a friend home to dinner unexpectedly.
That was unpardonable, and Amy took no more notice of him for a long while, except a word now and then when she came to her chaperon between the dances for a necessary pin or a moment’s rest.
ex.zh: 这是不可饶恕的；此后好一阵艾米都不理他，只在两支舞之间回到女伴身边要一枚别针、或者歇一口气时，才丢给他一句话。

senses.d: not perceived or commented on

ex.t: I saw him on the point of repeating his blow, when, overcome by pain and anguish, I quitted the cottage, and in the general tumult escaped unperceived to my hovel.”
ex.zh: 我看见他正要再打一下，这时我被痛苦和悲愤压倒，离开了农舍，在那一场混乱中没人看见地逃回了我的破屋。”

senses.d: a person regarded as nonexistent and having no rights; a person whose existence is systematically ignored (especially for ideological or political reasons)
x: the former senator is treated as a nonperson by this administration
George Orwell predicted that political dissidents would be treated as unpersons

ex.t: Withers, however, was already an UNPERSON.
ex.zh: 可威瑟斯已经是个非人了。

ex.t: But Syme was not only dead, he was abolished, an unperson.
ex.zh: 可赛姆不但死了，还被废除了，是个非人。

senses.d: a person regarded as nonexistent and having no rights; a person whose existence is systematically ignored (especially for ideological or political reasons)
x: the former senator is treated as a nonperson by this administration
George Orwell predicted that political dissidents would be treated as unpersons

ex.t: The only real clue lay in the words 'refs unpersons', which indicated that Withers was already dead.
ex.zh: 唯一真正的线索是“提及非人”这几个字，这说明威瑟斯已经死了。

senses.d: not pictured

ex.t: Some love might come across his life, and purify him, and shield him from those sins that seemed to be already stirring in spirit and in flesh—those curious unpictured sins whose very mystery lent them their subtlety and their charm.
ex.zh: 也许会有某种爱闯进他的生命，净化他，护住他，不叫那些仿佛已在精神与肉体中躁动的罪近身——那些奇异的、未曾入画的罪，正因神秘才显得幽微迷人。

senses.d: remove the pins from; unfasten the pins of

ex.t: “I’ll do my best to gratify you, Sir,” was Laurie’s unusually dutiful reply, as he carefully unpinned the posy Jo had put in his buttonhole.
ex.zh: “先生，我尽力叫您称心，”劳里答得比平日孝顺，一面把乔插在他纽孔里的那朵小花小心摘下。

senses.d: without mercy or pity

ex.t: When close to the whale, in the very death-lock of the fight, he handled his unpitying lance coolly and off-handedly, as a whistling tinker his hammer.
ex.zh: 贴近鲸的时候，在那场厮杀拼到死扣的当口，他使起他那无情的长矛来，仍旧冷静随便，像个一边吹着口哨一边敲打的补锅匠使他的锤子。

senses.d: offensive or disagreeable; causing discomfort or unhappiness

ex.t: And at first, this sort of thing is unpleasant enough.
He sank daily, and my mother and I had all the inn upon our hands, and were kept busy enough without paying much regard to our unpleasant guest.
A Rich Man took up his residence next door to a Tanner, and found the smell of the tan-yard so extremely unpleasant that he told him he must go.

senses.d: the feeling caused by disagreeable stimuli; one pole of a continuum of states of feeling
the quality of giving displeasure
x: the recent unpleasantness of the weather

ex.t: There were the same people, or at least the same sort of people, the same profusion of champagne, the same many-coloured, many-keyed commotion, but I felt an unpleasantness in the air, a pervading harshness that hadn't been there before.
There will probably be some small unpleasantness.
ex.zh: 多半会有一点小小的不愉快。

ex.t: "I'm just going to wait here and see if he tries to bother her about that unpleasantness this afternoon.
ex.zh: “我就在这儿等着，看他会不会拿今天下午那件不愉快的事去烦她。

senses.d: unpleasant or disagreeable to the senses

ex.t: It was curious and not unpleasing, how Peleg and Bildad were affected at this juncture, especially Captain Bildad.
ex.zh: 到了这个关头，佩莱格和比勒达受了怎样的触动，尤其是比勒达船长，说来奇怪，却也不叫人难受。

senses.d: free from admixture with noxious elements; clean

ex.t: What then can it possibly be, but sperm oil in its unmanufactured, unpolluted state, the sweetest of all oils?
ex.zh: 那么它还可能是什么，不就是未经加工、未受污染的抹香鲸油么？那是所有油中最甜的。

senses.d: regarded with disfavor or lacking general approval

ex.t: I confess that we were so unpopular with the outrageous mob, that I only got away from England at the risk of being ducked to death, and that Cly was so ferreted up and down, that he never would have got away at all but for that sham.
ex.zh: 我承认，我们那时被那帮无法无天的暴民恨得那么厉害，我逃出英格兰时险些被按进水里淹死；克莱被搜得那么紧，要不是那场假戏，他根本逃不掉。

senses.d: the quality of lacking general approval or acceptance

ex.t: His unpopularity with the blackguard multitude at the moment prevented my following his remains, but I helped to lay him in his coffin.”
ex.zh: 当时那帮流氓民众恨他，我没能送葬，可我是帮着把他放进棺材的。”

senses.d: not having had extensive practice

ex.t: He was always the saddest of the group, and even to my unpractised senses, he appeared to have suffered more deeply than his friends.
ex.zh: 他始终是这一群里最忧愁的，甚至凭我这不曾练过的感觉也看得出，他受的苦比他的同伴更深。

senses.d: having no precedent; novel
x: an unprecedented expansion in population and industry

ex.t: All here is so unprecedented, so changed, so sudden and unfair, that I am absolutely lost.
ex.zh: 这里一切都那么没有先例，那么变了样，那么突然、那么不公，我简直完全没了主意。

ex.t: Though such a movement on the part of the whale struck under such circumstances, is in no wise unprecedented; and indeed is almost always more or less anticipated; yet does it present one of the more perilous vicissitudes of the fishery.
ex.zh: 在这种情形下被刺中的鲸这样行动，绝非没有先例；其实几乎总是多少预料得到的；可这仍是捕鲸业中较危险的变故之一。

ex.t: Here be it said, that this pertinacious pursuit of one particular whale, continued through day into night, and through night into day, is a thing by no means unprecedented in the South sea fishery.
ex.zh: 这里要说一句：这样死盯住一条特定的鲸，从白天追到夜里，又从夜里追到白天，在南太平洋的捕鲸业里绝不是没有先例的。

senses.d: in an unprecedented manner

ex.t: But a sudden stop was put to further discoveries, by the ship’s being unprecedentedly dragged over sideways to the sea, owing to the body’s immensely increasing tendency to sink.
ex.zh: 可进一步的发现忽然被打断了：由于那尸体下沉的势头大增，船竟前所未有地被横着拽向海面。

senses.d: free from undue bias or preconceived opinions
x: an unprejudiced appraisal of the pros and cons
the impartial eye of a scientist

ex.t: To be friendless is indeed to be unfortunate, but the hearts of men, when unprejudiced by any obvious self-interest, are full of brotherly love and charity.
ex.zh: 没有朋友确实是不幸，可人心若不被任何明显的私利所偏，是充满手足之爱和仁慈的。

ex.t: Suddenly, as I gazed on him, an idea seized me that this little creature was unprejudiced and had lived too short a time to have imbibed a horror of deformity.
ex.zh: 我盯着他看，忽然一个念头抓住我：这小东西是没有偏见的，他活得太短，还没染上对丑的恐惧。

ex.t: Only the most unprejudiced of men like Stubb, nowadays partake of cooked whales; but the Esquimaux are not so fastidious.
ex.zh: 如今只有像斯塔布这样最没有成见的人才吃煮熟的鲸；可爱斯基摩人并不这样讲究。

senses.d: without preparation; not prepared for- R.E.Danielson

ex.t: Unprepared as he was for the large pill he had to swallow, he got it down.
ex.zh: 这颗大药丸他虽没准备好，还是咽下去了。

ex.t: Though he said the last words, with a slip into his usual manner, there was a true feeling and respect both in his tone and in his touch, that Mr. Lorry, who had never seen the better side of him, was wholly unprepared for.
ex.zh: 虽然他说最后几句时又滑回平常那副样子，可他的语气和举动里有一种真切的感情和敬意，是洛里先生从没见过的他较好的一面，完全没料到。

ex.t: This was a stroke of civility for which she was quite unprepared; and she could hardly suppress a smile at his being now seeking the acquaintance of some of those very people, against whom his pride had revolted, in his offer to herself.
ex.zh: 这份客气来得太突然，她全没防备；她几乎忍不住要笑：他当初向她求婚时，他的傲气还极力反对的正是这些人，如今他倒来结交他们了。

senses.d: not ostentatious

ex.t: He must know that she was as amiable and unpretending as we have found her.”
ex.zh: 他一定知道她跟我们见到的一样可亲、一样不摆架子。”

senses.d: lacking principles or moral scruples- A.E.Stevenson
having little or no integrity

ex.t: Thou art as unprincipled as the gods, and as much of a jack-of-all-trades.”
ex.zh: 你跟诸神一样没有原则，也一样是个什么都会的万金油。”

senses.d: not capable of being obtained
x: a rare work, today almost inaccessible
timber is virtually unobtainable in the islands

ex.t: But it needed desperate courage to kill yourself in a world where firearms, or any quick and certain poison, were completely unprocurable.
ex.zh: 可在一个火器、或任何迅速可靠的毒药都完全弄不到的世界里，自杀需要拼死的勇气。

senses.d: not characteristic of or befitting a profession or one engaged in a profession
x: described in unprofessional language so that high school students could understand it

ex.t: But quitting all these unprofessional attempts, let us glance at those pictures of leviathan purporting to be sober, scientific delineations, by those who know.
ex.zh: 不过，撇开所有这些外行的尝试，让我们来看看那些自称是内行人所作的严谨科学描绘的巨鲸图。

senses.d: producing little or no profit or gain
x: deposits abandoned by mining companies as unprofitable

ex.t: A very, very brief time, and you will dismiss the recollection of it, gladly, as an unprofitable dream, from which it happened well that you awoke.
ex.zh: 可是用不了多久，很短很短的时间，你就会把这段回忆当作一场无益的梦，高高兴兴地丢开；亏得你醒了过来。

ex.t: To Anne in particular things seemed fearfully flat, stale, and unprofitable after the goblet of excitement she had been sipping for weeks.
ex.zh: 尤其是安妮，她连喝了好几个星期那杯兴奋的酒，如今觉得样样都平淡得可怕、陈旧、没意思。

ex.t: He was in one of his moods, for the day had been both unprofitable and unsatisfactory, and he was wishing he could live it over again.
ex.zh: 他正闹着脾气，因为这一天既没长进，又不如意，他恨不得能重过一遍。

senses.d: unlikely to bring about favorable results or enjoyment
x: music for unpromising combinations of instruments

ex.t: Sydney Carton, idlest and most unpromising of men, was Stryver’s great ally.
ex.zh: 西德尼·卡顿，最懒散、最没出息的人，却是斯特赖弗的大帮手。

senses.d: not propitious

ex.t: At this unpropitious moment her name was called.
ex.zh: 就在这个不巧的时候，叫到了她的名字。

senses.d: lacking protection or defense

ex.t: The captain's order to mount at once and ride for Doctor Livesey would have left my mother alone and unprotected, which was not to be thought of.
This is not a good city, at this time, for you to be out in, unprotected; and as your escort knows Mr. Barsad, I will invite him to Mr. Lorry’s with us.
ex.zh: 这时候这城里不安全，你不便无人护送在外走；既然你的护送人认得巴萨德先生，我就请他跟我们一道去洛里先生那儿。

ex.t: I thought also of my father and surviving brother; should I by my base desertion leave them exposed and unprotected to the malice of the fiend whom I had let loose among them?
ex.zh: 我也想到父亲和活着的弟弟；我若这样卑劣地撇下他们，岂不是叫他们暴露在我放到他们中间的那个魔鬼的恶意之下，无人保护？

senses.d: not punctual; after the appointed time

ex.t: After a little while Mr. Gatz opened the door and came out, his mouth ajar, his face flushed slightly, his eyes leaking isolated and unpunctual tears.
ex.zh: 过了一会儿，盖茨先生开门出来，嘴微微张着，脸上有些泛红，眼里漏出一滴一滴不合时宜的泪。

senses.d: not punished
x: would he forget the crime and let it go unpunished?

ex.t: Promiscuity went unpunished, divorce was permitted.
ex.zh: 淫乱不受惩罚，离婚是允许的。

ex.t: They could not let such an outburst go unpunished.
ex.zh: 他们不会让这样一次发作不受惩罚。

ex.t: The heretical thought would be unpunished, unrepented, out of their reach for ever.
ex.zh: 那异端的念头将不受惩罚，不被悔改，永远在他们够不着的地方。

senses.d: not limited or restricted
not meeting the proper standards and requirements and training
legally not qualified or sufficient
x: a wife is usually considered unqualified to testify against her husband

senses.d: having no right or entitlement
x: a distinction to which he was unentitled

ex.t: This appearance excited our unqualified wonder.

These bitter accusations might have been suppressed, had I, with greater policy, concealed my struggles, and flattered you into the belief of my being impelled by unqualified, unalloyed inclination; by reason, by reflection, by everything.
ex.zh: 我若手段高明些，把心里的挣扎藏起来，只哄得你相信我是被纯粹无杂的好感所驱——被理智、被思量、被一切所驱——这些尖刻的责备本来也许可以不说。

senses.d: impossible to quench

ex.t: The Unquenchables had done their best to be worthy of the name, for like elves they had worked by night and conjured up a comical surprise.
ex.zh: 那两个“扑不灭的”也尽力不辜负这名号，因为他们像小精灵一样夜里干活，变出一个滑稽的惊喜。

senses.d: incapable of being questioned
not counterfeit or copied
not open to question
x: an unquestionable (or unequivocal) loss of prestige

ex.t: Did you get it from an unquestionable source?
ex.zh: 你是从一个靠得住的来源得来的么？

ex.t: His three whales are as good whales as were ever published in Wapping, at any rate; and his stump as unquestionable a stump as any you will find in the western clearings.
ex.zh: 无论如何，他那三头鲸跟沃平印行过的任何好鲸一样好；他那条断腿跟你在西部垦荒地里能找到的任何断腿一样确凿无疑。

ex.t: She wanted her life shaped now, immediately-and the decision must be made by some force-of love, of money, of unquestionable practicality-that was close at hand.
ex.zh: 她要自己的生活现在就成形，立刻成形——而这个决定必须由某种近在手边的力量来做，爱情也好，金钱也好，不容置疑的实利也好。

senses.d: without question
x: Fred Winter is unquestionably the jockey to follow
they hired unimpeachably first-rate faculty members

senses.d: without question and beyond doubt
x: she told him off in spades

ex.t: At first I thought it quite hopeless, but I have unquestionably seen, for a single moment, the face that I once knew so well.
ex.zh: 起初我以为完全没指望了，可我确确实实看见了，就在那一瞬，那张我从前那样熟悉的脸。

ex.t: To return to business:--Is it not remarkable that Doctor Manette, unquestionably innocent of any crime as we are all well assured he is, should never touch upon that question?
ex.zh: 回到正事上——马内特医生确凿无罪，这一点我们大家都深信不疑，可他竟从不触及那个问题，这岂不奇怪？

ex.t: She and her father would unquestionably be guilty of this crime, and this woman (the inveteracy of whose pursuit cannot be described) would wait to add that strength to her case, and make herself doubly sure.
ex.zh: 她和她父亲无疑会犯这罪，而这女人（她那追逐的执拗没法形容）会等着，拿这个给她的案子添一份力，叫自己加倍有把握。

senses.d: not inclined to ask questions
being without doubt or reserve

ex.t: He was a fattish but active man of paralysing stupidity, a mass of imbecile enthusiasms--one of those completely unquestioning, devoted drudges on whom, more even than on the Thought Police, the stability of the Party depended.
ex.zh: 他是个微胖而好动的人，蠢得叫人发僵，一肚子痴傻的热忱——正是那种毫无质疑、忠心耿耿的苦力，党的稳定所依靠的，与其说是思想警察，不如说是这种人。

senses.d: characterized by unrest or disorder
x: following the assassination of Martin Luter King ours was an unquiet nation

senses.d: causing or fraught with or showing anxiety
x: spent an anxious night waiting for the test results

ex.t: Up in the garret, where Jo’s unquiet wanderings ended stood four little wooden chests in a row, each marked with its owners name, and each filled with relics of the childhood and girlhood ended now for all.
ex.zh: 乔那不安的游荡止于阁楼；那儿一排立着四只小木箱，各标着主人的名字，各装着如今对谁都算完了的童年和少女时代的遗物。

ex.t: When I looked once more for Gatsby he had vanished, and I was alone again in the unquiet darkness.
ex.zh: 等我再看盖茨比时，他已经不见了，我又独自一人，置身于那不安的黑暗里。

senses.d: become or cause to become undone by separating the fibers or threads of
disentangle
become undone

ex.t: Their pronunciation was quick, and the words they uttered, not having any apparent connection with visible objects, I was unable to discover any clue by which I could unravel the mystery of their reference.
ex.zh: 他们说得很快，而他们发出的词跟可见的东西又没有明显的联系，我找不出任何线索去解开它们所指何物的谜。

ex.t: When the swallows heard this, they all came down on to the Doctor’s ship; and they told him to unravel some pieces of long rope and make them into a lot of thin strings as quickly as he could.
ex.zh: 燕子们听了，一齐落到医生的船上；它们叫他赶紧把几根长绳拆开，搓成许多细绳子，越快越好。

senses.d: become or cause to become undone by separating the fibers or threads of
disentangle
become undone

ex.t: This morning he was removed to a cell, and I, after going through all the police formalities, have hurried round to you to implore you to use your skill in unravelling the matter.
ex.zh: 今天早上他被押进牢房，我办完一切警察手续，就赶紧跑来找你，求你施展本领把这件事弄清楚。

senses.d: not informed through reading- V.L.Parrington
x: he seems to have been wholly unread in political theory

ex.t: Or, to the unread, unsophisticated Protestant of the Middle American States, why does the passing mention of a White Friar or a White Nun, evoke such an eyeless statue in the soul?
ex.zh: 或者，对中部美洲各州那些没读过什么书、质朴的新教徒来说，为什么顺口一提白衣修士或白衣修女，就在灵魂里唤出那样一尊没有眼睛的雕像？

senses.d: lacking in reality or substance or genuineness; not corresponding to acknowledged facts or criteria
not actually such; being or seeming fanciful or imaginary
x: this conversation is getting more and more unreal
the fantastically unreal world of government bureaucracy

senses.d: contrived by art rather than nature
lacking material form or substance; unreal
x: an insubstantial mirage on the horizon

ex.t: Among the many wild changes observable on familiar things which made this wild ride unreal, not the least was the seeming rarity of sleep.
ex.zh: 在这趟狂乱的行程所见的熟悉事物那许多离奇变化中，最显眼的一桩就是睡眠似乎变得稀罕。

ex.t: But the crowning unreality of his long unreal ride, was, their all at once rising to receive him, with every refinement of manner known to the time, and with all the engaging graces and courtesies of life.
ex.zh: 可是这趟漫长而不真实的行程最不真实的一桩，是他们忽然一齐起身迎接他，带着当时所知的一切优雅风度，带着生活中一切动人的温文礼数。

ex.t: Surely, the long unreal ride some progress of disease that had brought him to these gloomy shades!
ex.zh: 真的，那漫长而不真实的行程，是一场把他带到这些阴惨幽影里来的病的发展！

senses.d: the quality possessed by something that is unreal
the state of being insubstantial or imaginary; not existing objectively or in fact

ex.t: The leprosy of unreality disfigured every human creature in attendance upon Monseigneur.
ex.zh: 不真实的麻风把侍候爵爷的每一个活人都弄得丑陋。

ex.t: But the crowning unreality of his long unreal ride, was, their all at once rising to receive him, with every refinement of manner known to the time, and with all the engaging graces and courtesies of life.
ex.zh: 可是这趟漫长而不真实的行程最不真实的一桩，是他们忽然一齐起身迎接他，带着当时所知的一切优雅风度，带着生活中一切动人的温文礼数。

ex.t: For a while these reveries provided an outlet for his imagination; they were a satisfactory hint of the unreality of reality, a promise that the rock of the world was founded securely on a fairy's wing.
ex.zh: 有一阵子，这些遐想给他的想象提供了出口；它们令人满意地暗示现实并不真实，许诺这世界的磐石稳稳地奠在一只仙女的翅膀上。

senses.d: not reasonable; not showing good judgment
beyond normal limits

ex.t: “Commence,” was Monsieur Defarge’s not unreasonable reply, “at the commencement.”
ex.zh: “从头说起。”德法热先生这样回答，倒也不算没道理。

ex.t: People are so unreasonable!
ex.zh: 人就是这么不讲理！

ex.t: “Of all the unreasonable women I ever saw she’s the worst.
ex.zh: “我见过的不可理喻的女人里，她是最厉害的一个。

senses.d: not in a reasonable or intelligent manner
x: she reacted unreasonably when she learned she had failed

senses.d: to a degree that exceeds the bounds or reason or moderation

ex.t: The certainty of meeting him had not been checked by any of those recollections that might not unreasonably have alarmed her.
ex.zh: 她原以为一定能见到他，而那些本可以不失为合理地叫她警觉的回想，都没能动摇这份确信。

senses.d: not based on reason or evidence

ex.t: But in each event—in the living act, the undoubted deed—there, some unknown but still reasoning thing puts forth the mouldings of its features from behind the unreasoning mask.
ex.zh: 可在每一件事里——在那活生生的一举里，在那无可置疑的一行里——总有一个未知的、却仍在推理的东西，从那张无理性的面具后头，探出它面目的轮廓来。

ex.t: Mr. Rucastle told me in private that the reason why she had left them was that she had an unreasoning aversion to her stepmother.
ex.zh: 鲁卡斯尔先生私下告诉我，她离开他们的原因，是她对继母有一种没来由的厌恶。

ex.t: A mad, unreasoning terror rose up in me at the sight, Mr. Holmes.
ex.zh: 福尔摩斯先生，一见这情景，一种疯狂而无理的恐惧从我心中升起。

senses.d: actually being performed at the time of hearing or viewing
x: brought to you live from Lincoln Center

ex.t: Where unrecorded names and navies rust, and untold hopes and anchors rot; where in her murderous hold this frigate earth is ballasted with bones of millions of the drowned; there, in that awful water-land, there was thy most familiar home.
ex.zh: 在那里，无名的姓名和无名的舰队一同锈蚀，无从说起的希望和铁锚一同腐烂；在那里，这艘叫作地球的护卫舰用它那杀人的底舱，装着千百万溺死者的尸骨压舱；就在那里，在那片可怖的水中之国，曾有你最熟稔的家。

ex.t: Look your last, now, on these venerable hooded heads, while they yet lie together; for one will soon sink, unrecorded, in the sea; the other will not be very long in following.
ex.zh: 趁这两颗可敬的、戴着头巾的头还并放着，你们且看上最后一眼；因为不久其中一个就要无声无息地沉入海里；另一个也过不了多久就要跟去。

senses.d: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
not reformed morally or spiritually
unrepentant and incapable of being reformed

ex.t: As for his being in love, Elizabeth has given as just an exposition of the causes of that phenomenon as Darcy has of the conditions of his unregenerate state, only she has of course not counted in what was due to her own personal charm.
Do you think it’s because I’m really bad and unregenerate?”
ex.zh: 您觉得是因为我天生就坏，没得救吗？”

senses.d: nor relaxed- U.B.Phillips
x: his life was drawing to a close in baffled zeal and unrelaxed strain

ex.t: One secret which I alone possessed was the hope to which I had dedicated myself; and the moon gazed on my midnight labours, while, with unrelaxed and breathless eagerness, I pursued nature to her hiding-places.
ex.zh: 我只独自占着一个秘密，那就是我为之献身的这份希望；月亮照着我午夜的劳作，我以毫不松缓、屏息般的急切，把自然一直追进她的藏身之处。

senses.d: not to be placated or appeased or moved by entreaty
punishingly harsh
never-ceasing
x: the relentless beat of the drums

ex.t: Gnawed within and scorched without, with the infixed, unrelenting fangs of some incurable idea; such an one, could he be found, would seem the very man to dart his iron and lift his lance against the most appalling of all brutes.
ex.zh: 内里被啃噬，外头被烧灼，嵌着某种不治之念的那副不屈的牙；这样的人，若能找得到，似乎正该是把铁标掷出去、把长矛举向一切畜生中最可怖者的那个人。

senses.d: not lessened or diminished

ex.t: The sky looks lacquered; clouds there are none; the horizon floats; and this nakedness of unrelieved radiance is as the insufferable splendors of God’s throne.
ex.zh: 天空看去像漆过一般；没有一片云；地平线浮着；这种毫无遮拦、毫无调剂的强光，就像上帝宝座那叫人受不了的辉煌。

senses.d: not perceived or commented on

ex.t: My plan was to go back the road he had come, for the watchers, having seen it before, would probably let it pass unremarked, and Marmie’s figure was in no way like mine.
ex.zh: 我打算顺他来的路回去：那些眼线先前见过这车，多半会放它过去不起疑；而马米的身形一点也不像我。

senses.d: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

ex.t: These thoughts supported my spirits, while I pursued my undertaking with unremitting ardour.
ex.zh: 就是这些念头撑着我，我以毫不松懈的热忱推进我的事业。

ex.t: But I was in reality very ill, and surely nothing but the unbounded and unremitting attentions of my friend could have restored me to life.
ex.zh: 可我实际上病得很重，若不是我朋友那无边的、不间断的照料，绝没有别的什么能把我救活。

senses.d: unserviceable because necessary repairs have not been made

ex.t: There was little difficulty in entering the grounds, for unrepaired breaches gaped in the old park wall.
ex.zh: 进园子不难，因为老园墙上有些豁口一直没修。

senses.d: not penitent or remorseful
stubbornly persistent in wrongdoing

ex.t: Because the Inquisition killed its enemies in the open, and killed them while they were still unrepentant: in fact, it killed them because they were unrepentant.
ex.zh: “因为宗教裁判所公开杀死敌人，而且是在他们仍不悔悟的时候杀死：事实上，正因为他们不悔悟才杀。”

senses.d: not returned in kind

ex.t: Unlike some sufferers, he never spoke of his unrequited passion, and would allow no one, not even Mrs. March, to attempt consolation or offer sympathy.
ex.zh: 跟有些受苦的人不同，他从不说自己那份没人回应的热情，也不许任何人——就连马奇太太——来劝慰或表示同情。

senses.d: not reserved
not cautious or reticent

ex.t: Bingley had soon made himself acquainted with all the principal people in the room: he was lively and unreserved, danced every dance, was angry that the ball closed so early, and talked of giving one himself at Netherfield.
I had no difficulty in deducing from your unreserved conversation, and the rumour openly going about among your admirers, the nature of your calling.
ex.zh: 我从你那毫无顾忌的谈话，以及你的仰慕者中间公开流传的风声，不难推断出你干的是哪一行。

ex.t: Mr. Bingley had soon made himself acquainted with all the principal people in the room: he was lively and unreserved, danced every dance, was angry that the ball closed so early, and talked of giving one himself at Netherfield.
ex.zh: 宾利先生很快就跟厅里所有主要人物都结识了：他活泼坦率，每支舞都跳，还嫌舞会散得太早，说要自己在尼日斐办一场。

senses.d: without reservation
x: I can unreservedly recommend this restaurant!

ex.t: Cly (who I will unreservedly admit, at this distance of time, was a partner of mine) has been dead several years.
ex.zh: 克莱（隔了这么些年，我干脆承认，他当年是我的合伙人）已经死了好几年了。

senses.d: offering no resistance

ex.t: He had pulled her down on to the ground, she was utterly unresisting, he could do what he liked with her.
ex.zh: 他把她拉到地上，她完全不抗拒，他爱怎样就怎样。

ex.zh: 他扑到巴克身上，两次把牙咬进这不还手的仇敌身上，把肉撕到骨头。

ex.t:
Perhaps even as we speak he's lying with his head on the metals, an unresisting prey to any passing express--”

“Oh, don't try to talk like a book,” cried Bobbie, bolting what was left of her sandwich; “come on.
ex.zh:
说不定就在咱们说话这会儿，他头枕着铁轨躺着，随便哪列快车过来都能把他碾了——”

“哦，别学书里说话了，”博比喊，把剩下的三明治一口吞下，“走吧。

senses.d: a feeling of restless agitation

ex.zh: 它叫他满心不安，生出些古怪的欲望。

ex.zh: 他扭伤的肩膀没人治、也没歇，越发坏下去，最后哈尔用那把大号柯尔特左轮把他打死了。

senses.d: a state of agitation or turbulent change or development
x: the political ferment produced new leadership

senses.d: a feeling of restless agitation

ex.t: Oh, Pip! thy wretched laugh, thy idle but unresting eye; all thy strange mummeries not unmeaningly blended with the black tragedy of the melancholy ship, and mocked it!
ex.zh: 啊，皮普！你那可怜的笑，你那闲散却不得安歇的眼睛；你那些古怪的哑剧，都不是毫无意义地混进这条忧郁的船的黑悲剧里，而且在嘲弄它！

senses.d: not subject to restraint
marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
x: a crowd of delirious baseball fans

ex.t: Tears, unrestrained, fell from my brother’s eyes; a sense of mortal agony crept over my frame.
ex.zh: 泪从我弟弟眼里不受拘束地落下来；一种死的剧痛爬过我的全身。

ex.t: Mr. Darcy was eyeing him with unrestrained wonder; and when at last Mr. Collins allowed him to speak, replied with an air of distant civility.
ex.zh: 达西先生毫不掩饰地惊讶地打量他；等柯林斯先生终于让他开口，他便带着一种疏远的客气回答。

ex.t: I ejaculated an unrestrained "Huh!" and he must have heard me, for he went on nervously: "What I called up about was a pair of shoes I left there.
ex.zh: 我不由自主地“哼！”了一声，他一定听见了，因为他紧张地继续说：“我打电话是为了我落在那儿的一双鞋。

senses.d: not made known

ex.zh: 他曾以种种不便明说的身份接触过这类人，可中间总隔着一道看不见的铁丝网。

ex.zh: 不久，船员们正等着大船过来时，那尸体就显出要沉下去的迹象，而它所有的宝贝还没被取走。

ex.zh: 她驶近时，所有的眼睛都盯住她那两根宽大的横梁，叫做剪架；在有些捕鲸船上，那东西在八九尺高处横过后甲板；用来载备用的、未装备的或者残破的艇。

senses.d: not righteous

ex.zh: 斯塔布随即飞快划向那具浮尸，向裴廓德号喊话说明自己的打算，立刻动手收割他那不正当的机巧所结的果子。

senses.d: not fully developed or mature; not ripe
not fully prepared

ex.t: A green, an unripe time, a time of shallow moods, and sickly thoughts.
ex.zh: 一段青涩未熟的时光，一段心境浅薄、念头病态的时光。

senses.d: eminent beyond or above comparison

ex.zh: 克利福德爵士打算收两便士，让人窥一眼脊椎里那条“回音廊”；收三便士，让人听一听他小脑空腔里的回声；收六便士，让人从他额头上看那无可比拟的景致。

senses.d: reverse the winding or twisting of

ex.zh: 他身旁的桌上摊开着一张那种先前说起过的潮汐与洋流图。

ex.zh: 然后他把已经从桌子右边气压管里掉出来的四个小纸卷展开，夹在一起。

ex.t: Winston examined the four slips of paper which he had unrolled.
ex.zh: 温斯顿查看他展开的那四张纸条。

senses.d: reverse the winding or twisting of
unroll, unfold, or spread out or be unrolled, unfolded, or spread out from a furled state

ex.zh: 它们留下一道又大又宽的尾迹，仿佛在海上不停地展开一大卷宽阔的羊皮纸。

senses.d: neither expressive of nor exciting sexual love or romance

ex.zh: 再说安妮这名字多不浪漫呀。”

ex.t: “Unromantic fiddlesticks!” said the unsympathetic Marilla.
ex.zh: “不浪漫个鬼！”毫不体贴的玛丽拉说。

senses.d: noisy and lacking in restraint or discipline

incapable of being controlled
x: the little boy's parents think he is spirited, but his teacher finds him unruly

ex.t: Lo, Miss Pross, in harness of string, awakening the echoes, as an unruly charger, whip-corrected, snorting and pawing the earth under the plane-tree in the garden!
ex.zh: 瞧，普罗斯小姐戴着绳套，像个不服管、挨了鞭子的战马，在园子里那棵梧桐树下喷着鼻息、刨着地，把回声都惊醒了！

ex.t: It is full of unruly members.
ex.zh: 因为它满是闹哄哄、不服管的会员。

ex.t: The rest of the team, however, had grown unruly during the last days of Spitz, and their surprise was great now that Buck proceeded to lick them into shape.
ex.zh: 可其余的狗在斯皮茨最后那些日子里已经野了，如今巴克动手把他们收拾服帖，他们大吃一惊。

ex.t: All’s up--you can’t make nor mend; it’s to save your neck that I’m a-speaking, and if one of the wild uns knew it, where’d I be, Tom--now, tell me, where’d I be?”
ex.zh: 全都完了——你怎么也补不上了；我这是为救你这条脖子才说话，要是有哪个野家伙知道了，我还能在哪儿，汤姆——你说，我还能在哪儿？”

senses.d: lacking in security or safety
involving or causing danger or risk; liable to hurt or harm
not safe from attack

ex.t: But you will not be able to see him, my poor child, and even if you could, it would be unsafe for you to make a sign of recognition.”
ex.zh: 可是你看不见他，我可怜的孩子；就算看得见，你做出相认的表示也不安全。”

ex.t: It was unsafe to meddle with the corpses and ghosts of these creatures.
ex.zh: 去碰这些家伙的尸体和鬼魂，是不安全的。

senses.d: not made explicit
x: the unexpressed terms of the agreement

ex.t: What the white whale was to Ahab, has been hinted; what, at times, he was to me, as yet remains unsaid.
ex.zh: 白鲸对亚哈意味着什么，已经暗示过了；他有时对我意味着什么，却还没有说。

ex.t: He said things that would have been better unsaid, he had read too many books, he frequented the Chestnut Tree Cafe, haunt of painters and musicians.
ex.zh: 他说过一些本不该说的话，他书读得太多，他常去栗树咖啡馆，那是画家和音乐家出没的地方。

her performance proved to be unsatisfactory

He was tired of books, and found people so interesting now that Mr. Brooke was obliged to make very unsatisfactory reports, for Laurie was always playing truant and running over to the Marches’.
ex.zh: 他厌了书本，如今觉得人有趣得很，布鲁克先生只好交上很不成样子的报告，因为劳里老逃学，跑到马奇家去。

ex.t: He was in one of his moods, for the day had been both unprofitable and unsatisfactory, and he was wishing he could live it over again.
ex.zh: 他正闹着脾气，因为这一天既没长进，又不如意，他恨不得能重过一遍。

senses.d: not having been satisfied
worried and uneasy

ex.t: In spite of the intense labour and wonderful discoveries of modern philosophers, I always came from my studies discontented and unsatisfied.
I shall no longer feel the agonies which now consume me or be the prey of feelings unsatisfied, yet unquenched.
ex.zh: 我不再感到如今耗着我的那些痛苦，也不再做那些不得满足、却又不得平息的感情的猎物。

ex.t: It is exquisite, and it leaves one unsatisfied.
ex.zh: 它精致，又叫人得不到满足。

senses.d: not up to expectations

ex.zh: 可这笑话并不能让我满意，我一上午都在想那些身影，直到救薇娜的事把它们从脑中赶走。

not pleasing in odor or taste

ex.t: It may well be conceived, what an unsavory odor such a mass must exhale; worse than an Assyrian city in the plague, when the living are incompetent to bury the departed.
ex.zh: 很容易想见，这样一大团东西散发出的是何等难闻的臭气；比瘟疫中的亚述城还要糟，那时活人无力掩埋死者。

senses.d: take back what one has said
