ex.zh: 你们俩不如把招手以后说的话全收回，让面子也过得去，你说好不好？”

senses.d: take back what one has said

ex.t: But look ye, Starbuck, what is said in heat, that thing unsays itself.
ex.zh: 可你瞧，斯塔巴克，人在火头上说的话，那话自己会把自己收回。

senses.d: loosen something by unscrewing it
loosen by turning

ex.t: Run for the winch and unscrew the carriage pole!
ex.zh: 快去拿绞盘，把车辕卸下来！

ex.t: “Here’s the ship’s navel, this doubloon here, and they are all on fire to unscrew it.
ex.zh: “这就是船的肚脐，这儿的这枚达布隆；他们个个都急火火地要把它拧下来。

ex.t: But, unscrew your navel, and what’s the consequence?
ex.zh: 可把肚脐拧下来，后果如何？

senses.d: loosen something by unscrewing it
loosen by turning

ex.t: Happily then, when it was not too late, I thought of a danger I had hitherto forgotten, and reaching over the bars of the machine I unscrewed the little levers that would set it in motion, and put these in my pocket.
With an effort Wilson left the shade and support of the doorway and, breathing hard, unscrewed the cap of the tank.
ex.zh: 威尔逊费力地离开门口那片阴凉和倚靠，喘着粗气，拧开油箱盖。

senses.d: without scruples or principles
x: unscrupulous politicos who would be happy to sell...their country in order to gain power

ex.t: The pirate attack had been a complete surprise: a sure proof that the unscrupulous Hook had conducted it improperly, for to surprise redskins fairly is beyond the wit of the white man.
ex.zh: 海盗这一击完全出人意料：这确凿证明那毫无顾忌的胡克干得不守规矩，因为要正大光明地袭击红皮肤人，白人的脑筋是不够的。

senses.d: not established or confirmed
x: his doom is as yet unsealed

senses.d: not closed or secured with or as if with a seal

ex.t: At length, when the last pint is casked, and all is cool, then the great hatchways are unsealed, the bowels of the ship are thrown open, and down go the casks to their final rest in the sea.
ex.zh: 等到最后一品脱也装进桶、一切都凉了，那些大舱口就打开，船的肚肠全敞开来，桶便下到海里它们最后的安息处。

senses.d: not seamanlike

ex.t: “During the night, Radney had an unseamanlike way of sitting on the bulwarks of the quarter-deck, and leaning his arm upon the gunwale of the boat which was hoisted up there, a little above the ship’s side.
ex.zh: “夜里，拉德尼有一种不像水手的坐法：坐在后甲板的舷墙上，把胳膊倚在那条吊在那儿、略高于船舷的小艇的舷缘上。

senses.d: not in keeping with (and usually undesirable for) the season
x: unseasonable bright blue weather in November

senses.d: badly timed

ex.t: A severe and unseasonable attack of grippe had confined that good lady to her house ever since the occasion of her last visit to Green Gables.
ex.zh: 自从上回造访绿山墙以后，这位好心太太就害了一场来势凶猛、不合时令的流行性感冒，一直困在家里。

ex.t: Beware of enlisting in your vigilant fisheries any lad with lean brow and hollow eye; given to unseasonable meditativeness; and who offers to ship with the Phædon instead of Bowditch in his head.
ex.zh: 当心别把那种眉骨瘦削、眼窝深陷、动不动就发些不合时宜的沉思、来应募时脑子里装的是《斐多》而不是鲍迪奇《航海术》的小伙子，招进你们那警觉的渔业里。

senses.d: remove from political office
x: The Republicans are trying to unseat the liberal Democrat

senses.d: dislodge from one's seat, as from a horse

ex.t: “God knows I have!—a trouble which is enough to unseat my reason, so sudden and so terrible is it.
ex.zh: “老天知道我是遭了！——这难来得这样突然、这样可怕，足以叫我失去理智。

senses.d: remove from political office
x: The Republicans are trying to unseat the liberal Democrat

senses.d: dislodge from one's seat, as from a horse

ex.t: It was so sudden that Lady Anne was nearly unseated, but she soon recovered herself.

senses.d: not consciously observing
x: looked through him with blank unseeing eyes

senses.d: lacking sight

ex.t: As it progressed Anne became more and more abstracted, eating mechanically, with her big eyes fixed unswervingly and unseeingly on the sky outside the window.

senses.d: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society

ex.t: Secrets that few would like to scrutinise were bred and hidden in mountains of unseemly rags, masses of corrupted fat, and sepulchres of bones.
ex.zh: 很少有人愿意细究的秘密，就在那堆积如山的破布、成团的腐油和坟墓般的骨堆里滋生、藏匿。

ex.t: “Oh, Beth, he’s sent you...” began Amy, gesticulating with unseemly energy, but she got no further, for Jo quenched her by slamming down the window.
ex.zh: “哦，贝丝，他送了你……”艾米开口，手舞足蹈得不像样，可话没说完，乔砰地放下窗子，把她堵了回去。

senses.d: not seen or perceived
not seen or observed
not anticipated- H.W.Glidden
x: unanticipated and disconcerting lines of development

senses.d: a belief that there is a realm controlled by a divine spirit

ex.t: When he roused himself from his thoughtful quest, he fancied from the turn of the hand, and its situation in reference to himself, that the Unseen Eyes were looking at him keenly.
ex.zh: 等他从那沉思的寻觅中回过神来，从那手的方向和它相对自己的位置揣度，觉得那双看不见的眼睛正锐利地盯着他。

ex.t: The fountain in the village flowed unseen and unheard, and the fountain at the chateau dropped unseen and unheard--both melting away, like the minutes that were falling from the spring of Time--through three dark hours.
ex.zh: 村里的喷泉看不见、听不见地流着，宅邸的喷泉看不见、听不见地滴着——两者都像从时间之泉里落下的分分秒秒一样消逝——过了三个黑暗的钟头。

ex.t: A more remarkable face in its quiet, resolute, and guarded struggle with an unseen assailant, was not to be beheld in all the wide dominions of sleep, that night.
ex.zh: 那一夜，在睡梦的广阔疆域里，再也找不出一张脸，能像他这样安静、坚决、戒备地跟一个看不见的袭击者搏斗。

senses.d: disregarding your own advantages and welfare over those of others
not greedy

ex.t: Give me that unselfish nature, That with charity divine Can pardon wrong for love’s dear sake— Meek heart, forgive me mine!
ex.zh: 把那份无私的天性给我——它凭着神圣的慈爱，为了爱可以饶恕冤屈；温顺的心，也饶恕我的吧！

ex.t: The real drawback to marriage is that it makes one unselfish.
ex.zh: 婚姻真正的坏处，是叫人变得无私。

ex.t: And unselfish people are colourless.
ex.zh: 无私的人是没有色彩的。

senses.d: the quality of not putting yourself first but being willing to give your time or money or effort etc. for others
x: rural people show more devotion and unselfishness than do their urban cousins

senses.d: acting generously

ex.t: Your unselfishness cannot entirely comprehend how much my mind has gone on this; but, only ask yourself, how could my happiness be perfect, while yours was incomplete?”
ex.zh: 你的无私不能完全明白我为这事费了多少心思；可你只消问问自己，你的幸福不圆满，我的幸福怎么能圆满？”

ex.t: Peter, with heroic unselfishness, did not say anything about his Engine till after Father had had his dinner and his after-dinner cigar.
ex.zh: 彼得怀着英勇无私的心，直到爸爸吃过晚饭、抽完饭后雪茄，才提起他的火车头。

ex.t: The unselfishness was Mother's idea--but it was Peter who carried it out.
ex.zh: 这份无私是妈妈的主意——不过实行起来的是彼得。

senses.d: not ready for service
not capable of being used

ex.t: Organdy’s the most unserviceable stuff in the world anyhow, and I told Matthew so when he got it.
ex.zh: 玻璃纱本来就是天底下最不实用的料子，马修买的时候我就跟他说过。

senses.d: disturb the composure of

ex.t: It would unsettle her for a week.
ex.zh: 这叫她一个星期都安不下心来。

senses.d: still in doubt
not settled or established
subject to change
not yet settled

ex.t: “Unsettled weather, a long journey, uncertain means of travelling, a disorganised country, a city that may not be even safe for you.”
ex.zh: “天气不稳，路又远，路上怎么走没个准，国家乱成一团，那座城对你甚至可能不安全。”

ex.t: But my plan was unsettled, and I wandered many hours round the confines of the town, uncertain what path I should pursue.
ex.zh: 可我的计划没定，我在城郊转了许多个钟头，拿不准该走哪条路。

ex.t: We used to be faithful about it, but since Father went away and all this war trouble unsettled us, we have neglected many things.
ex.zh: 从前咱们还挺用心，可爸爸走了以后，这一场战争的烦恼把咱们的心搅乱了，许多事都荒废了。

senses.d: (of pictures) not having shadow represented
not darkened or dimmed by shade

ex.t: He unshaded his face after a little while, and spoke steadily.
ex.zh: 过了一会儿，他把手从脸上放下，稳稳地说。

senses.d: unshaken in purpose
x: wholly undismayed by the commercial failure of the three movies he had made

ex.t: My memory is circumstantial and unshaken.
ex.zh: 我的记忆周详而不可动摇。

senses.d: incompletely or imperfectly shaped

ex.t: But, in the stillness of the third hour of the morning, Lucie came downstairs again, and stole into his room; not free from unshaped fears, beforehand.
ex.zh: 可到了凌晨三点，万籁俱寂的时候，露西又下了楼，悄悄溜进他的房间；她来之前心里就不是没有些说不清的恐惧。

senses.d: of animals or fruits that have no shell

ex.t: The lobster was a scarlet mystery to her, but she hammered and poked till it was unshelled and its meager proportions concealed in a grove of lettuce leaves.
ex.zh: 那只龙虾对她是个通红的谜；她又是捶又是捅，总算把壳剥了，把它那点可怜的分量藏在一丛莴苣叶里。

senses.d: unpleasant to look at

ex.t: You must find them as awkward as they are unsightly.
ex.zh: 它们既不好看，又碍事，你一定也觉得。

senses.d: fully awake
x: so excited she was wide-awake all night

ex.t: Did you fixedly gaze, too, upon that ribbed and dented brow; there also, you would see still stranger foot-prints—the foot-prints of his one unsleeping, ever-pacing thought.
ex.zh: 你若也定睛去看那道起棱、凹陷的额头；在那儿你还会看见更奇特的脚印——他那唯一一个不眠的、永远在踱步的念头留下的脚印。

senses.d: not seeking or given to association; being or living without companions
x: the unsocial disposition to neglect one's neighbors

ex.t: We are each of an unsocial, taciturn disposition, unwilling to speak, unless we expect to say something that will amaze the whole room, and be handed down to posterity with all the éclat of a proverb.”
ex.zh: 我们俩都是不爱交际、沉默寡言的性情，除非指望说出一句能惊动满屋子人、并像格言一般风光地传之后世的话，就不肯开口。”

senses.d: not disposed of by purchase
x: the house has been on the market almost a year and is still unsold

ex.t: Jo couldn’t resist giving that little slap, but May took it so meekly she regretted it a minute after, and fell to praising the great vases, which still remained unsold.
ex.zh: 乔忍不住给了她这一小巴掌，可梅受得那么温顺，她过一分钟就后悔了，转而夸起那对大瓶子来——那瓶子还没卖出去。

senses.d: not solved

ex.t: No doubt in that perfect world there had been no unemployed problem, no social question left unsolved.
ex.zh: 无疑，在那个完美的世界里，没有失业问题，没有未解决的社会问题。

senses.d: not wise in the ways of the world- Kate O'Brien
x: either too unsophisticated or too honest to promise more than he could deliver

senses.d: lacking complexity
x: small and uncomplicated cars for those really interested in motoring

senses.d: awkwardly simple and provincial

ex.t: Or, to the unread, unsophisticated Protestant of the Middle American States, why does the passing mention of a White Friar or a White Nun, evoke such an eyeless statue in the soul?
ex.zh: 或者，对中部美洲各州那些没读过什么书、质朴的新教徒来说，为什么顺口一提白衣修士或白衣修女，就在灵魂里唤出那样一尊没有眼睛的雕像？

senses.d: not in good condition; damaged or decayed
not sound financially
containing or based on a fallacy
suffering from severe mental illness
physically unsound or diseased
of e.g. advice

ex.t: The jury found it a case of suicide while of unsound mind, and the few effects were handed over to the American Consul to deal with.
ex.zh: 陪审团裁定为精神失常下的自杀，几件遗物交给美国领事处理。

senses.d: situated at or extending to great depth; too deep to have been sounded or plumbed-Thomas Gray
x: the profound depths of the sea
the dark unfathomed caves of ocean

senses.d: not made to sound
x: the silent `h' at the beginning of `honor'
in French certain letters are often unsounded

ex.t: Over unsounded gorges, through the rifled hearts of mountains, under torrents’ beds, unerringly I rush!
ex.zh: 越过无底的峡谷，穿过被凿空的山心，钻过激流的河床，我毫厘不差地冲过去！

ex.t: That unsounded ocean you gasp in, is Life; those sharks, your foes; those spades, your friends; and what between sharks and spades you are in a sad pickle and peril, poor lad.
ex.zh: 你喘息其中的那片深不可测的海洋，就是人生；那些鲨鱼，是你的仇敌；那些铲子，是你的朋友；夹在鲨鱼和铲子之间，你就陷在一种又可悲又危险的境地，可怜的孩子。

ex.t: Mary!—boy! boy! boy!—But if I wake thee not to death, old man, who can tell to what unsounded deeps Starbuck’s body this day week may sink, with all the crew!
ex.zh: 玛丽！——孩子！孩子！孩子！——可我若是不叫你一睡不醒，老人家，谁说得清下礼拜的今天，斯塔巴克的尸体会同全船人一起沉到哪个没测过的深处去！

senses.d: defying expression or description
exceptionally bad or displeasing
too sacred to be uttered
x: the ineffable name of the Deity

ex.t: The spy looked round at the two gentlemen; they both looked in unspeakable astonishment at Jerry.
ex.zh: 探子回头看看那两位绅士；他们两人都难以言状地惊讶地看着杰里。

ex.t: “Well, I don’t envy you your job bringing that up, Marilla,” said Mrs. Rachel with unspeakable solemnity.
ex.zh: “唉，把这孩子拉扯大这份差事，我可不羡慕你，玛丽拉。”雷切尔太太一脸说不出的郑重。

ex.t: My rage is unspeakable when I reflect that the murderer, whom I have turned loose upon society, still exists.
ex.zh: 我一想到我放进人群里的那个凶手还活着，我的愤怒就无法言说。

senses.d: not left to spoil
not decayed or decomposed

ex.t: You were the most unspoiled creature in the whole world.
ex.zh: 你是这世上最没被败坏的人。

senses.d: expressed without speech- Emily Dickinson- Thomas Wolfe
not made explicit
x: the unexpressed terms of the agreement

ex.t: It was the best thing he could have done, far more soothing than the most eloquent words, for Jo felt the unspoken sympathy, and in the silence learned the sweet solace which affection administers to sorrow.
ex.zh: 这是他所能做的最好的事，比最会说话的话都更能安慰人；因为乔感到了那说不出的同情，在静默里懂得了情意给忧愁的那份甘甜的抚慰。

ex.t: The tradition--the unspoken tradition: somehow you knew it, though you never heard it said--was that they shot you from behind; always in the back of the head, without warning, as you walked down a corridor from cell to cell.
ex.zh: 那个传统——不出声的传统：不知怎么你就是知道，虽然从没听人说过——是从背后开枪；总是打后脑，没有警告，就在你顺着走廊从一个牢房走向另一个牢房的时候。

ex.t: “I didn't think that anyone would know but us,” said Bobbie, indignantly answering Peter's unspoken reproach.
ex.zh: “我以为除了我们没人会知道，”博比说，气鼓鼓地回敬彼得没说出口的责备。

senses.d: without soil or spot or stain

ex.t: One felt that he had kept himself unspotted from the world.
From my forenoon watch below, I ascended to the overclouded deck; and there, dashed upon the main hatches, I saw a regal, feathery thing of unspotted whiteness, and with a hooked, Roman bill sublime.
ex.zh: 我从午前的下舱值班里上来，走上阴云密布的后甲板；在那儿，撞在主舱口盖上的，我看见一只王者般的、羽毛丰盛的东西，一身无斑的白，配着一副崇高的、罗马式的钩喙。

ex.t: He had always the look of one who had kept himself unspotted from the world.
ex.zh: 他脸上总有一种不曾被这世界玷污的神情。

senses.d: lacking stability or fixity or firmness
x: the tower proved to be unstable in the high wind

senses.d: highly or violently reactive
affording no ease or reassurance
suffering from severe mental illness
disposed to psychological variability
subject to change; variable
x: a fluid situation fraught with uncertainty
everything was unstable following the coup

ex.t: Then I had to look down at the unstable hooks to which I clung.
ex.zh: 随后我只得低头去看自己抓着的不牢靠的铁钩。

ex.t: And this time I was not seated properly in the saddle, but sideways and in an unstable fashion.
ex.zh: 这一回我没能好好坐在坐鞍上，而是歪着身子，坐得不稳。

senses.d: not stained
x: An apron keeps his clothing unstained

senses.d: not having a coating of stain or varnish
without soil or spot or stain
(of reputation) free from blemishes

ex.t: They congregated round me; the unstained snowy mountain-top, the glittering pinnacle, the pine woods, and ragged bare ravine, the eagle, soaring amidst the clouds—they all gathered round me and bade me be at peace.
ex.zh: 它们聚在我周围；那不染纤尘的雪峰，那闪亮的尖顶，那松林，那崎岖光秃的峡谷，那在云中高翔的鹰——它们都聚到我身边，叫我安宁。

ex.t: He felt a wild longing for the unstained purity of his boyhood—his rose-white boyhood, as Lord Henry had once called it.
ex.zh: 他狂乱地渴望少年时代那不染的纯净——他玫瑰白的少年时代，亨利勋爵曾这样叫它。

senses.d: in an unsteady manner
x: he walked unsteadily toward the exit
The wounded soldier was swinging unsteadily on his legs

ex.t: Diana had stood up very unsteadily; then she sat down again, putting her hands to her head.
ex.zh: 黛安娜摇摇晃晃地站起来，又坐了下去，双手按住头。

ex.t: Then he rolled over and raised himself unsteadily on hands and knees.
ex.zh: 然后他翻过身，用手和膝盖颤巍巍地支起来。

ex.t: The man was led out, walking unsteadily, with head sunken, nursing his crushed hand, all the fight had gone out of him.
ex.zh: 那人被带出去，走得不稳，低着头，护着被踩坏的手，斗志全没了。

senses.d: subject to change or variation
x: his hand was unsteady as he poured the wine

senses.d: not firmly or solidly positioned
x: climbing carefully up the unsteady ladder

ex.t: After a time he fell asleep, and some unsteady fairies had to climb over him on their way home from an orgy.
They were done with some very poor instrument, and hurriedly, with an unsteady hand.
ex.zh: 那是用一件很粗劣的工具刻的，刻得匆忙，手在发抖。

ex.t: She needed both advantages, for the marks of gripping fingers were deep in her face, and her hair was torn, and her dress (hastily composed with unsteady hands) was clutched and dragged a hundred ways.
ex.zh: 她两样好处都需要，因为她脸上有深深的手指抓痕，头发被抓散，衣裳（用发抖的手匆匆理过的）被揪得、扯得七零八落。

senses.d: emotionally upset
x: the incident left him unstrung and incapable of rational effort

ex.t: She was really quite unstrung, for the reaction from her fright and cramped clinging was making itself felt.
ex.zh: 她实在有点撑不住了，因为惊吓和蜷着身子抓桥桩之后，那股反应上来了。

ex.t: Had the pirates kept together it is certain that they would have won; but the onset came when they were still unstrung, and they ran hither and thither, striking wildly, each thinking himself the last survivor of the crew.
ex.zh: 海盗们要是聚在一起，肯定能赢；可这一仗来时他们还没缓过劲，他们四处乱跑乱砍，个个以为自己是全船最后一个活着的。

senses.d: not brought under control

ex.t: She had dressed with more than usual care, and prepared in the highest spirits for the conquest of all that remained unsubdued of his heart, trusting that it was not more than might be won in the course of the evening.
ex.zh: 她打扮得比平日格外经心，兴致极高地准备去征服他心里还没降服的那一部分，相信那点地方，一个晚上总该拿得下来。

senses.d: not servile or submissive

ex.t: Often she started up at night, thinking Beth called her, and when the sight of the little empty bed made her cry with the bitter cry of unsubmissive sorrow, “Oh, Beth, come back!
ex.zh: 夜里她常惊起，以为贝丝叫她；看见那张空着的小床，她就带着不肯顺服的悲伤苦苦喊：“哦，贝丝，回来！

senses.d: lacking material form or substance; unreal
x: an insubstantial mirage on the horizon

ex.t: Within a minute afterwards, he was, to all outward appearance, as unsubstantial as ever.
ex.zh: 不到一分钟，从外表看，他又跟往常一样空虚无实了。

senses.d: not successful; having failed or having an unfavorable outcome
failing to accomplish an intended result
x: a stillborn plot to assassinate the President

ex.t: It is very interesting that we possess, in this same gallery, what may be called a spoiled first draught, or an unsuccessful study of him, in John Dashwood.
With them he pushed off; and, after much weary pulling, and many perilous, unsuccessful onsets, he at last succeeded in getting one iron fast.
ex.zh: 他带着他们离船而去；经过许多疲倦的划桨，许多次危险而无功的冲击，他终于把一支鲸镖扎牢了。

ex.t: His parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people-his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all.
ex.zh: 他父母是得过且过、一事无成的庄稼人——他的想象从未真正把他们认作父母。

senses.d: without success
x: she tried unsuccessfully to persuade him to buy a new car

ex.t: Anne laughed and tried unsuccessfully to withdraw her hand.
ex.zh: 安妮笑了，想抽回手，没抽成。

ex.t: They were confined for the evening at different tables; and she had nothing to hope, but that his eyes were so often turned towards her side of the room, as to make him play as unsuccessfully as herself.
ex.zh: 这一晚他们分坐在不同的牌桌上；她别无指望，只盼他的眼睛常常朝她这边看，害得他跟自己一样打不好牌。

ex.t: The girl addressed was trying, unsuccessfully, to slump against my shoulder.
ex.zh: 被问到的那姑娘正试图瘫靠在我肩上，没成功。

senses.d: not meant or adapted for a particular purpose
x: a solvent unsuitable for use on wood surfaces

senses.d: not capable of being applied
not conducive to good moral development
x: the movie is unsuitable for children

senses.d: not worthy of being chosen (especially as a spouse)

ex.t: It was a long time before she became at all reconciled to the idea of so unsuitable a match.
ex.zh: 过了很久，她才对这样不般配的一门亲事稍稍看得过去。

senses.d: spotlessly clean and fresh
(of reputation) free from blemishes

ex.t: I learned that the possessions most esteemed by your fellow creatures were high and unsullied descent united with riches.
ex.zh: 我得知，你们的同类所最看重的东西，是高贵无瑕的出身加上财富。

ex.t: Ah! in what a monstrous moment of pride and passion he had prayed that the portrait should bear the burden of his days, and he keep the unsullied splendour of eternal youth!
ex.zh: 啊！他是在怎样畸形的一刻，出于骄傲与激情，祈求让画像去承担他岁月的重负，而自己保住那不朽青春的无瑕辉煌！

senses.d: not sustained or maintained by nonmaterial aid
not held up or borne
x: removal of the central post left the roof unsupported

ex.t: Yet I fear such will be my fate; the men, unsupported by ideas of glory and honour, can never willingly continue to endure their present hardships.
ex.zh: 可我怕我的命运就是这样；这些人没有光荣和荣誉的念头撑着，决不会甘心继续受眼前的苦。

ex.t: Stones are hard, water is wet, objects unsupported fall towards the earth's centre.
ex.zh: 石头是硬的，水是湿的，没有支撑的东西会朝地心落下去。

senses.d: not suspected or believed likely
x: remained unsuspected as the head of the spy ring
he was able to get into the building unspotted and unsuspected

ex.t: “Criticism is the best test of such work, for it will show her both unsuspected merits and faults, and help her to do better next time.
ex.zh: “批评是这类作品最好的试金石，能把她自己都没想到的长处和毛病都显出来，帮她下次做得更好。

ex.t: A great uproar was raised, but he was unsuspected; while Dub, an awkward blunderer who was always getting caught, was punished for Buck’s misdeed.
ex.zh: 闹了一场大的，可没人疑心他；倒是达布——一条笨手笨脚、老被抓住的狗——替巴克的错挨了罚。

ex.t: I guessed the police had stuck that in, as a clumsy contrivance to persuade me that I was unsuspected.
ex.zh: 我猜是警察故意塞进去的，想笨拙地让我以为自己没被怀疑。

senses.d: not suspicious

ex.t: It was a hard matter to preserve the innocent deceit of which they were profoundly unsuspicious.
ex.zh: 要维持这无邪的瞒哄，而她们又深信不疑，那是件难事。

ex.t: For, innocent and unsuspicious as she was, she could not help understanding the gossip of her friends.
ex.zh: 因为她虽然天真、不疑心人，朋友们的这番闲话却由不得她听不懂。

ex.t: He declared himself to have been totally unsuspicious of her sister’s attachment; and she could not help remembering what Charlotte’s opinion had always been.
ex.zh: 他声明自己全然不曾疑心姐姐对他有意；她不由得想起夏洛特一向的看法。

senses.d: not suspicious

ex.t: I gave him good morning and he answered me unsuspiciously.
ex.zh: 我跟他道了声早，他也毫不疑心地回了。

senses.d: going directly ahead from one point to another without veering or turning aside
x: some people see evolution as an undeviating upward march from simple organisms to the very complex
a straight and narrow tree-lined road unswerving across the lowlands

senses.d: firm and dependable especially in loyalty
x: a staunch defender of free speech

ex.t: But François, chuckling at the incident while unswerving in the administration of justice, brought his lash down upon Buck with all his might.
ex.zh: 可弗朗索瓦一边为这事暗笑，一边执法不阿，使足力气把鞭子抽在巴克身上。

senses.d: in a constant and steadfast manner
without swerving; in a direct and unswerving manner
x: the ship travelled unswervingly through the night

ex.t: As it progressed Anne became more and more abstracted, eating mechanically, with her big eyes fixed unswervingly and unseeingly on the sky outside the window.

senses.d: not sympathetic or disposed toward
(of characters in literature or drama) tending to evoke antipathetic feelings
x: all the characters were peculiarly unsympathetic

senses.d: not having an open mind
x: a closed mind unreceptive to new ideas

senses.d: lacking in sympathy and kindness
not agreeing with your tastes or expectations
x: found the task disagreeable and decided to abandon it
a job temperamentally unsympathetic to him

ex.t: “Unromantic fiddlesticks!” said the unsympathetic Marilla.
ex.zh: “不浪漫个鬼！”毫不体贴的玛丽拉说。

ex.t: “I will tell you, Harry, but you mustn’t be unsympathetic about it.
ex.zh: “我告诉你，哈里，可你别不表同情。

ex.t: What if in this interval the race had lost its manliness, and had developed into something inhuman, unsympathetic, and overwhelmingly powerful?
ex.zh: 万一在这段时间里，人类已失去了人性，发展成了某种非人的、冷酷无情而又强大得压倒一切的东西呢？

senses.d: without sympathy; in an unsympathetic manner
x: the judge listened to the accused unsympathetically

ex.t: “I don’t think there is much fear of your dying of grief as long as you can talk, Anne,” said Marilla unsympathetically.
ex.zh: “安妮，只要你还说得动话，我看就不必担心你会伤心而死，”玛丽拉毫不同情地说。

ex.t: “Well, so nothing caught you?” said Marilla unsympathetically.
ex.zh: “哦，这么说没什么抓住你？”玛丽拉毫无同情地说。

senses.d: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated

ex.t: Why not still proceed over the untamed yet obedient element?
ex.zh: 为什么不能继续前进，越过这尚未驯服却仍顺服的元素呢？

ex.t: Lydia was Lydia still; untamed, unabashed, wild, noisy, and fearless.
ex.zh: 莉迪亚还是那个莉迪亚：不受管束，不知羞耻，野气十足，吵吵嚷嚷，什么都不怕。

senses.d: still full
x: an untouched cocktail in her hand

ex.t: Sleep forsook her eyes, meals stood untasted, day and night were all too short to enjoy the happiness which blessed her only at such times, and made these hours worth living, even if they bore no other fruit.
ex.zh: 睡意离开了她的眼睛，饭搁着不动，白天黑夜都太短，不够她享受这种只有这时候才降临的幸福；这些时辰就是没别的果子，也值得活一场。

ex.t: “Yes, this must be ginger,” peering into the as yet untasted cup.
ex.zh: “对，这准是姜，”他朝那杯还没人尝过的水细看。

ex.t: Plate after plate went away untasted.
ex.zh: 一盘盘菜原样撤了下去。

senses.d: lacking in schooling
x: untaught people whose verbal skills are grossly deficient

ex.t: The untaught peasant beheld the elements around him and was acquainted with their practical uses.

senses.d: incapable of being conceived or considered

ex.t: But a real love affair was an almost unthinkable event.
ex.zh: 可真正的恋爱几乎是不可想象的事。

ex.t: Unthinkable to disobey the iron voice from the wall.
ex.zh: 违抗墙里那个铁一般的声音是不可想象的。

ex.t: It is unthinkable.”
ex.zh: 这不可思议。”

senses.d: not exhibiting or characterized by careful thought

ex.t: "Tom's getting very profound," said Daisy, with an expression of unthoughtful sadness.
ex.zh: “汤姆变得很深奥了。”黛西说，脸上是一种不经思索的忧伤。

senses.d: in a messy, untidy manner
x: Rossi spat very deliberately, and very messily, upon Durieux's party card

ex.t: When Marilla came up for the light various skimpy articles of raiment scattered most untidily over the floor and a certain tempestuous appearance of the bed were the only indications of any presence save her own.

senses.d: the condition of being untidy
the trait of being untidy and messy

ex.t: We went to his study for coffee, a jolly room full of books and trophies and untidiness and comfort.
ex.zh: 我们到他书房喝咖啡，那是间快活的屋子，满是书、猎获物，乱而舒服。

senses.d: not neat and tidy
x: careless and untidy in her personal habits

ex.t: That is a very untidy habit, and I can’t allow it at all.
ex.zh: 这是个很不整洁的坏习惯，我可不能容许。

ex.t: Her solitary breakfast did not taste good, and the room seemed lonely and untidy, for Jo had not filled the vases, Beth had not dusted, and Amy’s books lay scattered about.
ex.zh: 一个人吃的早饭没滋味，屋里又冷清又零乱：乔没换花瓶里的花，贝丝没掸灰，艾米的书摊得到处都是。

ex.t: Elsewhere in this volume the slanderous aspersion has been disproved, that the vocation of whaling is throughout a slatternly, untidy business.
ex.zh: 本书别处已经驳倒了那项诽谤，说捕鲸这行业彻头彻尾是种邋遢不洁的营生。

senses.d: undo the ties of
cause to become loose

ex.t: And we shan't untie you till you promise never, never to talk to us about blood and wounds unless we say you may.
ex.zh: 你不答应永远、永远不再跟我们讲血啊伤口啊，除非我们说可以，我们就不解开你。

ex.t: Let me untie you, Pete.”
ex.zh: 我给你解开，皮特。”

ex.t:
“I don't care if you never untie me,” said Peter; “and if that's your idea of a joke--”

“If I were you,” said the Doctor, though really he did not quite know what to say, “I should be untied before your Mother comes down.
ex.zh:
“我不在乎你一辈子不解开我，”彼得说，“要是你管这叫玩笑——”

“我要是你，”医生说，其实他也不太知道该说什么，“就在你妈妈下来之前解开。

senses.d: not tied
with laces not tied
x: teenagers slopping around in unlaced sneakers

senses.d: not bound by shackles and chains

ex.t:
“I don't care if you never untie me,” said Peter; “and if that's your idea of a joke--”

“If I were you,” said the Doctor, though really he did not quite know what to say, “I should be untied before your Mother comes down.
ex.zh:
“我不在乎你一辈子不解开我，”彼得说，“要是你管这叫玩笑——”

“我要是你，”医生说，其实他也不太知道该说什么，“就在你妈妈下来之前解开。

ex.t: And if he is the great Head, he will be at my mercy; for I will roll this head all about the room until he promises to give us what we desire.
I do not intend to sail until the month of June; and when shall I return?
We, however, lay to until the morning, fearing to encounter in the dark those large loose masses which float about after the breaking up of the ice.

senses.d: not plowed or harrowed or hoed

ex.t: There were no fences at all by the roadside now, and the land was rough and untilled.
As they advanced the ground became rougher and hillier, for there were no farms nor houses in this country of the West, and the ground was untilled.
ex.zh: 越往前走，地面越崎岖，丘陵也越多，因为这西方的地方没有农舍，也没有人家，土地没人耕种。

senses.d: badly timed
uncommonly early or before the expected time
x: illness led to his premature death
alcohol brought him to an untimely end

senses.d: too soon; in a premature manner

ex.t: Was he the only passenger who came on board at that untimely hour?”
ex.zh: 在那个不合时宜的时辰上船的，只有他一个乘客吗？”

ex.t: Who that had seen him bright and joyous in his young beauty, but must weep over his untimely loss!
ex.zh: 谁见过他年少俊美、明快欢喜的样子，能不为他这样早夭而落泪！

ex.t: Margaret, what comment can I make on the untimely extinction of this glorious spirit?
ex.zh: 玛格丽特，对这个光荣的灵魂这样早地熄灭，我能说什么呢？

senses.d: characterized by hard work and perseverance

ex.t: But it takes time to make a raft, even when one is as industrious and untiring as the Tin Woodman, and when night came the work was not done.
So, with great perseverance and untiring industry, he prospered.
ex.zh: 就这样，凭着极大的坚忍和不倦的勤勉，他发达了。

ex.t: Her grandfather often called her ‘Beth’, and her grandmother watched over her with untiring devotion, as if trying to atone for some past mistake, which no eye but her own could see.
ex.zh: 爷爷常叫她“贝丝”；奶奶不知疲倦地守着她，仿佛想补赎从前一桩过错——那错除了她自己的眼睛，谁也看不见。

senses.d: not of the nobility

ex.t: They are descended, on the maternal side, from the same noble line; and, on the father’s, from respectable, honourable, and ancient, though untitled, families.
ex.zh: 论母系，他们同出一门贵胄；论父系，也都是体面、可敬、古老、虽无爵位却有名望的人家。

senses.d: too much to be measured

ex.t: The sights he had seen there, with brief snatches of food and sleep by intervals, shall remain untold.
ex.zh: 他在那里看见的景象，以及间或匆匆抓一口食、打个盹的情形，都不必再说了。

ex.t: The latter informs the party that she bequeaths untold wealth to the young pair and an awful doom to Don Pedro, if he doesn’t make them happy.
ex.zh: 信上说，她留给这对年轻人数不清的财富；唐彼德罗若不让他们幸福，就要遭可怕的报应。

ex.t: Where unrecorded names and navies rust, and untold hopes and anchors rot; where in her murderous hold this frigate earth is ballasted with bones of millions of the drowned; there, in that awful water-land, there was thy most familiar home.
ex.zh: 在那里，无名的姓名和无名的舰队一同锈蚀，无从说起的希望和铁锚一同腐烂；在那里，这艘叫作地球的护卫舰用它那杀人的底舱，装着千百万溺死者的尸骨压舱；就在那里，在那片可怖的水中之国，曾有你最熟稔的家。

senses.d: beyond the reach of criticism or attack or impeachment- Newsweek
x: for the first time criticism was directed at a hitherto untouchable target

senses.d: impossible to assail
forbidden to the touch
x: in most museums such articles are untouchable

senses.d: (especially used in traditional Hindu belief of the lowest caste or castes) defiling
not capable of being obtained
x: a rare work, today almost inaccessible
timber is virtually unobtainable in the islands

senses.d: belongs to lowest social and ritual class in India

ex.t: And though now nailed amidst all the rustiness of iron bolts and the verdigris of copper spikes, yet, untouchable and immaculate to any foulness, it still preserved its Quito glow.
ex.zh: 如今它虽然钉在满是铁栓锈迹和铜钉铜绿的中间，却仍旧不受任何污秽的沾染，保全着它那基多的光彩。

senses.d: beyond the reach of criticism or attack or impeachment- Newsweek
x: for the first time criticism was directed at a hitherto untouchable target

senses.d: impossible to assail
forbidden to the touch
x: in most museums such articles are untouchable

senses.d: (especially used in traditional Hindu belief of the lowest caste or castes) defiling
not capable of being obtained
x: a rare work, today almost inaccessible
timber is virtually unobtainable in the islands

senses.d: belongs to lowest social and ritual class in India

ex.t: But also they were outlaws, enemies, untouchables, doomed with absolute certainty to extinction within a year or two.
ex.zh: 但他们同时也是逃犯、敌人、不可接触者，绝对肯定地注定在一两年内被消灭。

senses.d: still full
x: an untouched cocktail in her hand

senses.d: not influenced or affected- V.L.Parrington
x: stewed in its petty provincialism untouched by the brisk debates that stirred the old world

senses.d: not having come in contact
emotionally unmoved
x: always appeared completely unmoved and imperturbable

ex.t: He set down his glass untouched.
ex.zh: 他把杯子放下，没有喝。

ex.t: The apple lay untouched on her desk until the next morning, when little Timothy Andrews, who swept the school and kindled the fire, annexed it as one of his perquisites.
ex.zh: 那苹果一直原封不动地搁在她桌上，直到第二天早上，扫教室、生炉子的小蒂莫西·安德鲁斯把它当作自己的一份外快收走了。

ex.t: “Yankees have a trick of being generous to their enemies,” said Jo, with a look that made the lad redden, “especially when they beat them,” she added, as, leaving Kate’s ball untouched, she won the game by a clever stroke.
ex.zh: “北方佬有个毛病，对敌人宽宏大量，”乔说，那眼神叫那小伙子红了脸，“尤其是打赢他们的时候，”她补了一句，放过凯特的球不碰，一杆巧打，赢了这一局。

senses.d: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
contrary to your interests or welfare
x: made a place for themselves under the most untoward conditions

ex.t: They had a very good time and nothing untoward happened until after tea, when they found themselves in the Barry garden, a little tired of all their games and ripe for any enticing form of mischief which might present itself.
ex.zh: 大家玩得很痛快，茶点之前没出什么事；茶后她们到了巴里家的园子里，游戏都玩腻了，正适合来点什么勾人的淘气花样。

ex.t: Her efforts in this line, however, were brought to an abrupt close by an untoward accident, which quenched her ardor.
ex.zh: 可她这一路的努力，被一桩倒霉的意外突然打断了，她的热劲儿也就此熄了。

ex.t: It has before been hinted, perhaps, that every little untoward circumstance that befell him, and which indirectly sprang from his luckless mishap, almost invariably irritated or exasperated Ahab.
ex.zh: 前面也许已经暗示过：凡是落到他头上的、由他那桩不幸的灾祸间接生出的每一件小小的不顺，几乎总要使亚哈恼怒或暴怒。

senses.d: not capable of being put into another form or style or language

ex.t: In the future such fragments, even if they chanced to survive, would be unintelligible and untranslatable.
ex.zh: 将来，这类残片即便侥幸留存，也会无法理解、无法翻译。

senses.d: not traveled over or through
not having traveled much, especially to foreign lands; not having gained experience by travel

ex.t: How vain and foolish, then, thought I, for timid untravelled man to try to comprehend aright this wondrous whale, by merely poring over his dead attenuated skeleton, stretched in this peaceful wood.
ex.zh: 于是我心想：怯生生的、没有远行的凡人，若只死盯着这头奇鲸那死了的、瘦削的骨架，看它摊在这片寂静的林子里，就想正确领会他，那是多么徒劳、多么愚蠢。

ex.t: And even of what he knew, how much could he make his untravelled friend either apprehend or believe?
ex.zh: 即便他所知道的那些，又能有多少让从未远行的朋友听懂或相信呢？

senses.d: not given medical care or treatment
x: the untreated wounded lay on makeshift cots

senses.d: not subjected to chemical or physical treatment
(of a specimen for study under a microscope) not treated with a reagent or dye

ex.t: His wrenched shoulder-blade, untreated and unrested, went from bad to worse, till finally Hal shot him with the big Colt’s revolver.
ex.zh: 他扭伤的肩膀没人治、也没歇，越发坏下去，最后哈尔用那把大号柯尔特左轮把他打死了。

senses.d: not trimmed

ex.t: He wore the white riding-coat and top-boots, then in vogue, and the light of the fire touching their light surfaces made him look very pale, with his long brown hair, all untrimmed, hanging loose about him.
ex.zh: 他穿着当时时兴的白色骑马外衣和长筒靴，火光触到那些浅色的表面，显得他脸色很苍白；他那头从不修剪的褐色长发松松地垂在脸旁。

senses.d: lacking pathways

ex.t: The wounded deer dragging its fainting limbs to some untrodden brake, there to gaze upon the arrow which had pierced it, and to die, was but a type of me.
ex.zh: 那受伤的鹿拖着发软的腿走到无人踏过的丛林里，在那里凝望射穿它的那支箭，然后死去——那不过是我的一幅小像。

senses.d: not beset by troubles or disturbance or distress
x: seemed untroubled by doubts of any kind

senses.d: free from fear or doubt; easy in mind
x: he was secure that nothing will be held against him

senses.d: free from turmoil or worries

ex.t: All things, however, were in their places; all was quiet; and he lay asleep, his white hair picturesque on the untroubled pillow, and his hands lying quiet on the coverlet.
ex.zh: 可一切都在原处；一切都安静；他躺着睡着了，白发在那只安然的枕头上显得很好看，两手静静地放在被子上。

ex.t: But you, Dorian, with your pure, bright, innocent face, and your marvellous untroubled youth—I can’t believe anything against you.
ex.zh: 可你，道林，你有那样纯净、明朗、天真的脸，有那样奇妙的、无忧的青春——我没法相信任何对你不利的话。

ex.t: His night had been untroubled by any images of pleasure or of pain.
ex.zh: 那一夜，没有任何欢愉或痛苦的影像来扰他。

senses.d: not according with the facts
x: unfortunately the statement was simply untrue

senses.d: not true to an obligation or trust-Bruno Laske
x: is untrue to his highest opportunity and duty

senses.d: not accurately fitted; not level
x: the frame was out of true
off-level floors and untrue doors and windows

senses.d: (used especially of persons) not dependable in devotion or affection; unfaithful

ex.t: To say that he was not startled, or that his blood was not conscious of a terrible sensation to which it had been a stranger from infancy, would be untrue.
ex.zh: 要说他没受惊，要说他的血没有感到一种从婴孩时起就未曾有过的骇人感觉，那是不真切的。

ex.t: If some men are shams and humbugs, that does not make religion untrue.
ex.zh: 就算有些人是假货、是骗子，也不能因此说道理是假的。

ex.t: It was so wicked, so untrue and ungrateful, how could I say it!
ex.zh: 这话太坏了，太不真、太没良心了，我怎么说得出口！

senses.d: in a untrue manner
x: he silenced the whisperings which connected her, untruly and unfairly, with his separation from his wife

ex.t: “No offence,” said the Porter, untruly but politely, and went.
ex.zh: “不碍事，”搬运工说——这话不老实，可说得客气——说完就走了。

senses.d: not worthy of trust or belief

ex.t: I must say, with all her faults, I never found her disobedient or untrustworthy before and I’m real sorry to find her so now.”
ex.zh: 说实在的，她毛病再多，我从前倒没觉得她不听话、不可靠，如今发现她这样，我真难过。”

ex.t: Don’t call her untrustworthy until you’re sure she has disobeyed you.
ex.zh: 还没断定她不听话，先别就说她不可靠。

ex.t: A Rogue laid a wager that he would prove the Oracle at Delphi to be untrustworthy by procuring from it a false reply to an inquiry by himself.
ex.zh: 一个无赖跟人打赌，说他只要拿一个问题去问德尔斐的神谕，诓它给个假答复，就能证明神谕靠不住。

senses.d: a false statement

ex.t: There was truth and there was untruth, and if you clung to the truth even against the whole world, you were not mad.
ex.zh: 有真，也有假；如果你抓住真，即使对抗全世界，你也没有疯。

senses.d: in a mendacious and untruthful manner
x: I told him, quite untruthfully, that I had just returned from leave

ex.t: 'I've been using the same blade for six weeks,' he added untruthfully.
ex.zh: “我一片刀片用了六个星期，”他补了一句假话。

senses.d: lacking in schooling
x: untaught people whose verbal skills are grossly deficient

ex.t: There was excellent blood in his veins—royal stuff; though sadly vitiated, I fear, by the cannibal propensity he nourished in his untutored youth.
ex.zh: 他血管里流着极好的血——王家的血；不过我担心，这血被他未受教化的少年时代养出来的吃人习性害得不轻。

ex.t: But like Czar Peter content to toil in the shipyards of foreign cities, Queequeg disdained no seeming ignominy, if thereby he might happily gain the power of enlightening his untutored countrymen.
ex.zh: 可就像彼得沙皇甘心在异邦城市的船厂里干活，魁魁格不嫌任何表面上的卑贱，只要借此能幸运地获得力量，好去开导他那些未受教化的同胞。

senses.d: cause to become untwisted

ex.t: Alice crouched down among the trees as well as she could, for her neck kept getting entangled among the branches, and every now and then she had to stop and untwist it.

senses.d: loosening the ties that fasten something
x: the tying of bow ties is an art; the untying is easy

ex.t: Everyone thinks this when he sees another person stirring a fire, or opening a box, or untying a knot in a bit of string.
ex.zh: 谁看见别人拨火、开箱子，或者解一小段绳子上的结，都会这么想。

senses.d: not capable of being used

ex.t: She is ballasted with utilities; not altogether with unusable pig-lead and kentledge.
ex.zh: 她用有用的东西压舱；不全是些用不上的铅锭和铁块。

senses.d: not yet used or soiled
not yet put into use
x: we bought an unused car for a change

senses.d: not in active use
x: the machinery sat idle during the strike

ex.t: The kitchen at Green Gables was a cheerful apartment--or would have been cheerful if it had not been so painfully clean as to give it something of the appearance of an unused parlor.
Marilla made no reply, but she hit the unlucky sorrel such a vicious clip with the whip that the fat mare, unused to such treatment, whizzed indignantly down the lane at an alarming pace.
Actually he had two unused ones which he was hoarding up.
ex.zh: 其实他有两片没用过的，正囤着。

senses.d: not usual or common or ordinary
being definitely out of the ordinary and unexpected; slightly odd or even a bit weird
x: a strange exaltation that was indefinable

senses.d: not commonly encountered
x: two-career families are no longer unusual

ex.t: Quite so; but the sequel was rather unusual.
It is most refreshingly unusual.
But there was no unusual sound--nothing but the low wash of the ripple and the croaking of the inmates of the wood.

senses.d: to a remarkable degree or extent
x: Notably missing from the network's fall line-up are any half-hour scripted comedies

ex.t: And in the sect--fairly large and yet unusually choice--of Austenians or Janites, there would probably be found partisans of the claim to primacy of almost every one of the novels.
the near leader violently shook his head and everything upon it--like an unusually emphatic horse, denying that the coach could be got up the hill.
He didn't say any more, but we've always been unusually communicative in a reserved way, and I understood that he meant a great deal more than that.

senses.d: too sacred to be uttered
x: the ineffable name of the Deity

senses.d: defying expression or description
very difficult to pronounce correctly

ex.t: Depart to your home and commence your labours; I shall watch their progress with unutterable anxiety; and fear not but that when you are ready I shall appear.”
ex.zh: 回你的家去，动手干活吧；我会以说不出的焦急看着它的进展；别怕，你准备好时我就会来。”

ex.t: It advertised his callowness—a callowness sheer and unutterable.
ex.zh: 它明明白白露出他的嫩——嫩得纯粹，说都说不出来。

ex.t: He was silent, and I guessed at his unutterable depression.
ex.zh: 他沉默了，我猜到了他那说不出的沮丧。

senses.d: to an inexpressible degree
x: she was looking very young tonight, and, as usual, indescribably beautiful, in a simple strapless dress of a green and white silky cotton

ex.t: Anne watched them as she talked and somehow felt that wind and stars and fireflies were all tangled up together into something unutterably sweet and enchanting.
ex.zh: 安妮一边说一边望着它们，不知怎么觉得风、星星和萤火虫都缠到了一处，缠成一种说不出的甜、说不出的迷人的东西。

ex.t: We drew in deep breaths of it as we walked back from dinner through the cold vestibules, unutterably aware of our identity with this country for one strange hour, before we melted indistinguishably into it again.
ex.zh: 我们从餐车穿过寒冷的车厢连接处走回来，深深吸着这空气，说不出的清楚：在这奇异的一个钟头里，我们与这片土地是一体的，随后又消融其中，再分不清彼此。

senses.d: not made explicit
x: the unexpressed terms of the agreement

ex.t: It almost seemed to her that those secret, unuttered, critical thoughts had suddenly taken visible and accusing shape and form in the person of this outspoken morsel of neglected humanity.
ex.zh: 她几乎觉得，那些隐秘的、从没说出声的挑剔念头，忽然化成了看得见、会指控人的形状，就长在这个心直口快、没人疼的小人儿身上。

ex.t: And when, released, he sprang to his feet, his mouth laughing, his eyes eloquent, his throat vibrant with unuttered sound, and in that fashion remained without movement, John Thornton would reverently exclaim, “God! you can all but speak!”
ex.zh: 一放开，他就跳起来站住，嘴笑着，眼睛说着话，喉咙里颤着没吐出来的声音，就那样一动不动；约翰·桑顿便会敬畏地叫一声：“天！你简直会说话！”

senses.d: unvarying in nature
lacking variety
always the same; showing a single form or character in all occurrences
x: a street of uniform tall white buildings

ex.t: Marilla kept her clothed in plain, dark dresses, all made after the same unvarying pattern.
ex.zh: 玛丽拉给她穿的都是素净的深色衣裳，全照一个一成不变的纸样做的。

ex.t: But calm, snow-white, and unvarying; still directing its fountain of feathers to the sky; still beckoning us on from before, the solitary jet would at times be descried.
ex.zh: 可那股孤零零的喷水，仍旧平静、雪白、不变；仍旧把它那羽毛的喷泉直射向天；仍旧在前头招手叫我们向前，有时还能被望见。

ex.t: The humming sound and the unvarying white light induced a sort of faintness, an empty feeling inside his head.
ex.zh: 嗡嗡声和一成不变的白光引起一种虚脱，脑袋里空空的。

senses.d: remove the veil from
x: Women must not unveil themselves in public in some religious societies

senses.d: make visible
x: He brings out the best in her

senses.d: remove the cover from
revealed; especially by having a veil removed
x: a new generation of unveiled women in Iran
applauding the unveiled statue of Winston Churchill

ex.t: He had partially unveiled the face of Nature, but her immortal lineaments were still a wonder and a mystery.

senses.d: incapable of being justified or explained

ex.t: Jupiter granted beards to the She-Goats at their own request, much to the disgust of the he-Goats, who considered this to be an unwarrantable invasion of their rights and dignities.

Still, looking round me again, and seeing no possible chance of spending a sufferable night unless in some other person's bed, I began to think that after all I might be cherishing unwarrantable prejudices against this unknown harpooneer.

Still, looking round me again, and seeing no possible chance of spending a sufferable night unless in some other person’s bed, I began to think that after all I might be cherishing unwarrantable prejudices against this unknown harpooneer.
ex.zh: 不过，我又四下看了一遍，看出除了睡到别人的床上，这一夜无论如何没法过得去，便渐渐觉得：我对这个素未谋面的鱼叉手，也许终究抱着些没有根据的成见。

senses.d: in an unwarrantable manner or to an unwarranted degree
x: in this painting, the relationship of the upper part of the body to the lower is uneasy and the right thigh seems unwarrantably stressed

ex.t: Should any unwarrantably pert young Leviathan coming that way, presume to draw confidentially close to one of the ladies, with what prodigious fury the Bashaw assails him, and chases him away!
ex.zh: 要是有哪头不知天高地厚的年轻利维坦打那条路过来，竟敢凑到哪位夫人身边去套近乎，这位帕夏便以何等惊人的狂怒扑上去，把他赶开！

ex.t: Applied to any other creature than the Leviathan—to an ant or a flea—such portly terms might justly be deemed unwarrantably grandiloquent.
ex.zh: 若用在利维坦以外的任何生物身上——用在蚂蚁或跳蚤身上——这样的字眼也许要被人觉得是毫无道理地夸大其词。

senses.d: incapable of being justified or explained
without a basis in reason or fact
lacking justification or authorization

ex.t: Matthew decided that he would give her one; that surely could not be objected to as an unwarranted putting in of his oar.
ex.zh: 马修决定送她一件；这总不至于被人说成是多管闲事、乱插一杠子。

ex.t: Nor did it remain unwarranted by the event.
ex.zh: 事后看来，这也并非没有应验。

senses.d: not alert to danger or deception- O.J.Campbell
x: the shrieks of unwary animals taken by surprise
some thieves prey especially on unwary travelers

ex.t: “Thank you, I prefer spiders,” she replied, fishing up two unwary little ones who had gone to a creamy death.
ex.zh: “谢谢，我更爱吃蜘蛛，”她答道，从里面捞出两只不小心淹死在奶油里的小虫。

senses.d: of or associated with the great masses of people
x: the common people in those days suffered greatly
behavior that branded him as common

senses.d: not cleaned with or as if with soap and water
x: a sink full of unwashed dishes

ex.t: When driven with his mates to the new owners' camp, Buck saw a slipshod and slovenly affair, tent half stretched, dishes unwashed, everything in disorder; also, he saw a woman.
When driven with his mates to the new owners’ camp, Buck saw a slipshod and slovenly affair, tent half stretched, dishes unwashed, everything in disorder; also, he saw a woman.
ex.zh: 跟同伴一起被赶到新主人的营地时，巴克看见一摊邋遢潦草的景象：帐篷支了一半，盘子没洗，什么都乱着；他还看见一个女人。

ex.t: The tin dishes were packed away unwashed.
ex.zh: 铁盘子没洗就收起来了。

senses.d: with unreduced energy

ex.t: Through the lacings of the leaves, the great sun seemed a flying shuttle weaving the unwearied verdure.
ex.zh: 透过叶子的网眼，那大太阳像一只飞梭，织着不知疲倦的绿。

senses.d: with unreduced energy

ex.t: To me he was unweariedly kind, and always glad to see me in the galley, which he kept as clean as a new pin, the dishes hanging up burnished and his parrot in a cage in one corner.
ex.zh: 对我他一直好得不知疲倦，总高兴我去厨房；那厨房他收拾得干干净净，跟新针似的，盘子擦得发亮挂起来，一只角上放着他那鹦鹉的笼子。

senses.d: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality
x: an indefatigable advocate of equal rights

ex.t: But since in reality Big Brother is not omnipotent and the party is not infallible, there is need for an unwearying, moment-to-moment flexibility in the treatment of facts.
ex.zh: 但既然实际上老大哥并非无所不能，党也并非绝无错误，处理事实就需要一种不知疲倦、每时每刻的灵活。

ex.t: Mr. Collins repeated his apologies in quitting the room, and was assured, with unwearying civility, that they were perfectly needless.
ex.zh: 柯林斯先生退出屋子时又连声道歉，对方不倦地客气作答，说这全然不必。

ex.t: Indeed, it was remarkable how well he bore these slights and with what unwearying politeness he kept on trying to ingratiate himself with all.
ex.zh: 的确，他受这些冷落受得那么好，又那么不倦地客气着，想讨所有人的好，真叫人惊奇。

senses.d: of someone who has not been married

ex.t: Our souls are like those orphans whose unwedded mothers die in bearing them: the secret of our paternity lies in their grave, and we must there to learn it.
ex.zh: 我们的灵魂就像那些孤儿，他们未嫁的母亲生他们时死了：我们出身的秘密就在她们的坟里，我们必须到那里去才知道。

senses.d: not welcome; not giving pleasure or received with pleasure
not welcome

ex.t: Here was an unexpectedly good chance to get this unwelcome orphan off her hands, and she did not even feel grateful for it.
ex.zh: 这本来是个意想不到的好机会，可以把这个不受欢迎的孤儿从手里推出去，她却连感激的意思都没有。

ex.t: There was novelty in the scheme; and as, with such a mother and such uncompanionable sisters, home could not be faultless, a little change was not unwelcome for its own sake.
ex.zh: 这计划里有新鲜；况且有那样一个母亲、那样几个合不来的妹妹，家里总不能十全十美，换换地方本身也就不算不受欢迎。

ex.t: “You certainly do,” she replied with a smile; “but it does not follow that the interruption must be unwelcome.”
ex.zh: “的确是打扰了，”她含笑答道，“可这并不等于说，这打扰一定不受欢迎。”

senses.d: somewhat ill or prone to illness

ex.t: I find myself very unwell this morning, which, I suppose, is to be imputed to my getting wet through yesterday.

senses.d: detrimental to physical or moral well-being

ex.t: A clammy and intensely cold mist, it made its slow way through the air in ripples that visibly followed and overspread one another, as the waves of an unwholesome sea might do.
They kept him out in the unwholesome mists at night, and ordered him back into his harness in the day.
ex.zh: 他们让他在夜里有毒的雾气里待着，白天又命令他回去套车。

ex.t: But Miss Stacy said it was a very silly, unwholesome book, and she asked me not to read any more of it or any like it.
ex.zh: 可史黛西小姐说那是本很蠢、很不健康的书，叫我别再读它，也别读那一类的。

senses.d: difficult to use or handle or manage because of size or weight or shape
x: we set about towing the unwieldy structure into the shelter

senses.d: difficult to work or manipulate
lacking grace in movement or posture
x: a gawky lad with long ungainly legs

ex.t: The overloaded and unwieldy sled forged ahead, Buck and his mates struggling frantically under the rain of blows.
ex.zh: 超载的笨雪橇往前挪动，巴克和同伴在雨点般的抽打下拼命挣扎。

senses.d: not disposed or inclined toward
in spite of contrary volition

ex.t: Unwilling to lose his nuts but unable to withdraw his hand, he burst into tears.
But my mother, frightened as she was, would not consent to take a fraction more than was due to her and was obstinately unwilling to be content with less.
This she would not hear of; but she was not so unwilling to comply with their brother's proposal; and it was settled that Mr.

senses.d: in an unwilling manner
x: he had sinned against her unwillingly

ex.t: When the clock struck three, Elizabeth felt that she must go, and very unwillingly said so.
He moved on as he spoke, and the Dormouse followed him: the March Hare moved into the Dormouse's place, and Alice rather unwillingly took the place of the March Hare.
He moved on as he spoke, and the Dormouse followed him: the March Hare moved into the Dormouse’s place, and Alice rather unwillingly took the place of the March Hare.
ex.zh: 他一边说一边挪过去，睡鼠跟着他；三月兔坐到了睡鼠的位子上，爱丽丝则很不情愿地坐到了三月兔的位子上。

senses.d: the trait of being unwilling
x: his unwillingness to cooperate vetoed every proposal I made
in spite of our warnings he plowed ahead with the involuntariness of an automaton

ex.t: His constraint was so manifest, and it was so manifest, too, that it originated in an unwillingness to approach the subject, that Charles Darnay hesitated.
ex.zh: 他的拘谨那么明显，而且那么明显地起于不愿触及这个话题，以至于查尔斯·达尔内犹豫了。

ex.t: Observant of his unwillingness to mar the effect by opening it again, Defarge said, “Go on, Jacques.”
ex.zh: 德法热看出他不肯再张嘴，怕破坏了这效果，就说：“往下说，雅克。”

ex.t: My return had only been delayed so long, from an unwillingness to leave Clerval in a strange place, before he had become acquainted with any of its inhabitants.
ex.zh: 我的归期之所以拖了这么久，只是不愿把克莱瓦尔一个人丢在生地方，他还不曾结识那里的任何人。

senses.d: reverse the winding or twisting of
separate the tangles of
become less tense, rest, or take one's ease
x: He relaxed in the hot tub
Let's all relax after a hard day's work

senses.d: cause to feel relaxed
x: A hot bath always relaxes me

ex.t: Ahab stood before him, and was lightly unwinding some thirty or forty turns to form a preliminary hand-coil to toss overboard, when the old Manxman, who was intently eyeing both him and the line, made bold to speak.
ex.zh: 亚哈站在他面前，轻轻解下三四十圈，先挽成一团好抛下海去，这时那老马恩岛人一直凝神看着他，也看着那根线，壮起胆子开口了。

senses.d: showing or resulting from lack of judgment or wisdom
x: an unwise investor is soon impoverished

senses.d: not appropriate to the purpose

ex.t: But one day he was unwise enough to start chattering, when they at once saw through his disguise and pecked him so unmercifully that he was glad to escape and join his own kind again.
“I was very unwise to let you go among people of whom I know so little, kind, I dare say, but worldly, ill-bred, and full of these vulgar ideas about young people.
ex.zh: “我太不明智了，竟让你到我自己都知之不深的人家去；他们心肠也许是好的，可满脑子俗气，没有教养，对年轻人尽是这些粗俗的念头。

ex.t: Indeed, it was unwise to be seen in such places, unless you had definite business there.
ex.zh: 确实，在这样的地方被人看见是不明智的，除非你在那里有明确的事。

senses.d: without knowledge or intention

ex.t: Unwittingly here a secret has been divulged, which perhaps might more properly, in set way, have been disclosed before.
ex.zh: 这里不知不觉泄露了一桩秘密；这秘密也许更该早些正式披露的。

ex.t: Of this offence Buck was unwittingly guilty, and the first knowledge he had of his indiscretion was when Sol-leks whirled upon him and slashed his shoulder to the bone for three inches up and down.
ex.zh: 巴克无意间犯了这个忌；他头一回知道自己莽撞，是索尔莱克斯转身扑来，一口把他的肩膀划开三寸长，深到骨头。

senses.d: not womanly
x: the logical clearness of her arguments...condemned her as eccentric and unwomanly

ex.t: It troubled her to remember that now, she wished she could take it back, it sounded so unwomanly.
ex.zh: 如今想起这个，她不安；她但愿能收回，因为那听着太不像个女人。

senses.d: unaccustomed or unusual
x: an unwonted softness in her face

ex.t: But even stripped of these supernatural surmisings, there was enough in the earthly make and incontestable character of the monster to strike the imagination with unwonted power.
ex.zh: 可是即便剥去这些超自然的揣测，这怪物凡间的形体和无可争辩的性格里，也有足够的东西，以一种不寻常的力量击中人的想象。

ex.t: For though it was a most unwonted hour, yet so impressive was the cry, and so deliriously exciting, that almost every soul on board instinctively desired a lowering.
ex.zh: 因为虽然那是个极不寻常的时辰，可这一声喊如此动人，又如此教人发狂地兴奋，船上几乎每一个灵魂都本能地想放艇。

ex.t: Such an unwonted bustle was he in that the staid Starbuck, his official superior, quietly resigned to him for the time the sole management of affairs.
ex.zh: 他忙乱得那样反常，以致他那沉稳的上级斯塔巴克索性暂时把一切事务都交给他一人掌管。

senses.d: not concerned with the temporal world or swayed by mundane considerations- Sheldon Cheney
x: was unworldly and did not greatly miss worldly rewards

senses.d: not wise in the ways of the world- Kate O'Brien
x: either too unsophisticated or too honest to promise more than he could deliver

ex.t: Other friends told the Marches that they had lost all chance of being remembered in the rich old lady’s will, but the unworldly Marches only said...
ex.zh: 别的朋友告诉马奇家，说他们再没指望在那位有钱老太太的遗嘱里得着什么了；可不通世故的马奇一家只说……

senses.d: in an unworthy manner

ex.t: He knew he was behaving unworthily, but he could not help it.
ex.zh: 他知道自己这样不体面，可忍不住。

ex.t: He answered me with the utmost civility, and even paid me the compliment of saying, that he was so well convinced of Lady Catherine’s discernment as to be certain she could never bestow a favour unworthily.
ex.zh: 他极有礼貌地回答我，还赏了我一句恭维话，说他深知凯瑟琳夫人有眼力，确信她决不会把恩宠错给不配的人。

senses.d: the quality or state of lacking merit or value
the quality of being not particularly suitable or befitting
x: he retracted nothing that he had said about the inappropriateness of either a corporeal God or a God who is a person
his praise released from her loud protestations of her unworthiness

ex.t: Perhaps during former years he had suffered from the late-discovered unworthiness of one beloved and so was disposed to set a greater value on tried worth.

senses.d: lacking in value or merit
x: dispel a student whose conduct is deemed unworthy

senses.d: not deserving
morally reprehensible
x: would do something as despicable as murder

ex.t: I asked, it is true, for greater treasures than a little food or rest: I required kindness and sympathy; but I did not believe myself utterly unworthy of it.
ex.zh: 我承认，我求的比一点食物或休息更贵重：我要的是善意和同情；可我不相信自己全然不配得到它。

ex.t: “Slave, I before reasoned with you, but you have proved yourself unworthy of my condescension.
